Changing the rune doesn't restore abilities that can be used only a limited number of times.

feats.name: Armor Assist
entries: You are practiced in helping yourself and others don heavy gear. You can attempt an Athletics or Warfare Lore check with a DC determined by the GM (usually DC 15 for common armor, DC 20 for uncommon armor, and DC 25 for rare armor) to halve the time you take to don armor. You can halve an ally's time to don armor by working with them to don the armor and succeeding at an Athletics or Warfare Lore check against the same DC.
feats.prerequisites: trained in {@skill Athletics|PC1} or Warfare Lore

feats.name: Armor Specialist
entries: You have trained hard to optimize your armor's unique protective qualities to maximize the materials used in its creation. You gain the armor specialization effects for all armors you are proficient with.

feats.name: Armored Rebuff
entries: You rebuff puny attacks with your armor, knocking back your foe. Attempt an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check to {@action Shove|PC1} the triggering enemy, even if you don't have a hand free. If you succeed, you can't {@action Stride|PC1} to follow the enemy, as you're knocking the enemy back with the rebounded attack, not by physically moving towards them.
feats.requirements: You are wearing medium armor or heavier. * This archetype offers Armored Rebuff at a different level than displayed here.
feats.trigger: An adjacent enemy critically fails an attack roll to {@action Strike|PC1} you with a melee weapon or unarmed attack.

feats.name: Armored Stealth
entries: You have learned techniques to adjust and modify your armor and movements to reduce the noise you make. When you wear non-{@trait Noisy|PC1|noisy} armor with which you are trained, your penalty to Stealth checks is reduced by 1 (to a minimum penalty of 0). If you're a master in Stealth, reduce the penalty by 2, and if you're legendary, reduce the penalty by 3. If your armor has the noisy trait, instead of reducing the penalty to Stealth checks, you ignore the effects of the noisy trait, enabling you to remove the penalty with a sufficient Strength score as normal.

feats.name: Ask the Bones
entries: You keep the bone of an ancestor or a friend to call upon for advice. Attempt to {@action Recall Knowledge|PC1}. If the bones belonged to a person particularly knowledgeable on the subject, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your check.

feats.name: Assassin Dedication
entries: You've trained to assassinate your foes, and you do so with tenacity and precision. You gain the Mark for Death activity.

{@b Mark for Death} {@as 3} ({@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}) {@b Requirements} The creature you intend to mark is {@condition Observed|PC1|observed} by you; {@b Effect} You designate a single creature as your mark. Using Mark for Death while hidden or undetected doesn't make you observed. Mark for Death lasts until the mark dies or you use Mark for Death again. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to Seek your mark, as well as to Deception checks to Feint against your mark. Your mark takes a –2 circumstance penalty to all Perception checks to Seek you.

In addition, when attacking your mark, you have the sneak attack class feature, except it deals 1d4 precision damage and you don't increase the number of dice as you gain levels. At 6th level, the damage increases to 1d6. If you already have the sneak attack class feature, you instead deal an additional 1 precision damage with your sneak attacks made against your mark, increasing to 2 precision damage at 6th level.

feats.name: Assassinate
entries: You strike with one swift movement, trying to instantly slay your mark. Make a Strike against your mark. If you hit, your mark takes an additional 6d6 precision damage with a basic Fortitude save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. If the mark critically fails, it dies unless its level is higher than yours. Regardless of the result of its save, the creature is temporarily immune to your Assassinate for 1 day.
feats.requirements: You have designated a mark using Mark for Death and are completely {@condition Unnoticed|PC1|unnoticed} by your mark.

feats.name: Assured Identification
entries: You rarely misidentify an item. When using Arcana, Nature, Occultism, or Religion checks to {@action Identify Magic|PC1}, if you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead. If you would misidentify a cursed item because you roll a success but not a critical success, you simply can't identify it instead.
feats.prerequisites: expert in {@skill Arcana|PC1}, {@skill Nature|PC1}, {@skill Occultism|PC1} or {@skill Religion|PC1}

feats.name: Assured Ritualist
entries: You can cover for a secondary caster's error. If you are the primary caster, after all the secondary checks are rolled, you can choose one check that was a failure or critical failure, and improve the result to one degree of success better than what the secondary caster rolled.

feats.name: Athletic Strategist
entries: You know how to calculatedly manipulate joints and body weight. In addition to using an attack stratagem's roll substitution for a Strike, you can use it to modify a {@action Disarm|PC1}, {@action Grapple|PC1}, {@action Reposition|PC1}, {@action Shove|PC1}, or {@action Trip|PC1} attempt, substituting your {@action Devise a Stratagem|PC2} roll for the {@skill Athletics|PC1} check. You must apply the substitution to the first eligible attack you make, whether it's a Strike or one of the Athletics actions.

You can also use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength for the Athletics check when you substitute your Devise a Stratagem roll, unless you're using a weapon for the maneuver and the weapon doesn't fit the restrictions for using Intelligence with a stratagem.

feats.name: Aura of Courage
entries: You stand strong in the face of danger and inspire your allies to do the same. Whenever you become {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened}, reduce the condition value by 1 (to a minimum of 0). At the end of your turn, each ally in your champion's aura reduces its frightened value by 1.

feats.name: Aura of Despair
entries: Your presence as an avatar of evil makes your foes more susceptible to terror and makes it almost impossible for them to shake off fear when you are near. Enemies in your champion's aura take a –1 circumstance penalty to saving throws against {@trait Fear|PC1|fear}. In addition, an enemy that ends its turn in your champion's aura can't reduce the value of its {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened} condition below 1.

feats.name: Aura of Determination
entries: Your aura protects against powers that would twist the mind and body. You and all allies in your champion's aura gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against {@trait Mental|PC1|mental}, {@trait Morph|PC1|morph}, and {@trait Polymorph|PC1|polymorph} effects.
feats.requirements: champion’s aura

feats.name: Aura of Faith
entries: You radiate an aura of belief that imbues your attacks and those of nearby allies with divine power. Each willing ally in your champion's aura adds the {@trait Holy|PC1|holy} trait to their Strikes if you're holy or adds the {@trait Unholy|PC1|unholy} trait to their Strikes if you're unholy.

feats.name: Aura of Life
entries: Your aura protects against the power of the Void. You and all allies in your champion's aura gain resistance 5 to void damage and a +1 status bonus to saves against {@trait Void|PC1|void} effects.
feats.requirements: champion’s aura

feats.name: Aura of Righteousness
entries: Your righteous aura dampens evil's might and prevents the unholy from escaping you. You and all allies in your champion's aura gain resistance 5 to {@trait Unholy|PC1|unholy} spells, unholy Strikes, and other unholy effects. If a {@trait Teleportation|PC1|teleportation} spell or effect would teleport an unholy creature out of your champion's aura, your aura attempts to counteract it, using the spell rank and DC of your devotion spells.

feats.name: Auspicious Mount
entries: Guided by your ongoing care, your steed has developed incredible intelligence and skill. The mount you gained with Faithful Steed is now a specialized animal companion. You can select one of the usual specializations or the auspice specialization. A faithful steed with the auspice specialization gains the following benefits.

items: It gains the {@trait Celestial|PC1|celestial}, {@trait Fiend|PC1|fiend}, or {@trait Monitor|PC1|monitor} trait—whichever best matches your deity's servitors, and its appearance shifts to look more like those servitors. It also gains the {@trait Holy|PC1|holy} trait if it's a celestial or the {@trait Unholy|PC1|unholy} trait if it's a fiend.
Its Intelligence modifier increases by 2 and its Wisdom modifier by 1.
Its proficiency rank in {@skill Religion|PC1} increases to expert.
It can speak the language associated with your deity's servitors (such as Empyrean for celestials, Chthonian for demons, or Requian for psychopomps).

Its maximum Hit Points increase by 20, increasing to 25 at 18th level and 30 at 20th level. If the mount has the celestial trait, the extra HP increase by 5, and the mount gains weakness 5 to unholy. If it has the fiend trait, the extra HP increase by 5, and the mount gains weakness 5 to holy.
It gains wings that grant it a fly Speed equal to its land Speed.

feats.name: Avalanche Strike
entries: You attack all nearby adversaries. Make a melee {@action Strike|PC1} with your two-handed weapon against each enemy within its melee reach. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but don’t increase your penalty until you have made all your attacks.
feats.requirements: You are wielding a melee weapon in two hands.

feats.name: Awesome Blow
entries: Your attacks are so powerful, they can flatten your opponents. When you use Knockback, you can attempt an Athletics check against your target's Fortitude DC.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: You gain the critical success effect of a {@action Shove|PC1}, then the critical success effect of a {@action Trip|PC1} against the target.

items.name: Success
entries: You gain the success effect of a Shove, then the success effect of a Trip against the target.

items.name: Failure
entries: You gain the normal effect of Knockback.

feats.name: Back to Back
entries: You excel at watching your allies’ backs and helping them watch yours. Any ally adjacent to you can’t be {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} due to {@rule Flanking|PC1|flanking} unless you’re also flanked. Similarly, while you’re adjacent to at least one ally, you can’t be off-guard due to flanking unless at least one ally you’re adjacent to is flanked as well.

feats.name: Backup Disguise
entries: You have a specific disguise that you keep at the ready, worn underneath your outer garment. You can change into this disguise to {@action Impersonate|PC1} as a 3-action activity. If you are a master in Deception, it is instead a 2-action activity, and if you are legendary in Deception, it is a single action. You can create a new backup disguise by spending the normal amount of time it takes you to Impersonate, but you can have only one backup disguise at a time. Having a backup disguise doesn't allow you to remove your armor or any other complex piece of clothing any more quickly, but once you have those off, the disguise is readily available. Because you have the backup disguise at the ready, it's possible that a thorough search might reveal some elements of the disguise.

feats.name: Barbarian Dedication
entries: You become trained in Athletics; if you were already trained in {@skill Athletics|PC1}, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You become trained in barbarian class DC. You can use the Rage action. While raging, you take a –1 penalty to AC. Choose an instinct as you would if you were a barbarian. You have that instinct for all purposes, but you don’t gain any of the other abilities it grants. If that instinct has anathema, you’re bound by them.

entries.name: {@action Rage|PC2} {@as 1}
entries: {@trait Barbarian|PC2} {@trait Concentrate|PC1} {@trait Emotion|PC1} {@trait Mental|PC1}
{@b Requirements} You aren't {@condition Fatigued|PC1|fatigued} or raging.
You tap into your inner fury and begin raging. You gain a number of {@rule Temporary Hit Points|PC1|temporary Hit Points} equal to your level plus your Constitution modifier. While you are raging:

items: You deal 2 additional damage on melee Strikes. This additional damage is halved if your weapon or {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed} attack is {@trait Agile|PC1|agile}.
You can't use actions with the {@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate} trait unless they also have the rage trait. You can {@action Seek|PC1} while raging.

entries: Rage lasts for 1 minute, until you fall {@condition Unconscious|PC1|unconscious}, or until the encounter ends, whichever comes first. You can't voluntarily stop raging. When you stop raging, you lose any remaining temporary Hit Points from Rage, and can't gain temporary Hit Points from using the Rage action again for 1 minute.

feats.name: Barbarian Resiliency
entries: You gain 3 additional Hit Points for each barbarian archetype class feat you have. As you continue selecting barbarian archetype class feats, you continue to gain additional Hit Points in this way.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Barbarian Dedication|PC2}; class granting no more Hit Points per level than 10 + your Constitution modifier

feats.name: Barreling Charge
entries: You rush forward, moving enemies aside to reach your foe. You {@action Stride|PC1}, attempting to move through your enemies’ spaces. Roll an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check and compare the result to the Fortitude DC of each creature whose space you attempt to move through during your Stride, moving through its space on a success but ending your movement before entering its space on a failure. You can then {@action Strike|PC1}, regardless of how your Stride ended. You can use Barreling Charge to {@action Burrow|PC1}, {@action Climb|PC1}, {@action Fly|PC1}, or {@action Swim|PC1} instead of Stride if you have the corresponding movement type.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.prerequisites: trained in {@skill Athletics|PC1} * This archetype offers Barreling Charge at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Bashing Charge
entries: You smash, bust, and charge through solid obstacles without hesitation. Stride twice. Once during your movement, if your movement passes through or ends adjacent to a door, window, fence, wall, or similar obstacle, you can attempt an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check to {@action Force Open|PC1} the obstacle with a +1 circumstance bonus to the roll; on a failure, your movement ends at that obstacle.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.prerequisites: trained in {@skill Athletics|PC1} * This archetype offers Bashing Charge at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Basic Blood Potency
entries: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level sorcerer feat.

feats.name: Basic Bloodline Spell
entries: You gain your bloodline’s initial bloodline spell. If you don’t already have one, you also gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can {@action Refocus|PC1} without any special effort.

feats.name: Basic Concoction
entries: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level alchemist feat.

feats.name: Basic Deduction
entries: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level investigator feat of your choice.

feats.name: Basic Devotion
entries: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level champion feat.

feats.name: Basic Eldritch Archer Spellcasting
entries: You gain the basic spellcasting benefits. Each time you gain a spell slot of a new level from this archetype, add a spell of the appropriate spell rank to your repertoire, either a common spell of your chosen tradition or another spell of that tradition you have learned or discovered.

feats.name: Basic Flair
entries: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level swashbuckler feat of your choice.

feats.name: Basic Fury
entries: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level barbarian feat.

feats.name: Basic Kata
entries: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level monk feat.

feats.name: Basic Mysteries
entries: You gain a 1st- or 2nd-level oracle feat of your choice.

feats.name: Basic Oracle Spellcasting
entries: You gain the basic spellcasting benefits. When you gain a spell slot of a new rank from the oracle archetype, add a common divine spell or another divine spell you have learned or discovered (including the granted spells associated with your mystery) to your repertoire, of that spell rank.

feats.name: Basic Scroll Cache
entries: You have a vast and overflowing collection of scroll scraps, riddled with errors and misspellings and leaking energy like a sieve. With enough care, you can coax these scroll scraps into functioning—briefly. Each day during your daily preparations, you can create a single temporary scroll containing a 1st-rank spell. The spell must be a common spell, a spell to which you have access, or a spell you are able to cast, and you must be trained in the skill corresponding to at least one of the spell's traditions. You can use {@action Learn a Spell|PC1} to add spells to those you can use with this feat, even if you aren't a spellcaster. This scroll is an unstable, temporary item and loses its magic the next time you make your daily preparations if you haven't already used it. This temporary scroll can't be used to Learn the Spell.
At 8th level, add a second temporary scroll containing a 2nd-rank spell.

feats.name: Basic Sorcerer Spellcasting
entries: You gain the basic spellcasting benefits. Each time you gain a spell slot of a new rank from the sorcerer archetype, add a spell of the appropriate spell rank to your repertoire: a common spell of your bloodline’s tradition, one of your bloodline’s granted spells, or another spell you have learned or discovered.

feats.name: Bastion Dedication
entries: You are particularly skilled at using a shield to protect yourself in combat. You gain the {@feat Reactive Shield|PC1} fighter feat.

feats.name: Battle Planner
entries: You are constantly drawing up plans and battle scenarios, assembling strategies and gathered intelligence for later use. When you scout an enemy's position or receive a detailed report from an ally who scouted the enemy's position, if you have a clear indication of the number, position, and identities of your potential foes, you can spend 1 minute to come up with a battle plan that takes such potential factors into account and reduces the role luck plays in the equation. Roll a Warfare Lore check. As long as the information was accurate and remains accurate when you roll initiative against those enemies, you can use the Warfare Lore result you previously rolled for your initiative roll; if you do, this is a {@trait Fortune|PC1|fortune} effect.

feats.name: Beastmaster Bond
entries: You can communicate telepathically with your animal companions within 100 feet. If you’re legendary in {@skill Nature|PC1}, you can communicate telepathically with your animal companions anywhere on the planet.

feats.name: Beastmaster Dedication
entries: You gain the service of a young animal companion that travels with you and obeys your commands. Contrary to the usual rules for animal companions, this feat can grant you a second animal companion. If you ever have more than one animal companion, you gain the Call Companion action.

Certain beastmaster feats give you focus spells. When you gain your first beastmaster focus spell, you become trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for beastmaster archetype spells is Charisma, and they are primal spells. You can {@action Refocus|PC1} by feeding, playing with, or otherwise tending to an animal companion.

feats.name: Beastmaster's Call
entries: You quickly call in a primal projection of a non-active companion to provide the companion’s support benefit. The projection arrives in an unoccupied square of your choice within 30 feet of you, grants you its support benefit, and then disappears at the start of your next turn. The projection has the same AC and saving throw modifiers as the real companion, and if it would take any damage before your next turn, it disappears, and the support benefit ends immediately.

feats.name: Beastmaster's Trance
entries: You can enter a trance that allows you to briefly inhabit the body of one of your animal companions and share its senses. You gain the focus spell {@spell Beastmaster Trance|PC2|beastmaster trance}.

feats.name: Benefactor's Majesty
entries: You tap into the grandeur of your warren's benefactor. You gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level, which last for 1 minute. In addition, you can immediately attempt a flat check to remove each type of {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent damage} you have. Finally, until the start of your next turn, any creature targeting you with a harmful attack, spell, or ability much first succeed at a DC 11 flat check or the action is disrupted as the creature avoids setting eyes upon your majesty.

feats.name: Bespell Strikes
entries: You siphon spell energy into one weapon you’re wielding, or into one of your unarmed attacks, such as a fist. Until the end of your turn, the weapon or unarmed attack deals an extra 1d6 force damage and gains the associated trait (see below) if it didn’t have it already. If the spell dealt a different type of damage, the Strike deals this type of damage instead (or one type of your choice if the spell could deal multiple types of damage).
{@b Oracle}: Your strike gains the {@trait Divine|PC1|divine} trait.
{@b Sorcerer:} Your strike gains the trait of your bloodline’s magical tradition.
{@b Wizard}: Your strike gains the {@trait Arcane|PC1|arcane} trait.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.requirements: Your most recent action was to cast a non-cantrip spell * This archetype offers Bespell Strikes at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Between the Scales
entries: You've learned to take advantage of slips in your foes' defenses. When you Strike an {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} creature using a melee weapon or unarmed attack that has the {@trait Agile|PC1|agile} and {@trait Finesse|PC1|finesse} traits, it gains the {@trait Backstabber|PC1|backstabber} trait.

feats.name: Big Mouth
entries: Instead of storing up to four items of Light Bulk in your cheek pouches, you can store up to 1 Bulk worth of items. The maximum size of a given item is unchanged.

feats.name: Biographical Eye
entries: In even a brief conversation or social interaction, you pick up on subtle social and visual cues to learn a great deal about a person's origin and history. You might notice bits of green under the person's fingernails and determine they're an herbalist, spy a pin indicating their membership in a secret society, or something similar. You pick up on only details that have to do with their societal role, so you might learn the city district where a vampire lives, but wouldn't learn any of their weaknesses, nor necessarily even that they are a vampire.

Spend 1 minute in the presence of someone you haven't met before, or haven't met since you first gained Biographical Eye, then attempt a DC 30 Society check. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the check if you engaged the person in conversation during this time. If the person is deliberately trying to conceal their nature or present a false identity, you learn about their false biography rather than their true one unless the result of your Society check exceeds their Will DC.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: You learn the creature's profession, their specialty within that profession, and a major accomplishment or controversy from their career. You also learn the nation and settlement where they live, as well as the district in a city large enough to have districts. In addition, you learn the nation or settlement where they spent their formative years.

items.name: Success
entries: You learn the creature's profession and specialty within that profession. You learn the nation or settlement where they normally live.

items.name: Failure
entries: You learn the creature's profession and the region of the world they hail from, but no more.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You learn a piece of erroneous information about the creature.

feats.name: Black Cat Curse
entries: You hiss a spiteful curse. The target rerolls the triggering saving throw and use the worse result.
feats.trigger: A creature within 30 feet you can see would succeed at a save.

feats.name: Blaze of Revelation
entries: Your mind and body can, for a short time and with great peril, surpass the final limits of your curse. For 1 minute, you shed torrential flames, become surrounded by spirits, or otherwise overflow with {@trait Divine|PC1|divine} power in a way that suits your mystery. On each of your turns during that time, you can cast one revelation spell without spending Focus Points.
At the end of the minute, the durations of any revelation spells you cast during that time end, and you must attempt a DC 40 Fortitude save.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: You aren’t otherwise affected.

items.name: Success
entries: You are {@condition Drained|PC1|drained} 2 and can't reduce or remove this condition until your next preparations.

items.name: Failure
entries: You are drained 4 and can't reduce or remove this condition until your next preparations.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You die.

feats.requirements: You are cursebound 4.

feats.name: Bleed Out
entries: You channel the residual energy from the last spell you cast into a ranged bloodletting. Make a ranged spell {@trait Attack|PC1|attack} roll against the AC of a target within 60 feet. This attack deals {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent bleed damage} equal to the rank of the spell you just cast.
feats.requirements: Your most recent action was to {@action Cast a Spell|PC1|cast} a non-cantrip spell that granted you a blood magic effect.

feats.name: Bleeding Finisher
entries: Your blow inflicts profuse bleeding. Make a slashing or piercing Strike. If you hit, the target also takes {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent bleed damage} equal to your precise strike finisher damage.

feats.name: Blessed Counterstrike
entries: You call upon divine power and make a weapon or unarmed Strike against the enemy who triggered your champion's reaction. The Strike deals one extra weapon damage die. If this Strike hits, until the start of your next turn, the target gains weakness equal to half your level to all Strikes made by you and your allies.
feats.prerequisites: champion’s reaction that grants an ally resistance to an enemy’s damage (including the grandeur, justice, liberation, and redemption causes)
feats.requirements: An enemy triggered your champion’s reaction since the end of your last turn.

feats.name: Blessed Denial
entries: You exude peace and protection, lessening a harmful condition as it falls upon an ally. Reduce the value of the condition your ally would take by 1 (to a minimum of 0). If the ally has more than one eligible condition at the same time, choose one to reduce.
feats.trigger: An ally within 30 feet would become {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened}, {@condition Drained|PC1|drained}, {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled}, {@condition Sickened|PC1|sickened}, or {@condition Stupefied|PC1|stupefied}.

feats.name: Blessed One Dedication
entries: You are touched by a deity and gifted with the ability to alleviate the suffering of others. You gain the {@spell Lay on Hands|PC2|lay on hands} devotion spell. You can {@action Refocus|PC1} by meditating, whether you reflect on the deity granting the blessing or not, allowing your blessing to refill your focus pool. Your devotion spells from the blessed one archetype are divine spells. You become trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC. Your spellcasting attribute is Charisma.

feats.name: Blessed Sacrifice
entries: You gain the {@spell Protector's Sacrifice|PC1|protector’s sacrifice} domain spell as a devotion spell.

feats.name: Blessed Spell
entries: When you focus your magic on an ally, you can remove harmful conditions. If your next action is to {@action Cast a Spell|PC1} from a spell slot, and that spell targets only a single ally, you can also attempt to remove a harmful condition from that ally. The condition must be one that could be removed by your {@feat Mercy|PC2} feat, including those granted by later feats such as {@feat Greater Mercy|PC2}. Attempt a counteract check based on the spell’s DC and rank. This effect is in addition to the normal effects of your spell.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Blessed One Dedication|PC2}; {@feat Mercy|PC2}; ability to cast spells from spell slots

feats.name: Blind-Fight
entries: Your battle instincts make you more aware of concealed and invisible opponents. You don’t need to succeed at a flat check to target concealed creatures. You’re not off-guard to creatures that are hidden from you (unless you’re off-guard to them for reasons other than the hidden condition), and you need only a successful DC 5 flat check to target a hidden creature.
While you’re adjacent to an undetected creature of your level or lower, it is instead only hidden from you

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.prerequisites: master in Perception * This archetype offers Blind-Fight at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Blood Ascendancy
entries: When you would benefit from a blood magic effect through Blood Rising, you can choose to benefit from two different blood magic effects you know. The effects follow the same rules as given in Blood Rising, and each effect can have a different target.

feats.name: Blood Rising
entries: The magic in your blood surges in response to your foe's spell. You generate a blood magic effect you know, even if you are already under the effects of blood magic. The target must be either you or the creature that triggered Blood Rising. If the blood magic effect grants you a bonus to AC or the appropriate saving throw, that bonus applies against the triggering spell. If the effect has a duration, it instead lasts until the beginning of your next turn.
feats.trigger: A creature targets you with a spell of the same tradition as your bloodline.
special: This feat has the traitcorresponding to the tradition of your bloodline.

feats.name: Blood Sovereignty
entries: You wield blood magic masterfully. When you would benefit from a blood magic effect, you can choose to lose Hit Points equal to twice the spell's rank as the energy of your blood is drawn out. This takes no extra action, and you benefit from two different blood magic effects you know as a result. The two effects can have different targets.

feats.name: Bloodletting Fangs
entries: You emulate your vampiric parent's techniques for drawing blood from a victim. Your fangs Strikes deal an additional 1d4 {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent bleed damage} on a critical hit.

feats.name: Bloodline Breadth
entries: Your repertoire expands, and you can cast more spells of your bloodline’s tradition each day. Increase the number of spells in your repertoire and number of spell slots you gain from sorcerer archetype feats by 1 for each spell rank other than your two highest sorcerer spell slots.

feats.name: Bloodline Conduit
entries: Your inborn magical nature lets you redirect ambient energies to fuel your spells. If your next action is to {@action Cast a Spell|PC1} of 5th rank or lower that has no duration, you don't expend the spell's slot when you cast it.

feats.name: Bloodline Focus
entries: By listening to the beating of your heart, your focus recovers faster. Whenever you {@action Refocus|PC1}, completely refill your focus pool.

feats.name: Bloodline Mutation
entries: You permanently mutate to become more like the creatures of your bloodline. You gain the appropriate trait or traits for those types of creatures ({@trait Aberration|PC1|aberration} for aberrant, angel and {@trait Celestial|PC1|celestial} for angelic, demon and {@trait Fiend|PC1|fiend} for demonic, and so on). You gain low-light vision or darkvision, if one is appropriate for creatures with those traits. Choose one of the following.

items: If the creatures associated with your bloodline have the ability to {@action Fly|PC1|fly}, you gain a fly Speed equal to your land Speed.

If the creatures associated with your bloodline are {@trait Aquatic|PC1|aquatic} or {@trait Amphibious|PC1|amphibious}, you become amphibious, able to breathe water and air equally well, and you gain a {@action Swim|PC1|swim} Speed equal to your land Speed.

If creatures associated with your bloodline have a resistance or immunity to {@trait Acid|PC1|acid}, {@trait Cold|PC1|cold}, {@trait Electricity|PC1|electricity}, {@trait Fire|PC1|fire}, {@trait Void|PC1|void}, or {@trait Sonic|PC1|sonic},choose an energy type your bloodline is immune or resistant to and gain resistance 20 against that energy type.

feats.prerequisites: a bloodline based on a specific type of creature

feats.name: Bloodline Perfection
entries: You command the ultimate powers of your bloodline and tradition. You gain an additional 10th-rank spell slot.

feats.name: Bloodline Resistance
entries: Your magical blood makes you more resistant to magic. You gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against spells and {@trait Magical|PC1|magical} effects.

feats.name: Blowgun Poisoner
entries: You can capably deliver toxins with a {@equipment Blowgun|PC1|blowgun}. Your blowgun {@action Strike|PC1|Strikes} can apply {@trait Injury|GMC|injury} {@trait Poison|PC1|poisons} even if they deal no damage due to a creature's resistance. If you critically succeed at a blowgun Strike using a poisoned dart, the target's initial save against the poison is one degree of success worse than the creature rolls; this is a {@trait Misfortune|PC1|misfortune} effect.

In addition, if you make a blowgun Strike while {@condition Hidden|PC1|hidden} or {@condition Undetected|PC1|undetected}, you don't automatically become {@condition Observed|PC1|observed}. Instead, immediately attempt a {@skill Stealth|PC1} check against the Perception DC of the target. If you succeed, you don't become observed, and are hidden (if you were undetected, you still become hidden rather than remaining undetected).

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Bon Mot
entries: You launch an insightful quip at a foe, distracting them. Choose a foe within 30 feet and roll a Diplomacy check against the target's Will DC.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: The target is distracted and takes a –3 status penalty to Perception and Will saves for 1 minute. The target can end the effect early with a retort to your Bon Mot. This can either be a single action that has the {@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate} trait or an appropriate skill action to frame their retort. The GM determines which skill actions qualify, though they must take at least 1 action. Typically, the retort needs to use a linguistic Charisma-based skill action.

items.name: Success
entries: As critical success, but the penalty is –2.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: Your quip is atrocious. You take the same penalty an enemy would take had you succeeded. This ends after 1 minute or if you issue another Bon Mot and succeed.

feats.name: Bone Investiture
entries: You encase yourself in spiritual dinosaur bones to become a Huge dinosaur. You can cast {@spell Dinosaur Form|PC1|dinosaur form} on yourself as a 5th-rank innate spell once per day.

feats.name: Bone Magic
entries: Your connection to your iruxi ancestors manifests as a simple primal spell that you cast using a fragment of an ancestor's bones. Choose one cantrip from either the occult spell list or the primal spell list. You can cast this cantrip as an innate spell at will, and it's heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up.
special: Choose when you gain this feat whether your innate spells are primal or occult; this choice applies to all innate spells you gain from lizardfolk ancestry feats that have Bone Magic as a prerequisite.

feats.name: Bonekeeper's Bane
entries: Whenever an enemy starts its turn adjacent to you, it must attempt a Will saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is highest. On a failure, the enemy takes a –1 status penalty to attack rolls and skill checks for as long as it remains adjacent to you. Regardless of the result of its save, the creature is then temporarily immune to bonekeeper's bane for 24 hours.

feats.name: Boneyard's Call
entries: You have a powerful connection to the Boneyard and its courts, granting you the ability to travel to and from the Boneyard. You can cast {@spell Interplanar Teleport|PC1|interplanar teleport} as a divine innate spell twice per week. This can be used only to travel to the Boneyard or from the Boneyard to the Universe. Due to your unique connection to the Boneyard, your body serves as the locus, and you don't require a planar key.

feats.name: Bounty Hunter Dedication
entries: When focused on finding your quarry, you’re relentless. You gain the {@action Hunt Prey|PC1} action. You can use Hunt Prey to designate a creature that you’ve observed, heard about, or learned about through some other means, such as a bounty board or wanted poster. In addition to the other benefits of Hunt Prey, you can designate a target as your prey while Gathering Information about them, in addition to designating them as your prey when Tracking them as normal. If you have already identified your target and selected them as your prey, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to Gather Information about them.
If you already have Hunt Prey, you gain the {@feat Monster Hunter|PC1} feat in addition to the other benefits of this feat.

feats.name: Brandishing Draw
entries: You draw and attack with the same motion. You Interact to draw a weapon, then either Strike or use a one-action {@trait Finisher|PC2|finisher}. You must still meet any other requirements to use a finisher, and any Strike you make must be made with the weapon you drew.

feats.name: Breath Like Honey
entries: You smell of honey and savory things. Your circumstance bonus to checks to {@action Make an Impression|PC1} if the target can smell your breath increases to +2. In addition, you can cast {@spell Enthrall|PC1|enthrall} as a 3rd-rank occult innate spell once per day, except the spell has a range of 30 feet and the {@trait Olfactory|PC1|olfactory} trait instead of the {@trait Auditory|PC1|auditory} trait. Targets don't gain any circumstance bonus for disagreeing with you.

feats.name: Breath of the Dragon
entries: Tapping into the physiology of your draconic ancestor, you can exhale a torrent of energy in a 15-foot cone or a 30-foot line, dealing 1d4 damage. Each creature in the area must attempt a basic saving throw against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. You can't use this ability again for 1d4 rounds.

At 3rd level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d4. The shape of the breath, the damage type, and the saving throw match those of your draconic exemplar (see above). This ability has the trait associated with the type of damage it deals.

feats.name: Briar Battler
entries: When you're in {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain} from an environmental feature, you can {@action Take Cover|PC1}, even if the feature wouldn't ordinarily be large enough for you to Take Cover.

feats.name: Brilliant Flash
entries: Your light cleanses souls of fear. When you use {@action Flash of Grandeur|PC2}, the attacker is also {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} for 1 round.

feats.name: Brutal Bully
entries: You push your foes around and leave bruises. While raging, when you successfully {@action Disarm|PC1}, {@action Grapple|PC1}, {@action Reposition|PC1}, {@action Shove|PC1}, or {@action Trip|PC1} an enemy, you deal that enemy bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier; add this to the damage from a critical success to Trip.

feats.name: Brutal Critical
entries: Your critical hits are particularly devastating. On a critical hit with a melee Strike, add one extra damage die. This is in addition to any extra dice you gain if the weapon is {@trait Deadly|PC1|deadly} or {@trait Fatal|PC1|fatal}. The target also takes {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent bleed damage} equal to two damage dice.

feats.name: Buckler Dance
entries: You spin your buckler defensively toward every attack. You constantly have your buckler raised as if you'd used {@action Raise a Shield|PC1}, as long as you meet that action's requirements.
feats.requirements: You are wielding a {@equipment Buckler|PC1|buckler}.

feats.name: Cadence Call
entries: You call out a quick cadence, guiding your allies into a more efficient rhythm. Each willing ally in your marshal’s aura is {@condition Quickened|PC1|quickened} until the end of their next turn, and they can use the extra action only to {@action Stride|PC1}. If an ally uses this extra action, at the end of its turn that ally becomes {@condition Slowed|PC1|slowed} 1 until the end of its following turn.

feats.name: Call the Swarm
entries: You give a shrill whistle and point, and a massive swarm of rats pours forth from the surrounding terrain to fill a 30-foot burst within 120 feet. The rats scurry over the ground and climb up walls and surfaces, biting and clawing as they deal 6d8 piercing damage to all enemies in the area. The rats continue to swarm in the area for the next minute, dealing 3d8 piercing damage to any enemy that ends its turn in the area and transforming the area into {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain} (though the rats allow you and your allies to pass normally). You can Dismiss the effect.

feats.name: Call Your Shot
entries: When you successfully Play to the Crowd, add the following to the list of benefits you can choose from:

items: A creature you can see within 30 feet becomes {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened 2}. This effect has the {@trait Emotion|PC1|emotion}, {@trait Fear|PC1|fear}, {@trait Mental|PC1|mental}, and {@trait Visual|PC1|visual} traits.

feats.name: Can't Fall Here
entries: You physically help an ally remain standing and encourage them to push through their pain against dire odds. Your ally doesn't fall {@condition Unconscious|PC1|unconscious} and remains at 1 Hit Point. The ally also gains a number of temporary Hit Points equal to your level that last for 1 minute. Fighting onward with such an injury isn't without consequence; your ally's {@condition Wounded|PC1|wounded} condition increases by 1.
feats.trigger: An adjacent and willing ally would be reduced to 0 HP but not killed.

feats.name: Cantorian Reinforcement
entries: The life energy that helped create the first hobgoblins is particularly potent in you, protecting you from ongoing maladies. If you roll a success on a saving throw against a {@trait Disease|PC1|disease} or {@trait Poison|PC1|poison}, you get a critical success instead. If you have a different ability that would improve the save in this way (such as the battle hardened fighter class feature), if you roll a critical failure on the save you get a failure instead.

feats.name: Cantorian Rejuvenation
entries: The life-giving energy that flows in your blood revitalizes you. You recover 4d6 Hit Points and gain 10 temporary Hit Points for 1 minute. At 15th level, you instead recover 6d6 HP and gain 15 temporary HP.

feats.name: Cantorian Restoration
entries: The energy that flows in your blood can save a life in the direst of times. You prevent the creature from dying and restore 6d8 + your Constitution modifier Hit Points to it. You can't use Cantorian Restoration if the triggering effect was a {@trait Death|PC1|death} effect or an effect that leaves no remains, such as {@spell Disintegrate|PC1|disintegrate}.
feats.trigger: A living creature within 60 feet would die.

feats.name: Cantrip Expansion
entries: Study broadens your range of simple spells.
{@b Prepared Caster (Cleric, Wizard, etc.)}: You can prepare two additional cantrips each day.
{@b Spontaneous Caster (Bard, Sorcerer, etc.)}: Add two additional cantrips from your spell list to your repertoire.

feats.name: Caravan Leader
entries: You know how to get the most effort out of your allies on the road. Your group can {@action Hustle|PC1} for an additional 20 minutes beyond the length of time that the member who could Hustle longest on their own.

feats.name: Cat Nap
entries: You can regain your energy quickly with a brief nap. You sleep for 10 minutes, after which you gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level that last for 1 hour.

feats.name: Cat's Luck
entries: You instinctively twist away from danger. Reroll the triggering saving throw and use the better result.
feats.trigger: You fail a Reflex saving throw

feats.name: Caterwaul
entries: You give a daring yowl, calling your companion back from the brink of unconsciousness. Your ally isn't knocked out and remains at 1 Hit Point. Their {@condition Wounded|PC1|wounded} condition still increases by 1 as though they had been dying and recovered.
feats.trigger: An ally within 30 feet would be reduced to 0 HP but not immediately killed.

feats.name: Catfolk Dance
entries: You have a habit of always being in the way when other creatures attempt to move. Attempt an {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} check against an adjacent creature's Reflex DC.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: The target creature gains a –2 circumstance penalty to Reflex saves and is {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Success
entries: The target creature gains a –2 circumstance penalty to Reflex saves until the start of your next turn.

feats.name: Catfolk Lore
entries: Growing up among catfolk has taught you the traditional values of freedom, stewardship, and quick reactions to trouble. You gain the trained proficiency rank in {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} and {@skill Survival|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
You also gain the {@feat Additional Lore|PC1} general feat for Catfolk Lore.

feats.name: Catfolk Weapon Familiarity
entries: You gain access to all uncommon weapons with the {@trait Catfolk|PC2|catfolk} trait. You have familiarity with weapons with the catfolk trait plus the {@equipment Kama|PC1|kama}, {@equipment Kukri|PC1|kukri}, {@equipment Scimitar|PC1|scimitar}, and {@equipment Sickle|PC1|sickle}—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.
At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.

feats.name: Cavalier Dedication
entries: You gain a young animal companion that serves as your mount. You can choose from animal companions with the mount special ability, as well as any additional options from your pledge (see Cavalier Pledges sidebar), as determined by your GM. You must choose an animal companion that’s at least one size larger than you, but if the animal usually starts as Small, you can begin with a Medium version of that animal (changing no statistics other than its size).
special: If you have pledged yourself to a cause, you can take a second dedication feat closely tied to that cause even if you haven’t taken two additional cavalier feats. For instance, if you pledged yourself to fight crime with a group of vigilantes, you could take the vigilante dedication without first completing the cavalier archetype. The GM determines what archetypes, if any, are valid choices.

feats.name: Cavalier's Banner
entries: You fly the banner of your pledge from your mount, raising your allies’ spirits. You and all allies in a 30-foot emanation from your mount gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves and DCs against fear effects. If your banner is destroyed or removed, allies within 30 feet become {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened} 1.
feats.requirements: You have pledged your service to a specific organization or ideal.

feats.name: Cavalier's Charge
entries: You {@action Command an Animal|PC1} to order your mount to {@action Stride|PC1} twice. At any point during this movement, you can {@action Strike|PC1} one enemy within reach or within the first range increment of a ranged weapon. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your attack roll.
feats.requirements: You are riding your mount.

feats.name: Celebrity Dedication
entries: The more people you have looking at you, the more content you are, and you take every opportunity to show up others when their performances are less than perfect. You gain the Upstage reaction. In addition, when you Earn Income, if the level of the task is higher than your level, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your check to Earn Income.

entries.name: {@action Upstage|PC2} {@as r}
entries: {@b Trigger} An enemy attempts a skill check and doesn’t get a critical success

After your foe has tried their best, you show everyone how it’s really done. Attempt a check using the same skill that triggered this reaction. The DC is typically the same as the check the enemy attempted, though the GM can adjust this as usual.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: You gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, Perception checks, saving throws, and skill checks until the end of your next turn.

items.name: Success
entries: As critical success, except you gain the benefits only if the triggering creature failed their skill check.

feats.name: Certain Strategem
entries: You know exactly where to strike a foe to target their weak spots. When you make a Strike that you're adding your Intelligence modifier to due to {@action Devise a Stratagem|PC2|Devising a Stratagem} and miss, you deal half of your strategic strike damage to the target. This damage type is that of the weapon or unarmed attack you used for the Strike.

feats.name: Champion Dedication
entries: Choose a deity. You are bound by your deity’s anathema and gain the champion’s aura and sanctification as described in the {@class Champion|PC2|champion} class. Choose a cause as you would if you were a champion, with the same options a champion must abide by. You gain its edicts and anathema but don’t gain the other abilities.

You become trained in {@skill Religion|PC1} and your deity’s associated skill; for each of these skills in which you were already trained, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You become trained in champion class DC. If you later gain a devotion spell, you become trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC.

You become trained in light armor and medium armor. If you already were trained in light armor and medium armor, you gain training in heavy armor as well. Whenever you gain a class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in any type of armor (but not unarmored defense), you also gain that proficiency in the armor types granted to you by this feat. If you have a class feature that grants you expert proficiency in unarmored defense and you’re 13th level or higher, you also become an expert in the armor types granted to you by this feat.

feats.name: Champion Resiliency
entries: You gain 3 additional Hit Points for each champion archetype class feat you have. As you continue selecting champion archetype class feats, you continue to gain additional Hit Points in this way.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Champion Dedication|PC2}; class granting no more Hit Points per level than 8 + your Constitution modifier

feats.name: Champion's Reaction
entries: You can gain and use the champion’s reaction associated with your cause.

feats.name: Champion's Sacrifice
entries: You can suffer so that others might live. You can cast the {@spell Champion's Sacrifice|PC2|champion's sacrifice} devotion spell.

feats.name: Chance Death
entries: Your previous life ended due to sheer poor luck, struck by lightning or choking on a fish bone. You can reroll the triggering recovery check or saving throw, but you must use the new result, even if it's worse.
feats.trigger: You would die as a result of a failed recovery check or saving throw.
special: You can select this feat only at 1st level, and you can't retrain into or out of this feat.

feats.name: Charmed Life
entries: When danger calls, you have a strange knack for coming out on top. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the triggering save. If you succeed on the triggering saving throw, you gain panache until the end of your next turn.
feats.trigger: You attempt a saving throw, but you haven’t rolled yet.

feats.name: Cheat Death
entries: Somehow you always escape the reaper by a hair's breadth. You avoid being knocked out or killed and remain at 1 Hit Point and gain panache, but you become {@condition Doomed|PC1|doomed 1} (or increase your doomed value by 1 if you were already doomed). You can't reduce or ignore the doomed condition from Cheating Death. The doomed condition from Cheating Death lasts for 10 minutes, though this doesn't affect the duration of any other doomed condition you have.
feats.trigger: You take damage that would reduce you to 0 Hit Points.

feats.name: Cheek Pouches
entries: Your cheeks are stretchy, and you can store up to four items of light Bulk or less in these cheek pouches. None of these items can have a dimension longer than 1 foot. As long as you have at least one item in your cheek pouches, your speech is noticeably difficult to understand. Placing an item in your cheek pouch or retrieving one is an Interact action. You can empty your mouth with a single action, causing everything you had stored in your cheek pouches to fall to the ground in your square.

feats.name: Chemical Contagion
entries: Your injury {@trait Poison|PC1|poisons} can spray onto creatures. You gain the toxicologist alchemist's greater field discovery.

feats.name: Clear the Way
entries: You put your body behind your massive weapon and swing, shoving enemies to clear a wide path. You attempt to {@action Shove|PC1} up to five creatures adjacent to you, rolling a separate {@skill Athletics|PC1} check for each target and ignoring the requirement that you have a hand free. Then {@action Stride|PC1} up to half your Speed. This movement doesn’t trigger reactions from any of the creatures you successfully Shoved. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but don’t increase your penalty until you have made all your attacks.
feats.requirements: You’re wielding a melee weapon in two hands.

feats.name: Cleave
entries: You swing clear through one foe and into another. Make a melee Strike against the second enemy.
feats.trigger: Your melee Strike reduces an enemy to 0 Hit Points, and another enemy is adjacent to that creature.

feats.name: Climbing Claws
entries: You can extend your claws to aid you in climbing. You gain a climb Speed of 10 feet.

feats.name: Clinch Strike
entries: Your opponents can’t slip your grasp without punishment. Make an unarmed melee Strike against the triggering creature.
feats.trigger: A creature you had {@condition Grabbed|PC1|grabbed} or {@condition Restrained|PC1|restrained} successfully {@action Escape|PC1|Escapes}.

feats.name: Clinging Shadows Initiate
entries: You learn a mystical stance that transforms your qi into sticky smoke that shrouds your limbs. You gain the {@spell Clinging Shadows Stance|PC2|clinging shadows stance} qi. While entering the stance is a qi spell, the shadow grasp attacks it grants are not, so you can use them as often as you like while in the stance.

feats.name: Close Quarters
entries: If you're Small or smaller, you can end your movement in the same square as a Small or smaller ally. No more than two creatures can share the same space when using this ability or a similar one.

feats.name: Clotting Elixirs
entries: Your restorative concoctions have a clotting effect on the drinker's blood. When a living creature drinks an {@trait Infused|PC2|infused} {@trait Elixir|PC1|elixir} with the {@trait Healing|PC1|healing} trait that you have created, it can immediately attempt a DC 10 flat check to remove any {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent bleed damage}.

feats.name: Clue Them All In
entries: You can clue in all your allies at once. When you use the {@action Clue In|PC2} reaction, any of your allies who are attempting the same check to investigate one of your active investigations receive the circumstance bonus from Clue In. If you use this ability during an encounter, they must attempt their check within 1 round of when you Clued them In.

feats.name: Cobra Envenom
entries: You slightly dislocate your joints to lash out with devious intent and the power to envenom your foe. Make a cobra fang Strike. Your {@trait Reach|PC1|reach} with this Strike is 5 feet greater than normal. If this Strike hits, the {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent poison damage} from your {@trait Venomous|PC2|venomous} trait increases to 1d4 persistent poison damage per weapon damage die.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Cobra Stance|PC2}; expert in unarmed strikes
feats.requirements: You are in Cobra Stance.
special: If you have this feat, the circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves and Fortitude DC granted by Cobra Stance increases from +1 to +2.

feats.name: Cobra Stance
entries: You enter a tightly coiled stance, with your hands poised as venomous fangs. While in this stance, the only Strikes you can make are cobra fang unarmed attacks. These deal 1d4 piercing damage; are in the brawling group; and have the {@trait Agile|PC1|agile}, {@trait Deadly|PC1|deadly d10}, {@trait Finesse|PC1|finesse}, {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed}, and {@trait Venomous|PC2|venomous} traits.
While in Cobra Stance, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves and your Fortitude DC, and you gain poison resistance equal to half your level.

feats.name: Collateral Thrash
entries: You smack the foe you're thrashing into someone else. When you Thrash, choose another enemy adjacent to the grabbed enemy. That enemy also takes your Thrash damage, with a basic Reflex save against your class DC.

feats.name: Combination Finisher
entries: You combine a series of attacks with a powerful finishing blow. Your finishers' Strikes have a lower multiple attack penalty: –4 (or –3 with an {@trait Agile|PC1|agile} weapon) if it's the second attack on your turn, or –8 (or –6 with an agile weapon) if it's the third or subsequent attack on your turn, instead of –5 and –10, respectively.

feats.name: Combine Elixirs
entries: You can add the full ingredients of a second elixir to an elixir you make to create a hybrid concoction. You must expend an additional versatile vial to make this combined elixir, and the ingredients must be for an elixir of the same level or lower that you could create with Quick Alchemy. When this combination elixir is consumed, both the constituent elixirs take effect. For example, you can combine two {@equipment Elixir of Life|PC2|lesser elixirs of life} to create a combined elixir that heals twice the normal amount, or you can combine a {@equipment Darkvision Elixir|PC2|lesser darkvision elixir} with a {@equipment Eagle-Eye Elixir|PC2|lesser eagle-eye elixir} to both gain darkvision and find secret doors.

feats.name: Come and Get Me
entries: You open yourself to attacks so you can respond in turn. Until your rage ends, you are {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard}, and damage rolls against you gain a +2 circumstance bonus. If a creature hits you, that creature is off-guard to you until the end of your next turn. If you hit it before the end of your next turn, you gain temporary Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier, or double that on a critical hit. These temporary Hit Points last until the end of your rage.

feats.name: Command Attention
entries: You command the attention of all around you with style, ensuring their gaze falls only upon you until the end of your next turn. Whenever a creature in a 30-foot emanation around you attempts a saving throw against a different visual effect, it gets a result one degree of success better than it rolled. This is a {@trait Fortune|PC1|fortune} effect. When an enemy within the aura attempts to use a visual effect that involves focusing its attention on a particular creature (such as a medusa’s Focus Gaze), it must succeed at a Will save against your {@rule Class DC|PC1|class DC} or {@rule Spell DC|PC1|spell DC}, whichever is higher, in order to target any creature except you. Allies in the aura can attempt to {@action Hide|PC1} even if they don’t have cover, as you are continually providing a distraction.

feats.name: Concealing Legerdemain
entries: Rather than hide an object somewhere the inspectors won't search, you're skilled at keeping the object on the move so it's never where they look. When you {@action Conceal an Object|PC1} of light Bulk or less, you can use Thievery instead of {@skill Stealth|PC1} for your checks and for the DC of an active searcher's Perception check. You roll the check only once, but you must continue to use actions to Conceal an Object throughout the process.

feats.name: Conduit of Void and Vitality
entries: You use the unstable energy of your {@trait Curse|PC1|curse} to manipulate the most basic of divine magic. You cast a 3-action {@spell Heal|PC1|heal} or {@spell Harm|PC1|harm} spell, expending the slot as normal. If the spell restores Hit Points to one or more creatures, then one creature healed by this spell regains a number of additional Hit Points equal to 1d8 × your {@trait Cursebound|PC2|cursebound} value; if the spell damages one or more creatures, then one creature harmed by this spell takes additional damage equal to 1d8 × your cursebound value.
feats.requirements: You have {@spell Heal|PC1|heal} or {@spell Harm|PC1|harm} as a signature spell and an available spell slot to cast it with.

feats.name: Connect the Dots
entries: Ephemeral connections between people, places, and concepts are invisible to most, but seeing them is your stock and trade. Choose an ally and a non-allied creature. You must be able to see both of them. You briefly study the way they both move and attempt a Perception check against the higher of the non-allied creature's {@skill Deception|PC1} DC or Will DC. Both targets are then temporarily immune to Connect the Dots for 10 minutes.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: You spot a way for your ally to take advantage of the other target's flaws and let them know about it. Your ally gains your Pursue a Lead investigation bonus as a circumstance bonus to all its Strikes or skill checks against the creature until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Success
entries: As critical success, but your ally gains the bonus only for their next Strike or skill check against the creature.

items.name: Failure
entries: You fail to make a connection.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You misconstrue a vital piece of information, which temporarily disconcerts you. You are {@condition Stupefied|PC1|stupefied 1} until the end of your next turn.

feats.name: Consult the Spirits
entries: You have learned rites or meditations that enable you to perceive minor, invisible spirits within a place. Choose Nature, Occultism, or Religion when you select this feat. Nature allows you to contact the spirits of nature that form leshies, who are born of pure life essence rather than spiritual energy and can answer questions about natural features like the location of nearby water or plant life. Religion reveals the presence of angelic, demonic, or other spirits in service to divine beings, who provide information about sources of powerful life energy or energy from the Void; sacred or profane influences; or the presence of undead. Occultism allows you to contact lingering spirits, psychic echoes of the departed dead, and spirits from beyond reality, who tell you about things like strange auras, effects, or the presence of unnatural occult beings.

Spend 10 minutes and attempt a check to {@action Recall Knowledge|PC1} with the chosen skill; the DC is determined by the GM (usually a very high DC for the level of the highest-level creature you might encounter in the area). If you're legendary in the chosen skill, you can use this feat once per hour, instead of only once per day, but you can't use it again on any area that overlaps a previous area.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: The spirits reveal themselves to you and have a helpful attitude toward you. Only you can perceive these spirits. They answer three simple questions about the environment within 100 feet of you, depending on the skill you chose and thus the type of spirits you contact. Their answers are almost always a single word, and their knowledge is limited to within their area of interest.

items.name: Success
entries: As with a critical success, but the spirits are indifferent to you and answer only one question.

items.name: Failure
entries: You are unable to contact the spirits of this place.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You contact one or more malevolent spirits. They are hostile toward you, though they may not immediately appear so. They answer up to three questions but give you information that is harmful to you in some way, as determined by the GM.

feats.prerequisites: master in {@skill Nature|PC1}, {@skill Occultism|PC1} or {@skill Religion|PC1}

feats.name: Contagious Rage
entries: You can drive your allies into a frenzy, granting them incredible benefits. You can ignore the requirements of Share Rage, using it multiple times in a Rage. Allies affected by Share Rage can choose to gain your instinct ability and the specialization ability it gains from weapon specialization, but not greater weapon specialization. They must abide by any restrictions of your instinct if they do so (such as the anathema of the superstition instinct).

feats.name: Contortionist
entries: You can squeeze out of tight situations by twisting and bending your body into unnatural positions, gaining an advantage against foes that try to pin you down. You gain the {@feat Quick Squeeze|PC1} skill feat, and if you're a master in {@skill Acrobatics|PC1}, you can Squeeze at full Speed. Whenever you successfully {@action Escape|PC1} using Acrobatics, the creature you Escaped from is {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} against the next attack you make against it before the end of your next turn.

feats.name: Coordinated Charge
entries: You heroically dash into the fray, inspiring your allies to follow. You {@action Stride|PC1} up to your Speed and make a melee {@action Strike|PC1}. If your Strike hits and damages an enemy, each ally within 60 feet who saw you hit can use a reaction to Stride, but they each must end their Stride closer to the creature you hit than where they started.

feats.name: Cornered Fury
entries: If a foe of a larger size than you critically hits and damages you, that foe is {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} to you for 1 round.

feats.name: Craft Philosopher's Stone
entries: Your research has paid off, culminating in the legendary philosopher's stone. You learn the formula for the {@equipment Philosopher's Stone|PC2|philosopher's stone} and can add it to your formula book.

feats.name: Crafter's Appraisal
entries: Your knowledge of items' construction allows you to discern their magical effects as well. You can use Crafting instead of a skill associated with a magic tradition to {@action Identify Magic|PC1} on magic items, though not on any other sorts of magic.

feats.name: Crane Flutter
entries: You interpose your arm between yourself and your opponent. Your circumstance bonus to AC from Crane Stance increases to +3 against the triggering attack. If the attack misses you and the attacker is within your reach, you can immediately make a crane wing Strike against the attacker at a –2 penalty.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.requirements: You are in Crane Stance. * This archetype offers Crane Flutter at a different level than displayed here.
feats.trigger: You are targeted with an attack by an observed attacker.

feats.name: Crane Stance
entries: Your arms flutter like a crane's wings. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC, but the only Strikes you can make are crane wing attacks. These deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage; are in the brawling group; and have the {@trait Agile|PC1|agile}, {@trait Finesse|PC1|finesse}, {@trait Nonlethal|PC1|nonlethal}, and {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed} traits.

While in Crane Stance, reduce the DC for {@action High Jump|PC1} and {@action Long Jump|PC1} by 5, and when you {@action Leap|PC1}, you can move an additional 5 feet horizontally or 2 feet vertically.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.requirements: You are unarmored. * This archetype offers Crane Stance at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Cringe
entries: With pitiful posturing, you cause your foe to pull back a deadly attack. The attacking creature takes a circumstance penalty to the damage of the triggering Strike equal to your level + 2. This penalty applies after doubling the damage for a critical hit. The attacker is then immune to your Cringe for 24 hours.
feats.trigger: A creature you are aware of critically succeeds on a Strike against you and would deal damage to you.

feats.name: Croak Talker
entries: You can communicate with the simplest of frogs and other similar creatures using longwinded croaks. You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the {@skill Diplomacy|PC1} skill with animals that are amphibians (most amphibians have the {@trait Amphibious|PC1|amphibious} trait).

feats.name: Crossblooded Evolution
entries: Odd interactions in your bloodline provide you with unexpected effects. Choose another bloodline. You know the blood magic effect of that bloodline. If the blood magic effect has a variable effect based on a choice you would have made at 1st level (such as the elemental bloodline's elemental influence), you make that decision when you take this feat.

feats.name: Crossbow Terror
entries: Your skill with a crossbow strikes terror into your opponents when you threaten them with the next bolt. Interact to reload a crossbow and then attempt an Intimidation check to {@action Demoralize|PC1}. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to this check if you succeeded at a Strike with a crossbow this turn.

feats.name: Crude Communication
entries: Even if you don’t speak a creature’s language, you can rely on inflection, root words, and body language to infer rudimentary meaning. If you interact with a creature for at least 10 minutes and that creature can speak a language, the GM rolls a secret {@skill Society|PC1} check for you, with a DC appropriate for the language’s rarity. On a success, you understand the gist of the meaning and can communicate basic concepts back to the creature; on a failure, you are mistaken or communicate incorrect concepts. If you’re legendary in Society, you can communicate instantly without needing to attempt a Society check; even if you didn’t know the medium of communication the creature uses (speech, sign language, and so on), you intuit this information as soon as they try to communicate.

feats.name: Cruelty
entries: The harm you deal with your corrupting touch saps the strength from your enemy's body. You can cast {@spell Touch of the Void|PC2|touch of the void} targeting a living creature using 2 actions instead of 1. If you do, the target is also {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled 1} for 1 minute if it fails its save (enfeebled 2 if it critically fails).
feats.prerequisites: {@spell Touch of the Void|PC2|touch of the void}

feats.name: Crunch
entries: Your jaws can crush bone and bite through armor. Your jaws {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed} attack deals 1d8 piercing damage instead of 1d6 and gains the {@action Grapple|PC1|grapple} trait.

feats.name: Crushing Grab
entries: Like a powerful constrictor, you crush targets in your unyielding grasp. When you successfully {@action Grapple|PC1} a creature, you can deal bludgeoning damage to that creature equal to your Strength modifier. You can make this attack nonlethal with no penalty.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Dancing Leaf
entries: You are as light as a leaf on the breeze. When you {@action Leap|PC1} or succeed at a {@action High Jump|PC1} or {@action Long Jump|PC1}, increase the distance you jump by 5 feet. When calculating the damage you take from {@rule Falling|PC1|falling}, don't count any distance fallen while you are adjacent to a wall.

feats.name: Dandy Dedication
entries: You are a consummate student of dignity, etiquette, and fashion. You become trained in {@skill Deception|PC1} and {@skill Society|PC1}; if you were already trained in either, you become an expert in it instead. You gain the Influence Rumor downtime activity.

entries.name: Influence Rumor
entries: ({@trait Downtime|PC1|downtime}) You spend at least 1 day of downtime attempting to manipulate the course, tone, or content of a rumor to your benefit. You need to succeed at a Diplomacy check to shift the rumor as you intend. The difficulty is determined by the GM based on the size of the community, the relative perceptiveness of the inhabitants, and the agency of other rumormongers, but it typically is no lower than DC 15 for a small village, DC 20 for a town, DC 30 for a city, or DC 40 for a metropolis.

feats.name: Dangle
entries: You can hang by your tail from any suitable anchor point, such as a tree branch, balcony, or rocky outcropping (subject to the GM's discretion), typically while climbing. While hanging, you have free use of all your other limbs, so you can perform tasks that require both hands, such as firing a bow or swinging a greatsword.

feats.name: Dastardly Dash
entries: You dash past an opponent, confounding them with underhanded tactics. Stride up to half your speed. You can attempt a {@action Trip|PC1} or a {@feat Dirty Trick|PC2} (if you have that action) against one opponent you pass within range of at any point during your movement.

feats.name: Deadly Aspect
entries: You have honed the unarmed attack your draconic heritage has granted you to a lethal degree. The unarmed attack you gained from Draconic Aspect gains the {@trait Deadly|PC1|deadly d8} trait.

feats.name: Deadly Grace
entries: Your graceful attacks are especially powerful. When you score a critical hit with an {@trait Agile|PC1|agile} or {@trait Finesse|PC1|finesse} melee weapon that has the {@trait Deadly|PC1|deadly} trait, you double the number of dice from that trait. When you wield an agile or finesse melee weapon that doesn't have the deadly trait, it gains the deadly d8 trait instead.

feats.name: Debilitating Bomb
entries: You can add a crystalline additive to an alchemical bomb to have it undermine your enemy. Choose {@condition Dazzled|PC1|dazzled}, {@condition Deafened|PC1|deafened}, {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard}, or a –5-foot status penalty to Speeds. If the attack with the bomb hits, in addition to the bomb's normal effects, the target must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw or take that effect until the start of your next turn. Use your class DC for this saving throw, even if someone else throws the bomb.

feats.name: Debilitating Dichotomy
entries: You reveal a glimpse of the impossible conflicts between the {@trait Divine|PC1|divine} anathema behind your {@trait Curse|PC1|curse}, forcing you to reckon with another's conflicts as well. You and one creature within 30 feet each take 9d6 mental damage with a basic Will save, and the target is stunned 1 if it critically fails its save. You get a degree of success one better than you rolled for your saving throw. At 10th level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 3d6.

feats.name: Deceptive Worship
entries: Members of your cult frequently pass themselves off as worshippers of other religions. You can use Occultism instead of {@skill Deception|PC1} to {@action Impersonate|PC1} a typical worshipper of another faith or to {@action Lie|PC1} specifically to claim you are a member of the faith you are Impersonating. You still need to use the Deception skill to Impersonate a specific worshipper or to perform other deceptive actions, such as attempting to Lie about any other matter.

feats.name: Deeper Dabbler
entries: With some streamlining to your process and a deeper collection of talisman materials, you make a greater number of talismans every day. You can create two additional talismans during your daily preparations.
special: You can select this feat a second time if you are 14th level or higher.

feats.name: Defend Mount
entries: You interpose yourself between an attacker and your mount, defending your mount from harm. Use your own defense against the triggering attack instead your mount’s defense. If the triggering attack hits, you take the effects of the attack instead of your mount.
feats.trigger: An enemy makes a {@action Strike|PC1} or spell attack against your mount while you’re riding it.

feats.name: Defensive Advance
entries: With the protection of your shield, you dive into battle! You {@action Raise a Shield|PC1|Raise your Shield} and Stride. If you end your movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, you can make a melee Strike against that enemy. You can use Defensive Advance while Burrowing, {@action Climb|PC1|Climbing}, Flying, or Swimming instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

feats.name: Defensive Stratagem
entries: By scrutinizing a foe, you learn how to better avoid its attacks. When you use {@action Devise a Stratagem|PC2}, you can choose a defensive stratagem instead of an attack or skill stratagem after you roll a d20.

{@b Defensive Stratagem} You can't attempt to Strike the target until the start of your next turn. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to all your defenses against effects caused by the target until the start of your next turn.

feats.name: Deflect Projectile
entries: You gain a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the attack misses, you have deflected it. You cannot use this feat to deflect unusually massive ranged projectiles (such as boulders or ballista bolts).
feats.requirements: You’re aware of the attack, are not {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} against it, and have a hand free.
feats.trigger: You are the target of a physical ranged attack.

feats.name: Deity's Domain
