entries: Your dramatic appearances can frighten bystanders. When you make a Startling Appearance, you can also attempt to {@action Demoralize|PC1} each enemy in a 10-foot emanation you were {@condition Unnoticed|PC1|unnoticed} by before your {@action Strike|PC1}.

feats.name: Furious Bully
entries: You bully foes across the battlefield. While raging, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to {@skill Athletics|PC1} checks for {@trait Attack|PC1|attack} actions.

feats.name: Furious Finish
entries: Desperate to finish the fight, you pour all your rage into one final blow. Make a Strike. If it hits, you gain a circumstance bonus to damage equal to the number of rounds remaining in your Rage (maximum 10). After this Strike, your {@action Rage|PC2} immediately ends, and you are {@condition Fatigued|PC1|fatigued} until you rest for at least 10 minutes.

feats.name: Furious Grab
entries: You grab your foe while it's distracted by your attack. The enemy you hit becomes grabbed by you, as if you had succeeded at an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check to {@action Grapple|PC1} it.
feats.requirements: Your last action was a successful {@action Strike|PC1}, and either you have a hand free or your Strike used a weapon with the grapple trait.

feats.name: Furious Sprint
entries: You rush forward. Stride up to five times, or up to eight times if you used 3 actions. All this movement must be in a straight line (though the GM might allow reasonable variance). You can replace any of these Strides with a {@action Balance|PC1} action if you need to, which you attempt using an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check instead of an {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} check, using the same DC.

feats.name: Furious Vengeance
entries: Your enemy's blow fuels your rage and provokes your immediate retaliation. Make a melee Strike against the triggering enemy.
feats.trigger: An enemy within your melee reach critically hits you with a melee {@action Strike|PC1}.

feats.name: Fuse Stance
entries: You have combined two stances into a single stance all your own. When you take this feat, choose two stances you know and combine them into a single fused stance. Give your new fused stance a unique name. When you enter your fused stance, you gain all the effects of both stances, including the requirements and restrictions.

If the stances both grant special attacks, you gain all those attacks. If a stance restricts you to one particular attack (such as {@feat Crane Stance|PC2}), you must abide by that restriction. If the fused stances have incompatible restrictions, the GM determines which apply, or determines you can't fuse those stances at all.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.prerequisites: at least two stances * This archetype offers Fuse Stance at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Gecko's Grip
entries: You cling to walls with a preternatural grip. You gain the {@feat Combat Climber|PC1} feat as a bonus feat, and if you roll a success on an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check to climb, you get a critical success instead.
special: If you have the cliffscale lizardfolk heritage, you instead gain a climb Speed of 15 feet.

feats.name: Get Used to Disappointment
entries: You capitalize on an opponent's failure with smug attitude and swagger, reminding them of the gap in skill between you and your opponent. You attempt to {@action Demoralize|PC1} the opponent. Regardless of the result, the target becomes temporarily immune for 1 minute.
feats.requirements: Your turn begins, and one target within 30 feet failed an attack roll or skill check against you on its last turn.

feats.name: Ghost Hunter
entries: Your connection to the Boneyard ensures that your blows strike true against spectral beings. Your weapon and unarmed Strikes against {@trait Incorporeal|GMC|incorporeal} creatures become {@trait Magical|PC1|magical}. If they are already magical, they instead gain the effects of a ghost touch property rune.

feats.name: Giant Snare
entries: You can create bigger {@trait Snare|PC2|snares} for quick deployment, making it more likely for a creature to walk into your snares. When you prepare snares for quick deployment, you can prepare some of them as giant snares. A giant snare takes up a 10-foot-by-10-foot area but costs two of your quick deployment snares. A giant snare can trigger from a creature entering any portion of its area, and all its effects apply over the full area.

feats.name: Giant's Lunge
entries: You extend your body and prepare to attack foes outside your normal reach. Until your rage ends, all your melee weapons and unarmed attacks gain a {@trait Reach|PC1|reach} of 10 feet. This doesn't increase the reach of any weapon or unarmed attack that already has the reach trait, but it does combine with abilities that increase your reach due to increased size, such as {@feat Giant's Stature|PC2}.

feats.name: Giant's Stature
entries: You grow to incredible size. You become Large, increasing your {@trait Reach|PC1|reach} by 5 feet and gaining the {@condition Clumsy|PC1|clumsy 1} condition until you stop raging. Your equipment grows with you.
feats.requirements: You are Medium or smaller.

feats.name: Gifted Power
entries: Your mystery grants you additional magic. You have an extra spell slot of your highest rank, which you can use only to cast one of your mystery's granted spells, heightened to this rank.
special: If you have the {@trait Divine|PC1|divine} access class feature or {@feat Mysterious Repertoire|PC2} feat, you can cast spells that you learned from those abilities using the additional spell slot from Gifted Power.

feats.name: Gladiator Dedication
entries: You know how to turn combat into a form of entertainment. You gain the {@feat Additional Lore|PC1} general feat for Gladiatorial Lore. If you were already trained in Gladiatorial Lore, you also become trained in a Lore skill of your choice.

At the start of a combat encounter, if you have spectators, you gain a number of temporary HP equal to your character level for 1 minute and you can roll Performance for your initiative. If there are sapient creatures observing a combat encounter, and these onlookers are neither engaged in the combat themselves nor directly assisting any participants, the combatants have spectators. The GM is the final arbiter of whether or not a combat has spectators.

feats.name: Glean Contents
entries: You are adept at quickly scanning loose papers and carefully discerning the contents of sealed letters without damaging the seal. You can attempt Society checks to {@action Decipher Writing|PC1} on a message that is only partially glimpsed, upside down or reversed from your perspective, and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the check when doing so. You can also use this feat to decipher sealed letters, adding the manipulate trait to your attempt to Decipher Writing. This doesn't prevent witnesses from noticing your efforts; you might need to attempt {@skill Deception|PC1} or {@skill Stealth|PC1} checks to avoid being noticed. In either use of this feat, the recipient is made aware of your efforts on a critical failure (for instance, you might be caught rubbernecking or you might disturb the papers in a way their owner notices).

feats.name: Glean Lore
entries: You tap into the collected lore of the divine, accessing a variety of potentially useful information. Attempt a {@skill Religion|PC1} check to understand the information you gain. The GM sets the DC (similar to the DC to {@action Recall Knowledge|PC1}), potentially adjusting the DC of the check for topics far removed from your mystery.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: You comprehend the lore accurately or gain a useful clue from the divine about your situation.

items.name: Success
entries: You learn two pieces of information about the topic, one true and one erroneous, but you don’t know which is which.

items.name: Failure
entries: You recall incorrect information or gain an erroneous or misleading clue.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You recall two pieces of incorrect information or gain two erroneous or misleading clues.

feats.name: Goading Feint
entries: Your tricks make foes overextend their attacks. On a {@action Feint|PC1}, you can use the following success and critical success effects instead of any other effects you would gain when you Feint; if you do, other abilities that adjust the normal effects of your Feint no longer apply. You can choose whether to use the Goading Feint benefits or the normal benefits each time you Feint a given foe.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: The target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to all attack rolls against you before the end of its next turn.

items.name: Success
entries: The target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its next attack roll against you before the end of its next turn.

feats.name: Godbreaker
entries: You have mastered an ultimate grappling technique capable of breaking even the mightiest of foes. You hurl the creature 20 feet into the air, following behind it with a powerful jump, and then make an unarmed Strike. If the Strike is successful, you can repeat this process up to two more times, moving the creature an additional 20 feet directly up into the air with each Strike; the creature keeps the grabbed or restrained condition throughout the sequence. If you miss with any of the Strikes, Godbreaker and the grabbed or restrained condition immediately end and both you and the opponent fall, taking falling damage as normal for the total height of your jump.

If all three Strikes are successful, you immediately grab the creature and bring it crashing to the ground, dealing your unarmed Strike damage plus falling damage to it. You land on your feet adjacent to the creature, you take no damage from the fall, and the creature remains grabbed or restrained by you.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.requirements: You have a creature {@condition Grabbed|PC1|grabbed} or {@condition Restrained|PC1|restrained}.

feats.name: Gossip Lore
entries: Your time gossiping in fashionable salons keeps you informed on every topic. You are trained in Gossip Lore, a special Lore skill that can be used only to Recall Knowledge, but on any topic. If you fail a check to Recall Knowledge with Gossip Lore, you get the effects of the {@feat Dubious Knowledge|PC1} skill feat. If you have legendary proficiency in {@skill Society|PC1}, you gain expert proficiency in Gossip Lore, but you can’t increase your proficiency rank in Gossip Lore by any other means.

feats.name: Graceful Guidance
entries: You can demonstrate how to quickly twist out of the way of dangerous effects. You can use the {@action Aid|PC1} reaction to grant a bonus to an ally's Reflex save. As usual for Aid, you need to prepare by using an action on your turn to encourage the ally.

feats.name: Graceful Leaper
entries: Mass and muscle are meaningless when you propel yourself through the air; only grace and balance matter. You can roll an {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} check instead of an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check when making a {@action High Jump|PC1} or {@action Long Jump|PC1}.

feats.name: Grandmaster Qi Spells
entries: You have unlocked a qi technique achievable only by those who attain complete mastery of both their body and their spirit. You gain {@spell Embrace Nothingness|PC2|embrace nothingness}, {@spell Qi Form|PC2|qi form}, or another 9th-rank qi spell you have access to.
special: You can select this feat more than once, choosing a different spell each time.

feats.name: Grandmother's Wisdom
entries: You carry the bones of your ancestors with you, and you can ask them for counsel. You can cast {@spell Augury|PC1|augury} twice per day as a 2nd-rank occult innate spell.

feats.name: Gravesight
entries: You can see in the darkness as easily as a psychopomp. You gain {@creatureability Darkvision|MC1|darkvision}.
special: You can select this feat only at 1st level, and you can't retrain into or out of this feat.

feats.name: Great Cleave
entries: Your fury carries your weapon through multiple foes. When you Cleave, if your Strike also reduces its target to 0 HP, you can continue to make melee Strikes until you make a Strike that doesn't reduce a creature to 0 HP, or until there are no creatures adjacent to the most recent creature you attacked while Cleaving, whichever comes first.

feats.name: Great Tengu Form
entries: You take on the imposing form of a large, winged spirit. Once per day, as part of using Long-Nosed Form, you also gain the benefits of 4th-rank {@spell Enlarge|PC1|enlarge} and fly. This lasts for 5 minutes or until you shift out of your Long-Nosed Form, whichever happens first.

feats.name: Greater Bloodline
entries: You uncover the greater secrets of your bloodline. You gain the greater bloodline spell associated with your bloodline.

feats.name: Greater Crossblooded Evolution
entries: Your bloodline is extraordinarily complex. Choose up to three of the sorcerous gift spells granted by your secondary bloodline. You add these spells to your spell repertoire, heightened to the highest rank of spells you can cast or to the highest rank they can be heightened to that is lower than the highest rank of spells you can cast. You cast these spells as the tradition from your primary bloodline.

feats.name: Greater Cruelty
entries: The extent of your corruption devastates your foes' minds and reflexes. When you use Cruelty, you can choose to make the target {@condition Clumsy|PC1|clumsy} or {@condition Stupefied|PC1|stupefied} instead, with the same condition value. Make the choice when you Cast the Spell (before you know the result of the target's save).

feats.name: Greater Debilitating Bomb
entries: You have learned enhanced techniques and alchemical secrets that allow you to expand the range of effects you can impose with your bombs. When you use Debilitating Bomb, add the following to the list you can choose from: {@condition Clumsy|PC1|clumsy 1}, {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled 1}, {@condition Stupefied|PC1|stupefied 1}, or –10-foot status penalty to Speeds.

feats.name: Greater Magical Scholastics
entries: You broaden the scope of your magical understanding, allowing you to find the right path, detect hidden objects, and conceal those objects from unscrupulous rivals. You can cast {@spell Augury|PC1|augury}, {@spell Locate|PC1|locate}, and {@spell Veil of Privacy|PC1|veil of privacy} as occult innate spells, each once per day. You can cast this {@i veil of privacy} spell only on an object, and it's automatically heightened to half your level rounded up.

feats.name: Greater Mental Evolution
entries: Your bloodline's deep connection to mental essence greatly enhances your spell repertoire. Add one spell to your spell repertoire for each spell rank you can cast.

feats.name: Greater Mercy
entries: Your faith enhances your ability to remove conditions. Add the following options to the list of conditions you can counteract for any type of mercy you can grant. {@b Mercy of the Body} {@condition Drained|PC1|drained}, {@condition Slowed|PC1|slowed}; if you're 16th level, add {@condition Stunned|PC1|stunned}; {@b Mercy of Grace} {@condition Immobilized|PC1|immobilized}, {@condition Restrained|PC1|restrained}, slowed; if you're 12th level, add {@condition Petrified|PC1|petrified}; if you're 16th level, add stunned; {@b Mercy of the Mind} {@condition Confused|PC1|confused}, {@condition Controlled|PC1|controlled}, slowed; if you're 16th level, add {@condition Doomed|PC1|doomed} and stunned.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.prerequisites: {@feat Mercy|PC2} * This archetype offers Greater Mercy at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Greater Physical Evolution
entries: You change form readily. Once per day, you can use a sorcerer spell slot to cast any common polymorph battle form spell of the spell slot's rank as if it were a signature spell in your repertoire. You can use the extra spell slot from or {@trait Primal|PC1} Evolution instead of a sorcerer spell slot.

feats.name: Greater Revelation
entries: You unlock deeper revelations hidden within your mystery. You gain your mystery’s greater revelation spell.

feats.name: Greater Security
entries: Shield in hand, you offer your ally its full protection you do yourself. While the companion shield is in effect, if your shield is raised, the ally with the companion shield gets the same bonus to AC your shield grants, and you can trigger {@feat Shield Block|PC1} if that ally would meet the trigger. This uses your shield's statistics and applies damage to your shield.

feats.name: Greater Spiritual Evolution
entries: Your magical blood allows your spells to be fully effective against {@trait Incorporeal|GMC|incorporeal} creatures. Your spells have the effects of a ghost touch property rune. They can target or affect a creature projecting its consciousness (such as via {@spell Project Image|PC1|project image}) or possessing another creature, even if its body is elsewhere, though you must know about the possession or projection and choose to do so. Your spells can affect creatures on the Ethereal Plane, though this doesn't grant you the ability to locate them.

feats.name: Greater than the Sum
entries: You call upon the familial bonds you share with your allies and other ratfolk to become an overwhelming force in battle. You can cast {@spell Enlarge|PC1|enlarge} as a 6th-rank primal innate spell once per day.

feats.name: Greater Vital Evolution
entries: Vital power surges through you like a font of energy. Twice per day, you can {@action Cast a Spell|PC1|cast a spell} after you've run out of spell slots of the appropriate spell rank; the two spells you cast with this feat must be of different spell ranks.

feats.name: Grievous Blow
entries: You know how to deliver focused, powerful blows that bypass your enemies’ resistances. Make an {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed} melee {@action Strike|PC1}. If this Strike hits, it deals two additional weapon damage dice and ignores an amount of {@rule Resistance|PC1|resistance} to physical damage (or to a specific physical damage type) equal to your level. This Strike counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty.
If you are at least 18th level, increase the additional damage to three weapon damage dice.

feats.name: Grovel
entries: You convince your foe you're less of a threat. You attempt to {@action Feint|PC1} against a creature. Unlike a normal Feint, the creature can be within 30 feet instead of in your melee reach, and you make your check against its Will DC instead of its Perception DC.

feats.name: Gruesome Strike
entries: Make a Strike against the creature that triggered your champion's reaction. If you hit, double the extra damage the target takes from your reaction, and the target must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or be {@condition Drained|PC1|drained 1}. Regardless of the result, the creature is temporarily immune to your Gruesome Strike for 24 hours.
feats.prerequisites: champion’s reaction that grants extra damage with your Strikes (including the desecration, iniquity, and obedience causes)
feats.requirements: Your Strikes currently deal extra damage from your champion’s reaction.

feats.name: Guarded Movement
entries: Your guard is up, even while moving. You gain a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against reactions triggered by your movement.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Guardian's Deflection
entries: You use your weapon to deflect the attack against your ally, granting a +2 circumstance bonus to their AC against the triggering attack. This turns the triggering critical hit into a hit, or the triggering hit into a miss. You gain panache until the end of your next turn.
feats.requirements: You are wielding a single one-handed melee weapon and have your other hand or hands free.
feats.trigger: An ally within your melee reach is hit by an attack, you can see the attacker, and a +2 circumstance bonus to AC would turn the critical hit into a hit or the hit into a miss.

feats.name: Hammer Quake
entries: You smash the ground with your weapon, knocking nearby creatures to the ground. Choose a square within your reach, including your own space. If there’s an enemy in the chosen square, you can {@action Strike|PC1} that enemy with your two-handed weapon. Regardless of whether you attempted a Strike, you then attempt to {@action Trip|PC1} every enemy in the chosen square plus each square adjacent to that square, ignoring Trip’s requirement that you have a hand free.
Hammer Quake counts as three attacks toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made the Strike, if any, and all the Trip attempts.
feats.requirements: You’re wielding a non-{@trait Finesse|PC1|finesse} melee weapon in two hands.

feats.name: Harbinger's Claw
entries: You caw ominously, cursing the creature with misfortune. The target creature must roll the triggering check twice and take the lower result.
feats.trigger: A creature within 60 feet is about to attempt an attack roll or skill check.

feats.name: Harmonize Self
entries: You can restore your health by tapping into your qi. You gain the {@spell Harmonize Self|PC2|harmonize self} qi spell.

feats.name: Heal Mount
entries: Your devotion to your mount manifests as a surge of vital energy. When you cast {@spell Lay on Hands|PC2|lay on hands} on your mount, instead of the normal amount, the spell restores 10 Hit Points, plus 10 for each heightened rank.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Faithful Steed|PC2}; {@spell Lay on Hands|PC2|lay on hands}

feats.name: Healing Bomb
entries: You can add a foamy catalyst to an {@equipment Elixir of Life|PC2|elixir of life} to turn it into a topical projectile. You can throw the elixir at a creature within 20 feet as an Interact action to heal that creature and those near it. The target is affected as though it drank the elixir, and each living creature adjacent to it regains HP from the bomb equal to the elixir's number of damage dice (3 HP for a lesser elixir of life, for example).

feats.name: Herbalist Dedication
entries: You can create natural remedies. You gain the advanced alchemy benefits. You can use advanced alchemy to create 4 {@trait Alchemical|PC1|alchemical} {@trait Consumable|PC1|consumables} with the {@trait Healing|PC1|healing} trait, though the number is reduced by 2 if you didn’t make your daily preparations in the wilderness. These consumables are called your herbal items. You remember herbal item {@rule formulas|PC1} and don’t need a formula book for them.

You become an expert in {@skill Nature|PC1} and can use Nature instead of {@skill Crafting|PC1} to {@action Craft|PC1} alchemical consumables with the healing trait. You don’t need to be trained in Crafting to do so, and you can use healer’s tools instead of alchemist’s tools.

feats.name: Hidden Magic
entries: You've learned to hide the magical auras of your gear. During your daily preparations, you carefully tweak any or all of your magic items to appear non-magical. Objects adjusted in this way remain so until your next preparations. A spellcaster using {@spell Detect Magic|PC1|detect magic} or {@spell Read Aura|PC1|read aura} must succeed at a Perception check against your {@skill Deception|PC1} DC to see through your obfuscations.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Vigilante Dedication|PC2}; expert in {@skill Arcana|PC1}, {@skill Nature|PC1}, {@skill Occultism|PC1} or {@skill Religion|PC1}

feats.name: Hobgoblin Lore
entries: You've studied traditional hobgoblin exercises and fieldcraft, all of which have a militaristic bent. You gain the trained proficiency rank in {@skill Athletics|PC1} and {@skill Crafting|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
You gain the {@feat Additional Lore|PC1} general feat for Hobgoblin Lore.

feats.name: Hobgoblin Weapon Familiarity
entries: You gain access to all {@trait Uncommon|PC1|uncommon} weapons with the {@trait Hobgoblin|PC2|hobgoblin} trait. You have familiarity with weapons with the hobgoblin trait plus the {@equipment Composite Longbow|PC1|composite longbow}, {@equipment Composite Shortbow|PC1|composite shortbow}, {@equipment Glaive|PC1|glaive}, {@equipment Longbow|PC1|longbow}, {@equipment Longsword|PC1|longsword}, and {@equipment Shortbow|PC1|shortbow}—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.
At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.

feats.name: Holistic Care
entries: You provide emotional and spiritual care. Add {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened}, {@condition Stupefied|PC1|stupefied}, and {@condition Stunned|PC1|stunned} to the list of conditions you can reduce with {@feat Treat Condition|PC2}. If the stunned condition has a duration instead of a value, you can’t use Treat Condition to reduce it.

feats.name: Homing Shot
entries: Your shots zip around corners and fly at impossible angles to reach your target. Make a bow or crossbow Strike against a foe you can see; the ammunition travels to your target, even going around corners. You ignore the target's {@condition Concealed|PC1|concealed} condition and all {@rule Cover|PC1|cover}.

feats.name: Hone Claws
entries: You grind or gnaw a particularly wicked edge onto your claws. The next claws Strike you hit and deal damage with deals an additional 1d6 bleed damage. You cannot have more than one instance of Hone Claws active at a time.

feats.name: Hop Up
entries: Your frog-like agility awakens as soon as you do. You Stand. This movement doesn't trigger reactions.
feats.trigger: You lose the {@condition Unconscious|PC1|unconscious} condition.

feats.name: Hunter's Defense
entries: Your canny understanding of natural and primal creatures helps you predict and dodge their attacks. The triggering attack roll targets your Nature DC instead of your AC. Though this allows you to avoid taking penalties to your AC, it doesn't remove any conditions or other effects causing such penalties. For example, an enemy with sneak attack would still deal extra damage to you for being {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard}, even though you wouldn't take the –2 circumstance penalty against the attack.
feats.trigger: A creature with the {@trait Animal|PC1|animal}, {@trait Beast|PC1|beast}, {@trait Elemental|PC1|elemental}, fey, {@trait Fungus|PC1|fungus}, or {@trait Plant|PC1|plant} trait attacks you, and you can see the attacker.

feats.name: Hurling Charge
entries: You make a ranged {@action Strike|PC1} with your thrown weapon, {@action Stride|PC1}, and then Interact to draw another weapon. This Interact action doesn't trigger reactions.
feats.requirements: You're wielding a {@trait Thrown|PC1|thrown} weapon.
special: If you are {@action Rage|PC2|raging} and end the Stride adjacent to an enemy, that enemy is {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} against the next Strike you make against it with the weapon you drew before the end of your next turn.

feats.name: Hyena Familiar
entries: Hyenas serve kholo as pets and trackers. Some kholos, such as yourself, draw the attention of smaller hyenas that are vessels for magical spirits. You gain a Tiny hyena as a familiar.

feats.name: Illimitable Finisher
entries: Your strikes flow endlessly. Step and attempt a single one-action {@trait Finisher|PC2|finisher}. This Strike gains the {@trait Bravado|PC2|bravado} trait, possibly replenishing your panache; if you regain panache, you can immediately attempt another finisher as part of this action, ignoring the restriction of using actions with the {@trait Attack|PC1|attack} trait after a finisher.

feats.name: Immortal Techniques
entries: You flow from technique to technique, renewing yourself as you embrace each style you have mastered. The first time each round that you use an action that has both the {@trait Monk|PC1|monk} and {@trait Stance|PC1|stance} traits, you gain 20 temporary Hit Points that last until the start of your next turn.

feats.name: Impaling Bone
entries: Once per day, you can cast {@spell Impaling Spike|PC1|impaling spike} as a 7th-rank innate occult spell, except the spike is made of bone instead of cold iron. The bone from the spell has the effects of the ghost touch property rune and can immobilize {@trait Incorporeal|GMC|incorporeal} creatures as if they were corporeal.

feats.name: Impaling Finisher
entries: You stab two foes with a single thrust or bash them together with one punch. Make a bludgeoning or piercing melee Strike and compare the attack roll result against the AC of up to two foes. One foe must be adjacent to you, and the other foe must be adjacent to and directly behind the first foe, in a straight line from your space. Roll damage once and apply it to each creature you hit. An Impaling Finisher counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty.

feats.name: Impaling Thrust
entries: You impale your enemy and hold it in place with your weapon, and leave it bleeding when it gets free. Make a melee Strike with a melee weapon that deals piercing damage. If the Strike hits and deals damage, your target is {@condition Grabbed|PC1|grabbed} until it successfully {@action Escape|PC1|Escapes}, you attack with the weapon again, or you Release the required weapon, whichever comes first. When the target is no longer grabbed, it takes {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent bleed damage} equal to the weapon's number of weapon damage dice.
feats.requirements: You are wielding a melee weapon that deals piercing damage.

feats.name: Implausible Purchase
entries: It seems impossible, but you've analyzed every angle and are able to just keep pulling out exactly the item you need, even in far-flung locations. You can use {@feat Prescient Planner|PC1} even if you have already used it after purchasing goods, and you can use it as a single action instead of a 2-action activity, during which you Interact to draw the item. In addition, five times per day, you can use Prescient Planner to pull out a common {@trait Consumable|PC1|consumable} item up to 6 levels lower than your level.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.prerequisites: {@feat Predictive Purchase|PC2} * This archetype offers Implausible Purchase at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Imposing Destrier
entries: Under your care, your mount has realized its innate potential. The mount you gained with Faithful Steed is now a nimble or savage animal companion.

Your animal companion has greater independence. During an encounter, even if you don't use the {@action Command an Animal|PC1} action, your animal companion can still use 1 action that round on your turn to Stride or Strike. It can do this at any point during your turn, as long as you aren't currently taking an action. If it does, that's all the actions it gets that round—you can't Command it later.

feats.name: Impossible Riposte
entries: Your ripostes can deflect attacks back at their source. You can use Opportune Riposte with a trigger of “A foe outside of your reach critically fails an attack roll against you” in addition to its usual trigger. When you use Opportune Riposte with this new trigger against a ranged attack, your Strike deflects some of the triggering effect back toward its source. Compare the result of your attack roll to the AC of the triggering foe. On a hit, you deal the normal amount of damage for your Strike, but the damage type changes to that of the triggering attack. For instance, if you used Opportune Riposte to deflect a {@spell Blazing Bolt|PC1|blazing bolt}, your Strike would deal fire damage instead of its normal damage type.

feats.name: Impossible Technique
entries: You execute a maneuver that defies possibility. If the triggering effect was an enemy's attack hitting you, the enemy rerolls the attack roll and uses the lower result. If the triggering effect was you failing a saving throw, you reroll the saving throw and use the higher result.
feats.requirements: You are not armored or {@condition Fatigued|PC1|fatigued}.
feats.trigger: An enemy’s attack hits you or you fail a saving throw against an enemy’s ability.

feats.name: Impressive Landing
entries: You slam into the ground, shattering it around you. Treat the fall as 10 feet shorter. You land on your feet. The ground in a 5-foot emanation becomes {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain}. Any creature in the emanation when you land takes 5 bludgeoning damage as the debris hits it and is {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} until the start of its next turn.
feats.trigger: You fall at least 10 feet and land on a solid surface.

feats.name: Impressive Mount
entries: You've trained your mount to become a powerful force on the battlefield. The mount you gained through the {@feat Cavalier Dedication|PC2} feat becomes a mature animal companion, granting it additional capabilities.

Your mount has greater independence. During an encounter, even if you don't use the {@action Command an Animal|PC1} action, your mount can still use 1 action that round on your turn to Strike or Stride (or {@action Burrow|PC1}, {@action Climb|PC1}, {@action Fly|PC1}, or {@action Swim|PC1} if it has that Speed). It can do this at any point during your turn, as long as you aren't currently taking an action. If it does, that's all the actions it gets that round—you can't Command it later.

feats.name: Improbable Elixirs
entries: Your mastery of alchemical secrets enables you to replicate effects most believe can be achieved only via magic. Select a number of {@trait Potion|PC1|potions} equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1); these potions must be of 9th level or lower. You gain formulas to create these potions as alchemical consumables with the {@trait Elixir|PC1|elixir} trait. When making these alchemical elixirs, you can substitute alchemical reagents for an equal value of magical components, and you can use an {@equipment Alchemist's Toolkit|PC1|alchemist's toolkit} (for {@action Quick Alchemy|PC2}) or an {@equipment Alchemist's Lab|PC1|alchemist's lab} (for the {@action Craft|PC1} activity) instead of any other required toolkits. Other than that, the formula doesn't change. Once you've chosen the potion formulas, they can't be changed.

feats.name: Improved Familiar
entries: You find it easy to attract a powerful and unusual familiar to your side. The number of abilities required to make your familiar a specific familiar is two lower than normal.

feats.name: Improved Invigorating Elixir
entries: Choose physical invigoration or mental invigoration, and add the listed conditions to those you can choose for an invigorating elixir you create to counteract: {@b Physical Invigoration} {@condition Blinded|PC1|blinded}, {@condition Deafened|PC1|deafened}, {@condition Drained|PC1|drained}, {@condition Paralyzed|PC1|paralyzed}, {@condition Slowed|PC1|slowed}; {@b Mental Invigoration} {@condition Confused|PC1|confused}, {@condition Controlled|PC1|controlled}, {@condition Fleeing|PC1|fleeing}, {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened}, {@condition Paralyzed|PC1|paralyzed}, {@condition Slowed|PC1|slowed}.
special: You can select this feat a second time to choose a different type of invigoration and add its options to those you can choose.

feats.name: Improved Knockback
entries: When you successfully {@action Shove|PC1} a creature, increase both the distance you can push the creature and the distance you can move to follow along with the target by 5 feet on a success or 10 feet on a critical success. If you push the target into another creature or obstacle, they both take 1d6 bludgeoning damage per 5 feet of movement that was prevented.

feats.name: Improvise Admixture
entries: You scrounge together enough ingredients from what's left in your alchemist's toolkit to produce a few more versatile vials on the fly. Attempt a {@skill Crafting|PC1} check. The DC is usually a standard-difficulty DC for your level, but the GM can assign a different DC based on the circumstances. The number of vials you regain depends on the result of your check (up to your maximum).

items.name: Critical Success
entries: You regain 3 versatile vials.

items.name: Success
entries: You regain 2 versatile vials.

items.name: Failure
entries: You regain 1 versatile vial.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You don't regain any versatile vials.

feats.requirements: You have fewer than your maximum number of versatile vials, and you’re either holding or wearing an {@equipment Alchemist's Toolkit|PC1|alchemist's toolkit}.

feats.name: Improvise Tool
entries: You can jury-rig solutions when you don't have the proper tools on hand. You can attempt to {@action Repair|PC1} damaged items without a {@equipment Repair Toolkit|PC1|repair toolkit}.

If you have the raw materials, you can {@action Craft|PC1} a basic caltrop set, {@equipment Candle|PC1|candle}, {@equipment Compass|PC1|compass}, {@equipment Crowbar|PC1|crowbar}, {@equipment Fishing Tackle|PC1|fishing tackle}, {@equipment Flint and Steel|PC1|flint and steel},{@equipment Hammer|PC1|hammer}, ladder, {@equipment Piton|PC1|piton}, {@equipment Rope|PC1|rope}, 10-foot pole, replacement thieves' picks, long or {@equipment Tool (Short)|PC1|short tool}, or {@equipment Torch|PC1|torch} as if you had their formulas.

feats.name: Improvised Critical
entries: You can apply critical specialization effects to improvised weapons you wield. For any given improvised weapon, the GM determines which critical specialization effect is most applicable, based on the type of object it is.

feats.name: Improvised Pummel
entries: When you make a {@action Strike|PC1} with an improvised weapon you're wielding, you gain a +1 item bonus to the attack roll, and you can have the Strike deal two weapon damage dice instead of the improvised weapon's normal number. If the attack is a critical hit, the improvised weapon breaks after the normal effects of a critical hit occur. If the item has a Hardness greater than your level, or if it's an artifact, cursed item, or other item that's difficult to break or destroy, it doesn't break but the attack is a normal hit instead of a critical hit. You can choose not to get any of the effects of Improvised Pummel on a Strike if you don't want to risk breaking the item. At 12th level, the item bonus increases to +2, and at 16th level, the Strike deals three weapon damage dice instead of the improvised weapon's normal number.

If you're benefiting from handwraps of mighty blows, you use the handwraps' item bonus if it's higher and can choose to use its number of damage dice. Any property runes from the handwraps also apply if you use the handwraps' number of weapon damage dice, provided they could apply to the improvised weapon (as determined by the GM).

feats.name: Improvised Repair
entries: You can hastily patch damaged equipment together, but the temporary fix lacks the full care required for lasting repairs. You patch together a broken item possessed by you or an adjacent willing creature. Until the item takes damage again, it still functions as a shoddy item of its type. If it's a magic item or another item with activations, it can't be activated while patched together, but can be used for normal functions (such as Striking with a weapon or using {@feat Shield Block|PC1} with a shield). This activity restores no Hit Points, so the item is easy to destroy. Once the item is Repaired normally such that it is no longer {@condition Broken|PC1|broken}, it is also no longer shoddy.

feats.name: Incorporeal Shot
entries: You can concentrate an immense amount of magic to create a piece of ammunition that phases through everything but your target. Make a bow or crossbow Strike against a foe who is {@condition Observed|PC1|observed} or {@condition Hidden|PC1|hidden} to you (but not {@condition Undetected|PC1|undetected}). The ammunition travels to your target in a straight line, passing through any non-magical barriers or walls in its way, though magical barriers stop the arrow. The shot ignores all {@rule Cover|PC1|cover}, the {@condition Concealed|PC1|concealed} condition, the hidden condition, and circumstance bonuses to AC from shields. It has a +4 status bonus to hit creatures wearing any type of armor. The Strike's damage can't be reduced with a {@feat Shield Block|PC1} reaction using a non-{@trait Magical|PC1|magical} shield.

feats.name: Incredible Beastmaster Companion
entries: Your mature animal companions continue to grow and develop. Each of them becomes a nimble or savage animal companion, gaining additional capabilities determined by the type of companion. You choose nimble or savage individually for each companion, including any companion that becomes mature after you take this feat.

feats.name: Incredible Familiar (Familiar Master)
entries: Your familiar is infused with even more magic than other familiars. You can select six familiar or {@rule Master Abilities|PC1|master abilities} each day, instead of four.

feats.name: Incredible Luck
entries: You always seem to bounce back from the worst. When you use Charmed Life, roll the save twice (including the +2 circumstance bonus from Charmed Life) and use the better result.

feats.name: Incredible Mount
entries: Under your care and training, your mount has realized its innate potential. The mount you gained through the {@feat Cavalier Dedication|PC2} feat becomes a nimble or savage animal companion (your choice), gaining additional capabilities determined by the type of companion.

feats.name: Incredible Scout
entries: When you scout, you are particularly alert for danger, granting your allies precious moments to prepare to fight. When using the {@action Scout|PC1} exploration activity, you grant your allies a +2 circumstance bonus to their initiative rolls instead of a +1 circumstance bonus.

feats.name: Inescapable Grasp
entries: Your grasp has a supernatural quality to it, preventing your foes from easily escaping—with or without magical assistance. If a creature you have {@condition Grabbed|PC1|grabbed} attempts to use a teleportation spell or effect, it must succeed at a DC 15 flat check or the spell fails. If a creature you have grabbed attempts to {@action Escape|PC1} while under the effect of unfettered movement or a similar effect, it must succeed at a DC 15 flat check or be forced to roll the Escape attempt normally, rather than automatically succeeding.

feats.name: Inexhaustible Countermoves
entries: At the start of each enemy's turn, you gain an extra reaction you can use only during that turn to perform an {@action Opportune Riposte|PC2}, or a {@feat Reactive Strike|PC2} if you have that reaction.

feats.name: Influence Nature
entries: With patience and time, you can make bird calls, leave game trails, and ultimately influence the behavior of a certain type of animals in the region to favor and even aid you in the days to come. The GM determines the DC of any check required and the amount of time your work requires (usually at least a day or two of downtime). While you can't directly control how you've influenced nature, you can hope for certain effects, such as easier hunts or birds falling silent whenever danger is approaching. If you're legendary in Nature, you can elicit these same adjustments to animal behavior in the area by spending only 10 minutes.

feats.name: Inner Strength
entries: Your strength is part of your rage. As long as your anger remains, you can gather your strength and rage to overcome any sort of enfeeblement. You reduce your {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled} condition's value by 1.

feats.name: Inoculation
entries: You have practice combating plague, and your patients are less likely to succumb to the same disease again for a time. When you successfully Treat a Disease on someone and they fully recover from the disease, they gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against that same disease for 1 week.

feats.name: Inspiring Marshal Stance
entries: You become a brilliant example of dedication and poise in battle, encouraging your allies to follow suit. When you spend this action, attempt a {@skill Diplomacy|PC1} check. The DC is usually an easy DC of your level, but the GM can assign a different DC based on the circumstances. The effect depends on the result of your check.

items.name: Success
entries: Your marshal’s aura grants you and allies a +1 status bonus to attack rolls and saves against {@trait Mental|PC1|mental} effects.

items.name: Failure
entries: You fail to enter the stance.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You fail to enter the stance and can’t take this action again for 1 minute.

feats.name: Instinct Ability
entries: Your rage stokes the spark of your barbarian instinct into a roaring flame. You gain the instinct ability for the instinct you chose for {@feat Instinct Ability|PC2|Barbarian Dedication}.

feats.name: Instinctive Strike
entries: You trust your instincts and your sense of smell, using all your senses to pinpoint your opponent's location. When you make a melee Strike against an opponent you're detecting using {@rule Scent|PC1|scent}, ignore any flat check required due to the target being {@condition Concealed|PC1|concealed} or {@condition Hidden|PC1|hidden}.

feats.name: Instrument of Slaughter
entries: Your blessed armament thirsts for the blood of your foes. Whenever you critically hit an enemy with a Strike that has the extra damage from your champion's reaction, the target also takes {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent bleed damage} equal to two of the weapon's damage dice.
feats.prerequisites: champion’s reaction that grants extra damage with your Strikes (including the desecration, iniquity, and obedience causes)

feats.name: Instrument of Zeal
entries: Divine energy fills your weapon. Whenever you critically hit an enemy with Blessed Counterstrike or Retributive Strike, your attack deals an extra weapon damage die, and the target is {@condition Slowed|PC1|slowed 1} on its next turn.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Blessed Counterstrike|PC2} or Retributive Strike; champion’s reaction that grants an ally resistance to an enemy’s damage (including the grandeur, justice, liberation, and redemption causes)

feats.name: Interweave Dispel
entries: You weave dispelling energy into a spell. If your next action is to cast a single-target spell against an enemy, and you either hit the enemy with the spell {@trait Attack|PC1|attack} roll or the enemy fails its saving throw, you can cast {@spell Dispel Magic|PC1|dispel magic} on the enemy as a free action, expending a spell slot as normal and targeting one spell effect affecting the enemy.
feats.prerequisites: {@spell Dispel Magic|PC1|dispel magic} in your spell repertoire

feats.name: Intimidating Strike
entries: Your blow not only wounds creatures but also shatters their confidence. Make a melee Strike. If you hit and deal damage, the target is frightened 1, or frightened 2 on a critical hit.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Into the Fray
entries: You charge into battle with shield-splintering fury. You {@action Leap|PC1}, {@action Stride|PC1}, or {@action Swim|PC1}. Make two melee {@action Strike|PC1|Strikes} during this movement, one with your one-handed melee weapon and one with your shield or a weapon attached to the shield (like a {@equipment Shield Boss|PC1|shield boss} or {@equipment Shield Spikes|PC1|shield spikes}). You can make these Strikes at any points during your movement, and each must target a different enemy. Both attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but don't increase your penalty until you have made both attacks.
feats.requirements: You are wielding a one-handed melee weapon in one hand and a shield in another hand.

feats.name: Investigator Dedication
entries: You gain the on the case class feature, which grants you both the Pursue a Lead activity and {@action Clue In|PC2} reaction. You become trained in {@skill Society|PC1} and another skill of your choice. If you were already trained in Society, you instead become trained in an additional skill of your choice. You also become trained in investigator class DC.

feats.name: Investigator's Stratagem
entries: You play out battles in your head, allowing you to strike when the time is right. You gain the {@action Devise a Stratagem|PC2} action; however, when you substitute its result for your attack roll, you can’t use your Intelligence modifier in place of your Strength or Dexterity modifier. You also can’t use your Intelligence modifier on other rolls from abilities that expand Devise a Stratagem, such as the {@feat Athletic Strategist|PC2} feat.

feats.name: Invigorating Elixir
entries: You can mix an aromatic salve into an elixir with the {@trait Healing|PC1|healing} trait to soothe physical maladies. In addition to its normal effects, the elixir can be imbibed by a creature prevented from doing so (such as a {@condition Sickened|PC1|sickened} creature). In addition to its other effects, the elixir attempts to counteract an effect imposing one of the following conditions of the imbiber's choice: {@condition Clumsy|PC1|clumsy}, {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled}, sickened, or {@condition Stupefied|PC1|stupefied}. Use half your level rounded up for the counteract rank and your class DC – 10 for the counteract modifier. The imbiber is then temporarily immune to the effects of this additive for 10 minutes. The additive can't counteract {@trait Curse|PC1|curses}, {@trait Disease|PC1|diseases}, or conditions that are part of the creature's normal state.

feats.name: Invulnerable Rager
entries: Even the heaviest armors serve only to enhance your unbridled fury. You are trained in heavy armor. Whenever you gain a barbarian class feature that grants you expert or greater proficiency in medium armor, you also gain that proficiency in heavy armor. If you have the {@action Quick-Tempered|PC2} action, you can use it while wearing heavy armor.

feats.name: Iron Repercussions
entries: Disobeying your Iron Command has lasting consequences. If an enemy refuses to kneel to you, you can deal {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent mental damage} instead of normal mental damage. You must decide whether the mental damage will be persistent before your enemy chooses whether to kneel or not. The amount of damage is unchanged.

feats.name: Ironblood Stance
entries: You enter the stance of impenetrable iron, refusing to yield to any blow. You can make iron sweep unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 bludgeoning damage; are in the brawling group; and have the {@trait Nonlethal|PC1|nonlethal}, {@trait Parry|PC1|parry}, {@trait Sweep|PC1|sweep}, and {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed} traits.
While in Ironblood Stance, you gain resistance 2 to all damage. The resistance increases to 3 at 12th level, to 4 at 16th level, and to 5 at 20th level.
feats.requirements: You are unarmored.

feats.name: Ironblood Surge
entries: You steel yourself, preparing to resist oncoming attacks and using your muscles to absorb the impact. You gain the benefits of your iron sweep's {@trait Parry|PC1|parry} trait (a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn) and your resistance from Ironblood Stance increases to your Strength modifier (if it's higher) for the same duration.
feats.requirements: You are in Ironblood Stance.

feats.name: Iruxi Armaments
entries: Your weapons are those you were born with. Choose one of the following options:

items: {@b Claws} Your claw attack deals 1d6 slashing damage instead of 1d4 and gains the {@trait Versatile|PC1|versatile P} trait.
{@b Fangs} You gain a fangs {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed} attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage and is in the brawling group.
{@b Tail} You gain a tail unarmed attack that deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage, is in the brawling group, and has the {@trait Sweep|PC1|sweep} trait.

entries: At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of the unarmed attacks you have gained or improved with this feat, you get its critical specialization effect.
special: You can take this feat multiple times, choosing a different unarmed attack option each time.

feats.name: Iruxi Spirit Strike
entries: Your iruxi unarmed attacks channel the spiritual energy of your ancestors. Any unarmed attacks you acquire from the lizardfolk ancestry, lizardfolk heritages, or lizardfolk ancestry feats gain the effects of a ghost touch property rune.

feats.name: Jinx Glutton
entries: You can Eat Fortune once per hour, rather than once per day.

feats.name: Juggernaut's Fortitude
entries: Your proficiency rank in Fortitude saves increases to master.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Barbarian Dedication|PC2}; expert in Fortitude saves

feats.name: Jungle Strider
entries: You are adept at dodging roots, foliage, and other jungle obstacles. You ignore {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain} in forests and jungles. In addition, when you use the {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} skill to {@action Balance|PC1} on narrow surfaces or uneven ground made of plant material, you aren't off-guard, and when you roll a success at one of these Acrobatics checks, you get a critical success instead.

feats.name: Just As Planned
entries: In the blink of an eye, you calculate your enemy's movements and know exactly where to aim your next blow. If your next action is to {@action Devise a Stratagem|PC2}, you can roll the d20 twice and take the higher result.

feats.name: Just One More Thing
entries: After your attempt to influence someone goes poorly, you add another bit of information or ask a pointed question, possibly salvaging your previous attempt. Reroll the failed check and use the new result. If the target of the failed check is involved with one of your active investigations, double your investigation bonus from Pursue a Lead on the rerolled check. That creature is temporarily immune to Just One More Thing for 1 day.

You can also use this action if you failed, but didn't critically fail, at a check to {@action Lie|PC1}, {@action Gather Information|PC1}, {@action Make an Impression|PC1}, or {@action Coerce|PC1}. In this case, rather than spending 1 action, adding Just One More Thing takes you half the amount of time you initially spent on the check, to a minimum of 1 more round.
feats.requirements: Your most recent action was to {@action Demoralize|PC1}, {@action Feint|PC1}, or {@action Request|PC1}, and you failed but didn’t critically fail.

feats.name: Just the Facts
entries: You fundamentally understand everything to the point where your research can't possibly be wrong. You are permanently {@condition Quickened|PC1|quickened} and can use the extra action to {@action Recall Knowledge|PC1}. In addition, you gain the following benefits with Recall Knowledge.

items: Your checks to Recall Knowledge are no longer {@trait Secret|PC1|secret}.
When you Recall Knowledge, you use the outcome for one degree of success better than the result of your check.
If an effect (such as {@feat Dubious Knowledge|PC1}) would give you inaccurate information from your Recall Knowledge check, you know which information is inaccurate.
When one of your allies Recalls Knowledge and gains false information, you also know that information is inaccurate if they share it with you.

feats.name: Keen Follower
entries: Your keen observation of your allies has made you better at following their lead. When using the {@action Follow the Expert|PC1} activity in exploration mode, you gain a +3 circumstance bonus if the ally you are following is an expert and a +4 circumstance bonus if your ally is a master.

You can share your observations with others to help further coordinate the group. If the ally you are following has {@feat Quiet Allies|PC1} or another skill feat that allows the group to roll a single skill check for an exploration activity and use the lowest modifier, they can instead use your modifier, even if it's not the lowest.

feats.name: Keen Recollection
entries: You can recall all sorts of information. You gain the keen recollection class feature.

feats.name: Keep Pace
entries: Once you are upon your prey, they can’t escape. {@action Stride|PC1} up to your Speed, following the foe and keeping it in reach throughout its movement until it stops moving or you’ve moved your full Speed. You can use Keep Pace to {@action Burrow|PC1}, {@action Climb|PC1}, {@action Fly|PC1}, or {@action Swim|PC1} instead of Stride if you have the corresponding movement type.
feats.trigger: Your prey is within reach and attempts to {@trait Move|PC1|move} away from you.

feats.name: Kholo Lore
entries: You paid close attention to the senior hunters in your clan to learn their tricks. You gain the trained proficiency rank in {@skill Stealth|PC1} and {@skill Survival|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
You also gain the {@feat Additional Lore|PC1} general feat for Kholo Lore.

feats.name: Kholo Weapon Familiarity
entries: You gain access to all {@trait Uncommon|PC1|uncommon} weapons with the {@trait Kholo|PC2|kholo} trait. You have familiarity with weapons with the kholo trait plus the {@equipment Flail|PC1|flail}, {@equipment Khopesh|PC2|khopesh}, {@equipment Mambele|PC2|mambele}, and {@equipment War Flail|PC1|war flail}—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.
At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.

feats.name: Knockback
entries: The weight of your swing drives your enemy back. You {@creatureability Push|RoE|push} the enemy back 5 feet, with the effects of a successful {@action Shove|PC1}. You can follow the enemy as normal for a successful Shove.
feats.requirements: Your last action was a successful {@action Strike|PC1}.

feats.name: Knockback Strike
entries: You focus your strength into a blow powerful enough to push an enemy away from you. Make an unarmed Strike. If you hit, attempt an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check to {@action Shove|PC1} the target. This attack uses the same multiple attack penalty as your Strike, and doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty.

feats.name: Knowledge of Shapes
entries: Inspiration lets you surpass your preconceptions of your spells' limits. You use {@feat Reach Spell|PC2} or {@feat Widen Spell|PC2} as a free action.

feats.name: Known Weaknesses
entries: Whenever you {@action Devise a Stratagem|PC2}, you can also attempt a check to {@action Recall Knowledge|PC1} as part of that action before rolling the d20. If you critically succeed at the Recall Knowledge check, you notice a weakness and can convey the information to allies to grant each of them a +1 circumstance bonus to their next attack roll against the subject, as long as their attack is made before the beginning of your next turn. If you choose an attack stratagem, this bonus applies to that attack roll too.

feats.name: Kobold Lore
entries: You attentively learned key kobold survival strategies from your elders. You gain the trained proficiency rank in {@skill Stealth|PC1} and {@skill Thievery|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
You also gain the {@feat Additional Lore|PC1} general feat for Kobold Lore.

feats.name: Kobold Weapon Familiarity
entries: You gain access to all {@trait Uncommon|PC1|uncommon} weapons with the {@trait Kobold|PC2|kobold} trait. You have familiarity with weapons with the kobold trait plus the {@equipment Greatpick|PC1|greatpick}, {@equipment Light Pick|PC1|light pick}, and {@equipment Pick|PC1|pick}—for the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.
At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.

feats.name: Lab Rat
entries: You've spent more than your share of time in an alchemy lab. You have been exposed to a wide variety of alchemical poisons and harmful substances, leaving you with an increased tolerance of their effects. You have a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against {@trait Poison|PC1|poisons} and {@trait Disease|PC1|diseases}. If you roll a success on your saving throw against a poison or disease, you get a critical success instead.

feats.name: Laughing Kholo
entries: Your sinister giggle is a sound of warning and threat. You gain the {@feat Battle Cry|PC1} skill feat. You don't take a penalty when you attempt to {@action Demoralize|PC1} a creature that doesn't understand your language.

feats.name: Lead Climber
entries: When climbing, you can prepare routes for others to follow, and you can pull your allies up to avoid disaster. When your allies attempt to {@action Climb|PC1} a route you set using the {@action Follow the Expert|PC1} exploration activity, if any of them critically fail their checks to Climb, you can attempt an Athletics check against the same DC. If you succeed, your ally only fails instead of critically failing. If you also critically fail, you both experience the consequences of the critical failure.

feats.name: Lead Investigator
entries: You spend 1 minute briefing up to four allies about one of your open investigations. Those allies gain the same circumstance bonus you do from Pursue a Lead to checks to investigate the question at the heart of that investigation. This bonus lasts until you cease Pursing that Lead or for 1 day, whichever comes first. This doesn't confer any other benefits of pursuing a lead, such as adding the circumstance bonus to your saves with {@feat Detective's Readiness|PC2}.

feats.name: Lead the Pack
entries: You can have up to two animal companions active at once. However, when you do, it’s slightly more difficult to Command them. If you don’t Command either of your companions, one of the two (your choice) can still use 1 action on your turn to {@action Stride|PC1} or {@action Strike|PC1}, per {@feat Mature Beastmaster Companion|PC2}, but not both. When you Command an Animal, either choose one of the companions to take 2 actions, as normal, or else each companion can take 1 action to Stride or Strike. Either way, you can’t Command an Animal to make either companion act again until your next turn
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Mature Beastmaster Companion|PC2}; you have multiple animal companions

feats.name: Leading Dance
entries: You sweep your foe into your dance. Attempt a Performance check against an adjacent enemy's Will DC.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: Your foe is swept up in your dance. You both move up to 10 feet in the same direction, remaining adjacent to one another. Your movement doesn't trigger reactions from the target (and the target's movement doesn't trigger reactions because it's {@rule Forced Movement|PC1|forced movement}).

items.name: Success
entries: As critical success, but you both move only 5 feet.

items.name: Failure
entries: The foe doesn't follow your steps. You can move 5 feet if you choose, but this movement triggers reactions normally.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You stumble, falling {@condition Prone|PC1|prone} in your space.

feats.requirements: You are adjacent to an enemy.

feats.name: Leech-Clip
entries: You are trained to capture deserters, or “leeches.” Make a melee Strike with weapon from the flail group. On a hit, the target takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speed (or a –15-foot status penalty on a critical hit). The penalty lasts for 1 round. It applies only if the target has a land Speed and depends on legs or other targetable appendages to use its land Speed. As with all penalties to Speed, this can't reduce a creature's Speed below 5 feet.

feats.name: Left-hand Blood
entries: It's said that the flesh of the right side of a hyena can heal diseases, but that the flesh of the left side is deadly and poisonous. You deal 1 slashing damage to yourself to poison a weapon you are holding. If you hit with the weapon and deal damage, the target also takes 1d4 {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent poison damage}. The poison on your weapon becomes inert after you hit, or at the end of your next turn, whichever comes first.

feats.name: Legendary Guide
entries: You know the wilderness so well that you can help your party travel through it with ease. When you are setting the path for your party through wilderness terrain, your party gains a +10-foot circumstance bonus to its Speed for the purpose of calculating the party's {@rule Travel Speed|PC1|travel Speed}, your party's travel Speed doesn't decrease in {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain}, and greater difficult terrain halves your party's travel Speed instead of reducing it to a third. This doesn't increase your party's Speed during an encounter or allow your party to ignore difficult terrain during an encounter.

feats.name: Legendary Laugh
entries: Your laugher echoes in the minds of your enemies. You can {@action Demoralize|PC1} creatures up to 60 feet away. Additionally, whenever you successfully Demoralize a creature, it takes 3d8 mental damage (or 6d8 mental damage on a critical success).

feats.name: Legendary Rider
entries: You and your mount move like one being, effortlessly reading each other’s signals and synchronizing even in the thick of battle. Whenever you’re riding your mount, you are quickened; you can use the extra action only to command your mount using the {@action Command an Animal|PC1} skill action.

feats.name: Lethal Finisher
entries: You stab your foe in a vital organ, possibly killing them outright. Make a Strike. On a success, you forego your precise strike damage from the finisher. Instead, your target takes additional precision damage based on a Fortitude save against your class DC. If your Strike was a critical hit, the target's saving throw outcome is one degree worse.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: You deal 6 precision damage.

items.name: Success
entries: You deal 6d6 precision damage.

items.name: Failure
entries: You deal 12d6 precision damage.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You deal 18d6 precision damage.

feats.name: Leverage Connections
entries: You know the right people who can get things done for you in certain circles. Once per week, when you're in an area that has an established group of influential nobles, mercantile elites, or the like (if you have Courtly Graces), or a network of unsavory characters such as a thieves' guild (if you have Streetwise), you can use Society to {@action Request|PC1} a favor or aid from those people as if they were friendly to you. Your request must make sense for the type of people you contact. For instance, a member of the royal court could secure you a proper invitation to a fancy ball, while a local burglar could point out a way to stealthily infiltrate that same party. If you critically succeed this check, your connection gives a piece of helpful advice or lets you in on a small secret, granting you or a member of your party a +2 circumstance bonus to the first skill check you attempt when acting on the favor. If you critically fail this check, you might have to perform some service for your connection to get back in their good graces, as determined by the GM.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Courtly Graces|PC1} or {@feat Streetwise|PC1}; expert in {@skill Society|PC1}

feats.name: Lie Detector
entries: You're adept at noticing the tells of a liar—sweat, flushing, a quavering voice, a quickening pulse. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to {@action Sense Motive|PC1} and to Perception DCs against attempts to {@action Lie|PC1} to you. When you determine someone is lying to you, you can use their deceit to your advantage to gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the next {@skill Deception|PC1}, {@skill Diplomacy|PC1}, {@skill Intimidation|PC1}, or {@skill Performance|PC1} check you attempt against that creature within the next minute.
If you would gain your Pursue a Lead investigation bonus to any of the above checks, that bonus increases by 1 instead of you gaining the +1 bonus listed.

feats.name: Lifesense
entries: You have a limited ability to sense life force, like your psychopomp forebears. You gain {@creatureability Lifesense|MC1|lifesense} as an imprecise sense with a range of 10 feet. This allows you to sense the life force of living and {@trait Undead|PC1|undead} creatures within the listed range. The sense can distinguish between the vitality energy animating living creatures and the void energy animating undead creatures, much as sight distinguishes colors.

feats.name: Light Paws
entries: You can balance on your toes to step carefully over obstructions. You Stride and then Step, or Step and then Stride, ignoring {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain} during this movement.

feats.name: Lighter than Air
entries: Your mysterious steps become even lighter, transcending the mortal world altogether. When you have the {@trait Cursebound|PC2|cursebound} condition, you gain the effects of {@spell Fly|PC1|fly}. If you are cursebound 3 or greater, you gain a +10-foot status bonus to your fly Speed.

feats.name: Lightning Qi
entries: Qi flows freely from within you. If your next action is to cast a qi spell that takes at least two actions to cast, reduce the number of actions to cast it by 1 (minimum 1 action).

feats.name: Lightning Snares
entries: You can rig a trap with incredible speed. When you create a {@trait Snare|PC2|snare} that normally takes 1 minute to {@action Craft|PC1}, you can Craft it using a single Interact action instead.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Snarecrafter Dedication|PC2}; master in {@skill Crafting|PC1} * This archetype offers Lightning Snares at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Lingering Breath
entries: Your draconic breath destroys the surrounding environment and leaves your enemies in pain. When you use Breath of the Dragon, the area of your breath becomes {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain} for 1 minute. In addition, a creature who fails or critically fails its saving throw takes 2d6 {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent damage} of the same type.

feats.name: Linguist Dedication
entries: You have studied languages and their development. You become trained in {@skill Society|PC1}; if you were already trained in Society, you instead become an expert in Society. You gain the {@feat Multilingual|PC1} skill feat twice.

feats.name: Lizardfolk Lore
entries: You listened carefully to the tales passed down among your community. You gain the trained proficiency rank in {@skill Survival|PC1} and either {@skill Nature|PC1} or {@skill Occultism|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
You also gain the {@feat Additional Lore|PC1} general feat for either Astrology Lore or Lizardfolk Lore.

feats.name: Long Tongue
entries: You've learned to stretch your exceptionally long tongue beyond its original limits. When you use your tongue to deliver touch-range spells or perform very simple Interact actions, you can do so at a distance that is 5 feet beyond your usual reach.

feats.name: Long-Nosed Form
entries: You transform into a specific, curious-looking human form. This human form is the same age and body type as your tengu form and has roughly analogous physical traits, such as height, though your nose remains as long as your beak and your complexion has red undertones, no matter the skin color of your human form. Using Long-Nosed Form counts as creating a disguise for the {@action Impersonate|PC1} use of {@skill Deception|PC1}. Due to your imperfect transformation, your transformation doesn't automatically defeat Perception DCs to determine whether you are human, though you may be able to explain away or hide your tengu traits.

You lose your beak unarmed Strike in your human form, as well as any other unarmed Strikes you gained from a tengu heritage or ancestry feat. You remain in your human form indefinitely, until you Dismiss this effect.

feats.name: Loyal Warhorse
entries: The loyalty you and your mount share is unbreakable. The mount you gained with Faithful Steed is now a mature animal companion. In addition, your mount never attacks you, even if it is magically compelled to do so.

feats.name: Luck of the Clowder
entries: When you use Cat's Luck to reroll, any creatures you choose within 10 feet who also just failed against the same effect (such as a single spell) can also reroll their saving throws and use the better result.

feats.name: Lucky Break
entries: You are luckier even than most catfolk. You can trigger Cat's Luck when you fail or critically fail a Fortitude saving throw, Will saving throw, {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} check, or {@skill Athletics|PC1} check in addition to Reflex saving throws. You still can use Cat's Luck only once per day.

feats.name: Mage Hunter
entries: You use your hatred of magic to lash out at a known spellcaster. Make a melee Strike against the required creature. If you hit and deal damage, the target is {@condition Stupefied|PC1|stupefied 1}, or stupefied 2 on a critical hit, until the beginning of your next turn.
feats.requirements: You’ve seen the target {@action Cast a Spell|PC1}.

feats.name: Magic Ammunition
entries: You imbue your ammunition with raw and potent magic, transforming it to suit your needs in any situation. When you select this feat, choose three types of common magical ammunition of 4th level or lower from {@i GM Core} or this book. Your GM might allow you to choose from other types of magical ammunition of an appropriate level, such as {@trait Uncommon|PC1|uncommon} ammunition, or ammunition from other books. You gain the Transform Ammunition action.

{@b Transform Ammunition} {@as f} ({@trait Magical|PC1|magical}) {@b Frequency} once per round; {@b Effect} You transform a non-magical arrow or bolt on your person into a piece of magical ammunition of one type you chose for the Magic Ammunition feat. You must shoot the ammunition before the end of your turn or the magic dissipates. If the ammunition has an Activate entry, you still need to spend the required actions to activate the ammunition before shooting it. You can choose a type of magical ammunition that is typically not available to the type of ammunition you're using—for example, you can use climbing bolt on an arrow, even though that magical ammunition is normally only found on bolts.
special: You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do, select three additional types of magical ammunition as described above.

feats.name: Magic Sense
entries: You have a literal sixth sense for ambient magic in your vicinity. You can sense the presence of magic auras as though you were always using a 1st-rank detect magic spell. This detects magic in your field of vision only. When you Seek, you gain the benefits of a 3rd-rank detect magic spell on things you see (in addition to the normal benefits of Seeking). You can turn this sense off and on with a free action at the start or the end of your turn.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Magical Scholastics
entries: While study is key to your success, a bit of magic can be a helpful aid in discovering the secrets of the past. You can cast {@spell Detect Magic|PC1|detect magic}, {@spell Guidance|PC1|guidance}, and {@spell Read Aura|PC1|read aura} as occult innate cantrips.

feats.name: Magical Scrounger
entries: You can {@action Craft|PC1|craft} a temporary wondrous item using the magic scrounged from all around. Once per day, you can Cobble Together a temporary magic item. The temporary item must be common, magical, half your level or lower, and be able to be held, wielded, or worn. Any Craft requirements must be provided as normal.
You can't Cobble Together a consumable, a rune, or an item with runes. If the item must be worn or affixed, removing it once it's affixed or donned destroys it.

feats.name: Magpie Snatch
entries: You move quickly, snatching a shiny item that catches your eye. Stride twice, and you can Interact to pick up an unattended object at any point during your movement.

feats.name: Majestic Presence
entries: By taking an impressive stance, the full force of your personality cows lesser beings. Each creature in a 20- foot emanation must attempt a Will save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. Regardless of the result of the saving throw, the creature is temporarily immune to your Majestic Presence for 24 hours.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: The creature is unaffected.

items.name: Success
entries: The creature is {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened 1}.

items.name: Failure
entries: The creature is frightened 2.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: The creature is frightened 4.

feats.name: Make 'em Sweat
entries: Your line of questioning lets a suspect know you can see right through them, shaking them to the core. When you succeed at using {@action Pointed Question|PC2}, the target is also {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened 1} (or frightened 2 on a critical success). This added effect is an {@trait Emotion|PC1|emotion} and {@trait Fear|PC1|fear} effect, but the other effects of Pointed Question still apply even if the target is immune to fear.

feats.name: Makeshift Strike
entries: You quickly snatch up whatever is nearby and then attack with it as an improvised weapon. You Interact to pick up an unattended object in reach you could use as an improvised weapon, then {@action Strike|PC1} with that improvised weapon.

feats.name: Many Guises
entries: You can take on any number of mundane guises. Whenever you change your identity, instead of taking on your social or vigilante identity, you can become someone completely ordinary. This identity isn't a specific individual—rather, you become a nondescript member of your ancestry, of any gender, and from a mundane occupation such as common laborer, farmer, or peasant. Spells and abilities detect you as if you were this ordinary identity, rather than either of your two real identities, unless they succeed at a counteract check against the same Deception DC used for Vigilante Dedication. Using class or dedication abilities ends this disguise.

feats.name: Mariner's Fire
entries: You conjure uncanny orbs of spiritual flame that float above or below the water's surface.
