You can cast the {@spell Ignition|PC1|ignition} cantrip as a primal innate spell at will, heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up. Your {@i ignition} spell takes the form of orbs of fire, and you can cast it underwater.

feats.name: Marsh Runner
entries: When you use the Step action, you can ignore {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain} caused by flooding, swamps, or quicksand. In addition, when you use the {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} skill to {@action Balance|PC1} on narrow surfaces or uneven marshy ground, you aren't {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard}, and if you roll a success on the Acrobatics check, you get a critical success instead.

feats.name: Marshal Dedication
entries: You’ve combined your social skills and combat training to become a talented combat leader. Choose {@skill Diplomacy|PC1} or {@skill Intimidation|PC1}. You become trained in that skill or become an expert if you were already trained in it.

In addition, while you’re conscious, you’re surrounded by a marshal’s aura in a 15-foot emanation. Your aura has the {@trait Emotion|PC1|emotion}, {@trait Mental|PC1|mental}, and {@trait Visual|PC1|visual} traits and grants you and allies in the aura a +1 status bonus to saving throws against {@trait Fear|PC1|fear}.
feats.prerequisites: trained in {@skill Diplomacy|PC1} or {@skill Intimidation|PC1}; trained in martial weapons

feats.name: Martial Artist Dedication
entries: You have trained to use your fists as deadly weapons and can deliver devastatingly powerful blows with them. The damage die for your {@equipment Fist|PC1|fist} unarmed attacks becomes 1d6 instead of 1d4. You don’t take the –2 circumstance penalty for making a lethal attack with your {@trait Nonlethal|PC1|nonlethal} unarmed attacks.

feats.name: Master Eldritch Archer Spellcasting
entries: You gain the master spellcasting benefits.

feats.name: Master of Many Styles
entries: You move fluidly between stances, using your mastery of combat to always adopt the best tactics. You use an action with the stance trait.
feats.trigger: Your turn begins

feats.name: Master Oracle Spellcasting
entries: You gain the master spellcasting benefits.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Expert Oracle Spellcasting|PC2}; legendary in {@skill Religion|PC1}

feats.name: Master Qi Spells
entries: You have achieved near-total mastery of your qi. You gain {@spell Medusa's Wrath|PC2|medusa's wrath}, {@spell Touch of Death|PC2|touch of death}, or another 8th-rank qi spell you have access to.
special: You can select this feat more than once, choosing a different spell each time.

feats.name: Master Scroll Cache
entries: Your scroll collection is incredible, brimming with eldritch power, and you can prepare far more of them than an ordinary scroll trickster. In addition to your daily scrolls from the Basic and Expert Scroll Caches, add a single scroll with a 6th-rank spell. At 20th level, add a scroll with a 7th-rank spell.

feats.name: Master Sorcerer Spellcasting
entries: You gain the master spellcasting benefits.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Expert Sorcerer Spellcasting|PC2}; legendary in {@skill Arcana|PC1}, {@skill Nature|PC1}, {@skill Occultism|PC1}, or {@skill Religion|PC1}, depending on bloodline

feats.name: Master Spotter
entries: Your proficiency rank in Perception increases to master.

feats.name: Mature Beastmaster Companion
entries: All of your animal companions grow up, becoming {@rule Mature Animal Companions|PC1|mature animal companions} and gaining additional capabilities.

Your animal companion has greater independence. During an encounter, even if you don't use the {@action Command an Animal|PC1} action, your active animal companion can still use 1 action that round on your turn to Strike or Stride (or {@action Burrow|PC1}, {@action Climb|PC1}, {@action Fly|PC1}, or {@action Swim|PC1} if it has that Speed). It can do this at any point during your turn, as long as you aren't currently taking an action. If it does, that's all the actions it gets that round— you can't Command it later.

feats.name: Mauler Dedication
entries: You specialize in melee weapons that require two hands. You have familiarity with all melee weapons that require two hands to wield or have the {@trait Two-Hand|PC1|two-hand} trait. For the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons. If you are at least an expert in such a weapon, you gain access to the {@rule Critical Specialization|PC1|critical specialization} effect with that weapon.

feats.name: Meddling Futures
entries: You open yourself to the guidance of whatever spirits or powers deign to help you. Roll 1d4 to see what type of spirit is drawn to you. Your next action must be the type of action the spirit prefers, but you also gain the listed benefit for the action as the spirit guides you. If you attempt to use a different action, you must succeed at a DC 6 flat check or the action is lost.

{@b 1 Warrior} You must attempt a {@action Strike|PC1}. You gain a +1 status bonus to your attack roll and a +2 status bonus to damage, or a +6 status bonus to damage if you are at least {@trait Cursebound|PC2|cursebound} 3.
{@b 2 Adept} You must attempt a Perception check or a skill action. You gain a +1 status bonus to the check, or a +2 status bonus if you are cursebound 3.

{@b 3 Sage} You must attempt to {@action Cast a Spell|PC1}. You gain a status bonus to the spell's damage or healing equal to the spell's rank, or equal to the spell's rank + 3 if you are at least cursebound 3.

{@b 4 Wanderer} You must attempt a {@action Stride|PC1} action, or a {@action Fly|PC1}, {@action Climb|PC1}, or {@action Burrow|PC1} action if you have the relevant speed. You gain a +10- foot status bonus to your Speed for the action, or a +20-foot status bonus if you are at least cursebound 3.

feats.name: Medic Dedication
entries: You become an expert in {@skill Medicine|PC1}. When you succeed with {@feat Battle Medicine|PC1} or {@action Treat Wounds|PC1}, the target gains a circumstance bonus to the number of Hit Points they regain equal to 5 HP at DC 20, 10 HP at DC 30, or 15 HP at DC 40.
Once per day, you can use Battle Medicine on a creature that’s temporarily immune due to having already been treated with Battle Medicine. If you’re a master in Medicine, you can do so once per hour.

feats.name: Meditative Focus
entries: Your meditation is so effective that you can achieve a deep focus with the world around you. When you {@action Refocus|PC1}, you regain all your Focus Points instead of 1.

feats.name: Mega Bomb
entries: You can add a highly explosive additive to an alchemical bomb to turn it into a mega bomb. Throwing this bomb takes a 2-action activity instead of a Strike. This isn't a Strike, and you don't make an attack roll. The mega bomb explodes in a 30-foot burst within 60 feet. It deals damage as if each creature were the primary target, with a basic Reflex save. On a failed save, a creature also takes any extra effects that affect a primary target (such as {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} from {@equipment Bottled Lightning|PC2|bottled lightning}). Though all targets in the area take splash damage as primary targets, there is no further splash beyond that area.

feats.name: Mercy
entries: Your touch soothes the body or mind. You can cast {@spell Lay on Hands|PC2|lay on hands} targeting a living creature using 2 actions instead of 1. If you do, you can attempt to counteract one condition of your choice affecting the target. When you select this feat, choose one of the following options, which determines the conditions you can choose: {@b Mercy of the Body} {@condition Blinded|PC1|blinded}, {@condition Dazzled|PC1|dazzled}, {@condition Deafened|PC1|deafened}, {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled}, {@condition Sickened|PC1|sickened}; {@b Mercy of Grace} {@condition Clumsy|PC1|clumsy}, {@condition Grabbed|PC1|grabbed}, {@condition Paralyzed|PC1|paralyzed}; {@b Mercy of the Mind} {@condition Fleeing|PC1|fleeing}, {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened}, {@condition Stupefied|PC1|stupefied}.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.prerequisites: {@spell Lay on Hands|PC2|lay on hands} * This archetype offers Mercy at a different level than displayed here.
special: You can select this feat up to three times. Each time, choose a different type of mercy and add its options to those you can choose when you cast a 2-action {@i lay on hands}.

feats.name: Mesmerizing Gaze
entries: When you meet someone's gaze, they're unable to look away from you. Choose one target creature you can see and that can see you. That creature must succeed at a Will save or be {@condition Fascinated|PC1|fascinated} with you until the end of your next turn; the DC is the higher of your class DC or spell DC. If the creature succeeds at its save or its fascination ends due to a hostile action, it becomes temporarily immune to your Mesmerizing Gaze for 1 day.

feats.name: Mighty Bulwark
entries: Thanks to the incredible connection you have forged with your armor, you can use it to shrug off an extensive array of dangers. Your bonus from the {@trait Bulwark|PC1|bulwark} armor trait increases from +3 to +4, and it applies on all Reflex saves, not just damaging Reflex saves.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.prerequisites: {@feat Sentinel Dedication|PC2} * This archetype offers Mighty Bulwark at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Minion Guise
entries: When you are in your social identity, you can also grant a social identity to an animal companion, familiar, pet, or other minion you gained from a class feature or feat. When changing to your social identity, you also change your minion's appearance to that of a socially acceptable creature of its type, such as grooming a wolf to appear as a large dog or disguising a familiar to appear as an exotic pet. Commanding your minion to use unusual magical or combat abilities it gained from your class features or feats while in this social identity risks exposing your vigilante identity.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Vigilante Dedication|PC2}; expert in {@skill Deception|PC1}; animal companion or familiar

feats.name: Miracle Worker
entries: Your alchemical mastery can resuscitate the recently slain. You can administer a {@equipment Elixir of Life|PC2|major or true elixir of life} to a creature who has been dead for no more than 2 rounds. When you do, that creature is immediately returned to life with 1 Hit Point and becomes {@condition Wounded|PC1|wounded 1}.

feats.name: Mixed Maneuver
entries: You leverage your knowledge of martial arts to mix different maneuvers together into a single flowing combination. Choose any two of {@action Grapple|PC1}, {@action Reposition|PC1}, {@action Shove|PC1}, and {@action Trip|PC1}. Attempt both of the attacks you chose against the same or different creatures, but don't apply the multiple attack penalty until after resolving both attacks.

feats.name: Mobile Finisher
entries: You attack in motion. Stride and then Strike. You can use Mobile Finisher while Burrowing, {@action Climb|PC1|Climbing}, Flying, or Swimming instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

feats.name: Moisture Bath
entries: Your moist skin is especially resistant to damage from temperature-altering effects. Attempt a DC 10 flat check; on a success you recover from any ongoing {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent fire and persistent cold damage}. Additionally, you gain fire and cold resistance equal to half your level for 1 minute.

feats.name: Moment of Clarity
entries: You push back your rage for a moment in order to think clearly. Until the end of this turn, you can use actions with the {@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate} trait even if those actions don't have the {@trait Rage|PC2|rage} trait.

feats.name: Monastic Archer Stance
entries: You enter a specialized stance for a unique martial art centered around the use of a bow. While in this stance, the only Strikes you can make are those using longbows, shortbows, or bows with the monk trait. You can use {@action Flurry of Blows|PC2} with these bows. You can use your other monk feats or monk abilities that normally require {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed} attacks with these bows when attacking within half the first range increment (normally 50 feet for a longbow and 30 feet for a shortbow), so long as the feat or ability doesn't require a single, specific Strike.
feats.requirements: You are unarmored and wielding a {@equipment Longbow|PC1|longbow}, a {@equipment Shortbow|PC1|shortbow}, or a bow with the {@trait Monk|PC1} trait.
special: When you select this feat, you become trained in the longbow, shortbow, and any simple and martial bows with the monk trait. If you gain the expert strikes class feature, your proficiency rank for these weapons increases to expert, and if you gain the master strikes class feature, your proficiency rank for these weapons increases to master.

feats.name: Monastic Weaponry
entries: You have trained with the weaponry of your monastery or school. You gain access to {@trait Uncommon|PC1|uncommon} weapons with the {@trait Monk|PC1|monk} trait and become trained in simple and martial monk weapons. When your proficiency for unarmed attacks increases to expert or master, your proficiency rank for these weapons increases to expert or master as well. If you have familiarity with an {@trait Agile|PC1|agile} or {@trait Finesse|PC1|finesse} weapon (such as from the {@feat Catfolk Weapon Familiarity|PC2} feat), that weapon also gains the monk trait for you.

You can use melee monk weapons with any of your monk feats or monk abilities that normally require unarmed attacks, though not if the feat or ability requires you to use a single specific type of attack, such as {@feat Crane Stance|PC2}. If you gain the critical specialization benefit for unarmed attacks—with the expert strikes class feature, for example— you also gain it with monk weapons.

feats.name: Monk Dedication
entries: You become trained in unarmed attacks and gain the powerful fist class feature. You become trained in your choice of {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} or {@skill Athletics|PC1}; if you’re already trained in both of these skills, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You become trained in monk class DC; if you later gain a qi spell from a monk class feat, you also become trained in spell attack modifier and spell DC.

feats.name: Monk Moves
entries: You gain a +10-foot status bonus to your Speed when you’re not wearing armor.

feats.name: Monk Resiliency
entries: You gain 3 additional Hit Points for each monk archetype class feat you have. As you continue selecting monk archetype class feats, you continue to gain additional Hit Points in this way.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Monk Dedication|PC2}; class granting no more Hit Points per level than 8 + your Constitution modifier

feats.name: Monk's Flurry
entries: You gain the {@action Flurry of Blows|PC2} action. Your fists’ power, however, exceeds your conditioning; once you use Flurry of Blows, you can’t use it again for 1d4 rounds as your muscles recover.

feats.name: Mountain Quake
entries: You stomp, shaking the earth beneath you. Creatures on the ground within a 20-foot emanation take damage equal to your Strength modifier (minimum 0), with a basic Fortitude save against your class DC. On a failure, they also fall {@condition Prone|PC1|prone}. After you use this action, you can't use it again for 1d4 rounds.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.requirements: You are in Mountain Stance.  * This archetype offers Mountain Quake at a different level than displayed here.
special: If you have this feat, the Dexterity modifier cap to your AC while using Mountain Stance increases from +1 to +2.

feats.name: Mountain Stance
entries: You enter the stance of an implacable mountain—a technique created by {@ancestry Dwarf|PC1|dwarven} monks—allowing you to strike with the weight of an avalanche and block blows with your garments. The only Strikes you can make are falling stone unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 bludgeoning damage; are in the brawling group; and have the {@trait Forceful|PC1|forceful}, {@trait Nonlethal|PC1|nonlethal}, and {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed} traits.

While in Mountain Stance, you gain a +4 item bonus to AC and a +2 circumstance bonus to any defenses against {@action Reposition|PC1}, {@action Shove|PC1}, {@action Trip|PC1}, and other {@rule Forced Movement|PC1|forced movement} effects. You have a Dexterity modifier cap to your AC of +0, meaning you don't add your Dexterity to your AC, and your Speeds are all reduced by 5 feet. The item bonus to AC from Mountain Stance is cumulative with armor potency runes on your {@equipment Explorer's Clothing|PC1|explorer's clothing}, {@spell Mystic Armor|PC1|mystic armor}, and bands of force.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.requirements: You are unarmored and touching the ground. * This archetype offers Mountain Stance at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Mountain Stronghold
entries: You focus on your connection to the earth and call upon the mountain to block attacks against you. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC until the beginning of your next turn.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.requirements: You are in Mountain Stance. * This archetype offers Mountain Stronghold at a different level than displayed here.
special: If you have this feat, the Dexterity modifier cap to your AC while you're in Mountain Stance increases from +0 to +1.

feats.name: Mounted Shield
entries: You’ve trained with your shield to defend both yourself and your mount. When you {@action Raise a Shield|PC1} while mounted, both you and your mount gain the shield’s circumstance bonus to AC. If you have the {@feat Shield Block|PC1} reaction, you can use it when your mount would take physical damage, as long as you’re riding your mount. If you do, the shield prevents your mount from taking damage instead of preventing you from taking damage, following the normal rules for Shield Block.

feats.name: Multilingual Cipher
entries: You use multiple languages to create and break codes. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to {@action Decipher Writing|PC1}. If another creature attempts to Decipher Writing you encoded, they take a –2 circumstance penalty unless they speak all the languages you used when you created the writing.

feats.name: Mutable Familiar
entries: Your familiar's supernatural spirit has outgrown its corporeal body. You can conduct a special 10-minute exploration activity to reselect certain familiar abilities, switching one or more of the following abilities for other abilities on this list: amphibious, burrower, climber, darkvision, fast movement, manual dexterity, resistance, and scent. You can reselect only familiar abilities you would normally be able to reselect each day, not required familiar abilities for your familiar. You can't remove an ability that is required for another ability your familiar has (for instance, you can't remove manual dexterity if the familiar has {@companion Item Delivery|PC2|item delivery}).

feats.name: Mutant Innervation
entries: Basic mutagens that affect your mind and thoughts can make you communicate telepathically, protect you from being detected, or let you communicate with anyone. While you're affected by one of the listed mutagens, you get an additional benefit.

items: {@b {@equipment Cognitive Mutagen|PC2}} You also gain the mutagen's item bonus to {@skill Deception|PC1}, {@skill Diplomacy|PC1}, {@skill Intimidation|PC1}, {@skill Medicine|PC1}, {@skill Nature|PC1}, {@skill Performance|PC1}, {@skill Religion|PC1}, and {@skill Survival|PC1} checks. In addition, you can communicate telepathically with creatures within 60 feet with whom you share a language. The communication is two-way once you establish it, so a creature you contact can also communicate with you.

{@b {@equipment Serene Mutagen|PC2}} {@trait Detection|PC1}, {@trait Revelation|PC1|revelation}, and {@trait Scrying|PC1|scrying} effects of 9th rank (or 17th level) or lower detect nothing from you or your possessions and auras. For instance, {@spell Detect Magic|PC1|detect magic} would still detect other magic in the area, but not any magic on you.

{@b {@equipment Silvertongue Mutagen|PC2}} Ignore circumstance penalties you would take to {@skill Deception|PC1}, {@skill Diplomacy|PC1}, {@skill Intimidation|PC1}, and {@skill Performance|PC1} checks. In addition, your words transcend linguistic barriers; everyone listening to you speak hears your words as if you were speaking in their own language (though you don't actually speak that language, nor does this ability allow you to understand any additional languages).

special: If you can be under the effects of multiple mutagens (with the mutagenist greater field discovery, for example), you get all relevant benefits.

feats.name: Mutant Physique
entries: Basic mutagens that affect your physical form can bring out the beast within you, turn you nigh invincible, or make your body more elastic. While you're affected by one of the listed mutagens, you get an additional benefit.

items: {@b {@equipment Bestial Mutagen|PC2}} You gain the mutagen's item bonus to your {@skill Intimidation|PC1} checks. In addition, you increase the damage die size of your claws and jaws by one step, and they gain the {@trait Deadly|PC1|deadly d10} trait.
{@b {@equipment Juggernaut Mutagen|PC2}} You gain {@rule Resistance|PC1|resistance} to all physical damage equal to half your level.

{@b {@equipment Quicksilver Mutagen|PC2}} You can stretch your legs and Step up to 10 feet, and you can squish and compress your body, allowing you to make it through tight spaces as if you were one size smaller, in addition to any effect from Squeezing.

special: If you can be under the effects of multiple mutagens (with the mutagenist greater field discovery, for example), you get all relevant benefits.

feats.name: Mysterious Breadth
entries: Increase the number of spells in your repertoire and number of spell slots you gain from oracle archetype feats by 1 for each spell rank other than your two highest oracle spell slots.

feats.name: Mysterious Repertoire
entries: Your mystery holds unknowable depths of magic not always associated with the divine. You can have one spell in your spell repertoire not on the {@trait Divine|PC1|divine} spell list, in addition to spells you've added to your spell list from abilities like divine access. You cast that spell as a divine spell. You can swap which spell you add and from which tradition as you could any other oracle spell, but you can't use this feat to have more than one spell from another tradition in your spell repertoire at the same time.

feats.name: Mystery Conduit
entries: The power of your mystery enables you access to myriad magic. If your next action is to {@action Cast a Spell|PC1} of 5th rank or lower that has no duration, you do not expend a spell slot.

feats.name: Necromantic Physiology
entries: Your unusual physiology has developed in a way that makes it difficult for parasites and other infestations to prey upon you. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against diseases. If you roll a success on a saving throw against a {@trait Disease|PC1|disease}, you get a critical success instead. If you have a different ability that would improve the save in this way (such as the battle hardened fighter class feature), if you roll a critical failure on the save you get a failure instead.

feats.name: Never Tire
entries: As long as you have an audience, you can continue to perform even when you are on the brink of collapse. Indeed, you must— you have an obligation to your fans! You delay the effects of the {@condition Fatigued|PC1|fatigued} condition for 1 minute or until you are no longer observed by at least three creatures who aren’t enemies, whichever comes first. If the fatigued condition has a duration, the duration begins to elapse only after the delay. You can’t further delay or prevent the fatigued condition after this ability ends.
feats.requirements: You are observed by at least three creatures who aren’t enemies.
feats.trigger: You would gain the {@condition Fatigued|PC1|fatigued} condition.

feats.name: Night Magic
entries: You can tap into the magic that runs through your blood. You gain {@spell Animal Form|PC1|animal form} (wolf only, using the statistics for a canine) and {@spell Mist|PC1|mist} as 2nd-rank divine innate spells. You can cast each of these spells once per day.

feats.name: Nimble Reprisal
entries: You can use {@action Retributive Strike|PC2} at greater distance. You can use a ranged weapon to make a ranged Strike instead of a melee Strike for Retributive Strike. The enemy needs to be in range, but not in reach, and it must still be in your champion's aura. You can also make melee Strikes against enemies a bit farther away. If the enemy that triggered your reaction is outside your reach but is within 5 feet of your reach, as part of your reaction you can Step to put the enemy in your reach before making a melee Retributive Strike.

feats.name: Nimble Shield Hand
entries: You are so used to wielding a shield that you can do so even while using the hand that’s holding it for other tasks that require the dexterity of a hand. The hand you use to wield a shield counts as a free hand for the purposes of the Interact action. You can also hold another object in this hand (but you still can’t use it to wield a weapon). This benefit doesn’t apply to tower shields, which are still too cumbersome.

feats.name: No Escape
entries: You keep pace with a retreating foe. Stride up to your Speed, following the enemy and keeping it in reach throughout its movement until it stops moving or you've moved your full Speed. You can use No Escape to {@action Burrow|PC1}, {@action Climb|PC1}, {@action Fly|PC1}, or {@action Swim|PC1} instead of Stride if you have the corresponding movement type.
feats.trigger: An enemy within reach attempts to {@trait Move|PC1|move} away from you.

feats.name: Nocturnal Senses
entries: Your senses gain even greater clarity. While raging, if you have {@rule Low-Light Vision|PC1|low-light vision} you gain {@creatureability Darkvision|MC1|darkvision}, and if you have scent the range of your {@rule Imprecise Senses|PC1|imprecise} {@rule Scent|PC1|scent} increases to 60 feet.

feats.name: Nocturnal Tripkee
entries: You tend to do most of your hunting and work at night and have adapted to the requirements of nocturnal life. You gain {@creatureability Darkvision|MC1|darkvision}, allowing you to see in {@rule Darkness|PC1|darkness} and {@rule Dim Light|PC1|dim light} just as well as you can in bright light. However, in darkness, you see in black-and-white only.
special: You can take this feat only at 1st level, and you can't retrain out of this feat or into this feat.

feats.name: Nudge the Scales
entries: You lay a finger on the scales of life and death to heal a creature, regardless of whether it's living or {@trait Undead|PC1|undead}. You restore Hit Points equal to 2 + double your level to one creature within 30 feet.

In addition, you can mediate during your daily preparations to place yourself on one side of the scales. Choose life or death. If you align yourself with life, you can be targeted and healed by vitality healing effects, as normal for most living creatures; if you align yourself with death, you gain the {@creatureability Void Healing|MC1|void healing} ability, and can instead be targeted and healed by {@trait Void|PC1|void} effects and other effects that restore Hit Points to undead creatures.

feats.name: Numb to Death
entries: Your past has left you numb to death's call. The first time each day that you regain Hit Points while you are {@condition Dying|PC1|dying}, you gain a circumstance bonus to the number of Hit Points you regain equal to your level, and you neither gain the {@condition Wounded|PC1|wounded} condition nor increase the value of this condition.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Diehard|PC1}; you have died at least once

feats.name: Occult Dragonblood
entries: Your blood contains a tiny fragment of unusual or inexplicable power from a mysterious dragon, such as a conspirator dragon or omen dragon. You are drawn to the stranger parts of the world and can generally spot them with a glance. You gain the trained proficiency rank in {@skill Occultism|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in Occultism (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the {@feat Oddity Identification|PC1} skill feat. If you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose an occult dragon.

feats.name: Occult Evolution
entries: You draw power from the obscure secrets of the universe. You become trained in one skill of your choice. Additionally, once per day, you can spend 1 minute to choose one {@trait Mental|PC1|mental} occult spell you don't know and add it to your spell repertoire. You lose this temporary spell the next time you make your daily preparations (though you can use this ability to add it again later).

feats.name: One For All
entries: With precisely the right words of encouragement, you bolster an ally's efforts. Designate an ally within 30 feet; this action counts as sufficient preparation to {@action Aid|PC1} that ally. When you use the Aid reaction to help that ally, you can roll {@skill Diplomacy|PC1} in place of the usual check and the action gains the {@trait Bravado|PC2|bravado} trait.

feats.name: One-inch Punch
entries: You put all your force into a single mighty, carefully controlled blow. Make an unarmed Strike. If you spend two actions and this Strike hits, you deal an extra die of weapon damage. You can instead spend 3 actions to perform an even more powerful attack, dealing a second additional die of weapon damage on a hit. If you're at least 10th level, the number of additional dice you add from this feat doubles, for a total of 2 additional dice if you spend 2 actions or 4 additional dice if you spend 3 actions. If you're at least 18th level, the number of additional dice you add from this feat triples, for a total of 3 additional dice if you spend 2 actions or 6 additional dice if you spend 3 actions.

feats.name: One-millimeter Punch
entries: Your punches have incredible force and control. When you damage a target using One-Inch Punch, you can focus your qi to send the foe flying. If you do, the target must attempt a Fortitude save against your class DC.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: The target is unaffected.

items.name: Success
entries: The target is pushed back 5 feet.

items.name: Failure
entries: The target is pushed back 10 feet.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: The target is pushed back 10 feet for each action you spent on One-Inch Punch.

feats.name: One-Toed Hop
entries: Assuming a peculiar stance, you make a short hop on each toe. You make a vertical {@action Leap|PC1} without triggering reactions that can be triggered by {@trait Move|PC1|move} actions or upon leaving or entering a square.

feats.name: Ongoing Investigation
entries: You're always investigating what's around you, even as you perform other activities. You can move at full Speed while using the {@action Investigate|PC1} exploration activity, and you can use another exploration activity while Investigating.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Ongoing Selfishness
entries: Your powerful personality and incredible ego demand that you protect yourself above all else. After you use {@action Selfish Shield|PC2}, you gain resistance to all further damage from the triggering enemy until the end of the turn on which you used the reaction. This resistance is equal to half your Selfish Shield resistance.

feats.name: Ongoing Strategy
entries: You're constantly studying small aspects of everyone's movements, even if you don't have a stratagem in place ahead of time. On any Strike for which you didn't {@action Devise a Stratagem|PC2}, you still deal precision damage equal to your number of strategic strike damage dice so long as the weapon or {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed} attack you used is one that would have let you use your Intelligence modifier had you Devised a Stratagem.

feats.name: Opportunistic Grapple
entries: You use an opening to capture your prey. You attempt an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check to {@action Grapple|PC1} your prey.
feats.requirements: Your prey is within your reach, you have one free hand, and your target is no more than one size larger than you.
feats.trigger: Your prey critically fails on an attack roll against you with a melee {@action Strike|PC1}.

feats.name: Oracle Dedication
entries: Choose a mystery. You become trained in {@skill Religion|PC1} and the mystery’s skill; if you were already trained, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the curse associated with your mystery, which follows the normal rules for an oracular curse.

You cast spells like an oracle and gain the {@action Cast a Spell|PC1} activity. You gain a spell repertoire with two cantrips, either common divine cantrips or other divine cantrips you learn or discover. You’re trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for oracle archetype spells is Charisma, and they are divine oracle spells.

feats.name: Oracular Providence
entries: Your mystery grants you access to deep reserves of truly miraculous {@trait Divine|PC1|divine} power. You gain an additional 10th-rank spell slot.

feats.name: Oracular Warning
entries: You have a premonition about impending danger that you use to warn your allies. Each ally within 20 feet gains a +2 status bonus to their initiative roll and gains temporary Hit Points equal to half your level, which last for 1 minute. If you are {@trait Cursebound|PC2|cursebound} 2 when you use Oracular Warning, the bonus increases to +3, and if you are cursebound 3, the bonus increases to +4.
feats.trigger: You are about to roll for initiative.

feats.name: Overcrowd
entries: As long as you are Small, you can end your movement in the same square as a Small ally. Only two creatures total can share the same space when using this ability or a similar one.

feats.name: Overpowering Charge
entries: You trample foes as you charge past. When you use Barreling Charge and successfully move through a creature’s space, that creature takes bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier. On a critical success, the creature takes double damage and is off-guard until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.prerequisites: {@feat Barreling Charge|PC2} * This archetype offers Overpowering Charge at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Oversized Throw
entries: With a great heave, you seize a piece of your surroundings, such as a boulder, log, table, wagon, or chunk of earth, and hurl it at your foes. The object must be your size or one size smaller than you, and it must not have too much Bulk for you to lift it in the first place. Make a ranged Strike with the object; regardless of the result, the object takes the same amount of damage it would deal on a success. The object is a simple ranged weapon that deals 1d10 bludgeoning damage, has a range increment of 20 feet, and has the {@trait Thrown|PC1|thrown} weapon trait. The damage increases to 2d10 if you have weapon specialization in simple weapons, or 3d10 if you have greater weapon specialization.
feats.requirements: You have one or more hands free.

feats.name: Overwhelming Breath
entries: You control your breathing and align it with your qi, exhaling with controlled force in order to overcome your opponent's resistance. If you use your next action to Cast a Spell that has the {@trait Monk|PC1|monk} trait and no duration, the spell and any Strikes you make as a result of casting it ignore an amount of the target's resistance to physical damage equal to your level.

feats.name: Overwhelming Energy
entries: With a complex gesture, you call upon the primal power of your spell to overcome enemies' resistances. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell, the spell ignores an amount the target's resistance to energy damage equal to your level. This applies to all damage the spell deals, including persistent damage and damage caused by an ongoing effect of the spell, such as the wall created by {@spell Wall of Fire|PC1|wall of fire}. A creature's immunities are unaffected.

feats.name: Pack Hunter
entries: You were taught how to hunt as part of a pack. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to {@action Aid|PC1}, and your allies gain a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to Aid you.

feats.name: Pack Rat
entries: You've learned how to cram vast quantities into small spaces. You can fit an additional 50% of the listed Bulk capacity into mundane storage containers or vehicles. For example, you can fit 6 Bulk in a {@equipment Backpack|PC1|backpack}, or 12 Bulk in a {@equipment Chest|PC1|chest}. This doesn't alter the items' Bulk, nor does it change how much you can store in a {@trait Magical|PC1|magical} or {@trait Extradimensional|PC1|extradimensional} storage space, such as a spacious pouch.

feats.name: Pack Stalker
entries: Ambushes are an honored kholo tradition. You gain the {@feat Terrain Stalker|PC1} feat and can extend its effects to a single ally so long as they remain within 10 feet of you. If you have master proficiency in Stealth, you can extend the effect to two allies. If you have legendary proficiency in Stealth, you can extend it to four allies.

feats.name: Panache Paragon
entries: You find opportunities to perform stylish feats in the moments between others' heartbeats and eye blinks. You are permanently {@condition Quickened|PC1|quickened}. You can use the extra action only to perform a {@trait Bravado|PC2|bravado} action.

feats.name: Paradoxical Mystery
entries: The truest depths of your {@trait Divine|PC1|divine} mystery are fathomless and contradictory, granting you changing powers that even you can barely begin to fathom. Each day during your daily preparations, choose one basic or advanced domain spell from any domain from {@i Player Core}, one of the domains granted by your mystery, another domain to which you have access, or any initial or advanced revelation spell from another mystery. You gain that spell as a revelation spell until your next daily preparations.

feats.name: Parry and Riposte
entries: Your parries and finishers allow you to riposte with the slightest provocation. You can use Opportune Riposte against an enemy who fails at a Strike against you (not just critically fails), provided you have both damaged that creature with a {@trait Finisher|PC2|finisher} on your last turn and currently have a circumstance bonus to AC from the {@trait Parry|PC1|parry} weapon trait, or {@feat Extravagant Parry|PC2}.

feats.name: Parthenogenic Hatchling
entries: You were hatched from an unfertilized egg during hard times for your people, and are a biological copy of your mother. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against {@trait Disease|PC1|diseases}. If you roll a success on a saving throw against a disease, you get a critical success instead. If you have a different ability that would improve the save in this way (such as the battle hardened fighter class feature), if you roll a critical failure on the save you get a failure instead.
You take damage only every 2 hours from thirst and every 2 days from starvation, rather than every hour and every day.
special: You can select this feat only at 1st level.

feats.name: Party Crasher
entries: You attend all the fashionable society parties, no matter how exclusive they might be. Any time you encounter a social event you would ordinarily be denied access to, such as a coronation, royal gala, or other society function, you can spend 1d4 hours to secure entry without the need for a skill check. You find invitations, invitees looking for fashionable dates, temporary jobs with the caterers, event staff willing to look the other way, or some other mode of access for yourself and your allies. This ability doesn’t apply to secret events or other small private gatherings with no staff, dates, or outsiders involved.

feats.name: Path of Iron
entries: With a burst of effort and speed, you weave a nimble path through your many enemies, striking each in turn as you move past them. You {@action Stride|PC1}; this movement doesn’t trigger reactions. You can attempt a melee {@action Strike|PC1} up to three times at any point during your movement, each against a different enemy. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but your multiple attack penalty doesn’t increase until you have made all your attacks.

feats.name: Peerless Form
entries: Your mastery over your body is perfect enough to hold back the ravages of time. You cease aging, though you still die when your time is up. In addition, you gain a +2 status bonus to Fortitude and Will saving throws.

feats.name: Penetrating Projectile
entries: Your projectiles are unhindered by flesh and bone. Make a ranged Strike with a ranged or thrown weapon that deals piercing damage against each creature in a 30-foot line (this uses only one projectile despite the number of Strikes). These Strikes ignore all {@rule Cover|PC1|cover} granted by creatures. Roll damage only once and apply it to each creature you hit. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but don't increase your penalty until you have made all your attacks.
feats.requirements: You are wielding a ranged or thrown weapon that deals piercing damage

feats.name: Perfect Clarity
entries: You burn out all your rage to ensure that your attack lands and your mind remains free. Reroll the triggering attack roll or Will save with a +2 circumstance bonus, and use the better result. You then immediately stop raging.
feats.trigger: You fail or critically fail an attack roll or Will save.

feats.name: Perfect Debilitation
entries: You have perfected the formulas for bombs that impede your enemies. When you use {@feat Debilitating Bomb|PC2}, your target avoids the condition the bomb imposes only if it critically succeeds at its saving throw.

feats.name: Perfect Finisher
entries: You focus your panache into an impeccable assault. Make a Strike, rolling the attack roll twice and using the better result.

feats.name: Perfection's Path
entries: Choose one saving throw (Fortitude, Reflex, or Will) in which you’re an expert. Your proficiency rank in the chosen saving throw increases to master.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Monk Dedication|PC2}; expert in at least one saving throw

feats.name: Performative Weapons Training
entries: You're skilled with flashy weapons and can use them to great effect. You have familiarity with the {@equipment Bo Staff|PC1|bo staff}, {@equipment Dueling Cape|PC1|dueling cape}, {@equipment Spiked Chain|PC1|spiked chain}, {@equipment Sword Cane|PC1|sword cane}, {@equipment Trident|PC1|trident}, {@equipment War Flail|PC1|war flail}, and {@equipment Whip|PC1|whip}. For the purposes of proficiency, you treat these as simple weapons. The GM may add other martial weapons to this list as appropriate for the world or region you are playing in.
Whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.

feats.name: Pernicious Poison
entries: You can add a toxic additive to an alchemical poison to make it splash poison on its target. A poison with this additive deals an amount of poison damage equal to the poison's level if the target succeeds at its initial saving throw against it. A target that critically succeeds at its saving throw against this poison still takes no damage.

feats.name: Persistent Mutagen
entries: You've trained your physical form to remain stable. Once per day, when you consume an alchemical item with the {@trait Infused|PC2|infused} and {@trait Mutagen|PC2|mutagen} traits, you can extend its duration to last until the next time you make your daily preparations instead of its normal duration. Unlike with the normal extension from Extend Elixir, this can exceed the duration of an item created with {@action Quick Alchemy|PC2} beyond its normal 10-minute limit.

feats.name: Person of Interest
entries: Sometimes, you need to follow the leads as they come in the middle of an investigation. Choose a creature that you can see who isn't, to your knowledge, tied to any of your current investigations. For the next minute, you can {@action Devise a Stratagem|PC2} against that creature as a free action.

feats.name: Phonetic Training
entries: You can pronounce and repeat words with near-perfect accuracy even if you don’t understand their meaning, and you can write them down in a phonetic script that allows you or another creature with Phonetic Training to read it later. Even if the words are in a language with sounds you can’t pronounce, you can faithfully transcribe them. Memorizing long sequences of words remains just as difficult as it is normally.

feats.name: Pick Up the Pace
entries: You lead by example and can help others push themselves beyond their normal limits. When Hustling in a group during exploration mode, your group can Hustle for as long as the member who could Hustle longest on their own.

feats.name: Pilgrim's Token
entries: You carry a small token of protection from a site holy to your faith. You gain a {@equipment Religious Symbol (Wooden)|PC1|wooden religious symbol} for your deity for free. As long as this religious symbol is in your possession, when you tie an adversary's initiative roll, you go first.

If you lose this religious symbol, you must purchase or {@action Craft|PC1} a replacement and attune it. Such a token usually costs at least 1 sp, and the attunement takes 10 minutes of prayer. You can also attune a different religious symbol with the same amount of time, but you lose the benefit of the previous religious symbol.
feats.prerequisites: trained in {@skill Religion|PC1}; follower of a specific religion

feats.name: Pinning Fire
entries: You target your opponent's clothing, equipment, or loose flesh with a series of piercing projectiles to pin them to the ground or a nearby surface. If both your attacks hit, the target must succeed at a Reflex save against your class DC or become {@condition Immobilized|PC1|immobilized} until it or an adjacent creature succeeds at a DC 10 {@skill Athletics|PC1} check to remove the pinning projectiles. The creature doesn't become stuck if it is incorporeal, is liquid (like a water elemental or some oozes), or could otherwise escape without effort.
feats.trigger: You use Flurry of Blows to make two ranged piercing weapon {@action Strike|PC1|Strikes} against the same target.

feats.name: Pinpoint Poisoner
entries: Unsuspecting targets are especially vulnerable to your poisons. When you successfully Strike an {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} creature with a poisoned weapon or expose an off-guard creature to an {@trait Inhaled|GMC|inhaled} poison, that creature takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its initial save against that poison.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Pirate Combat Training
entries: You're particularly skilled at wielding the weapons used traditionally by pirates. You gain either the {@feat Combat Climber|PC1} or {@feat Underwater Marauder|PC1} skill feat, even if you do not meet its prerequisites. You have familiarity with the following weapons: {@equipment Hatchet|PC1|hatchet}, {@equipment Rapier|PC1|rapier}, {@equipment Scimitar|PC1|scimitar}, and {@equipment Whip|PC1|whip}—for the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these weapons as simple weapons. Your GM may add additional martial weapons to this list as appropriate for your world or region.
At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.

feats.name: Pirate Dedication
entries: As a pirate, you sail the seas in search of enemy ships to plunder and great adventures to embark on. You gain the {@feat Additional Lore|PC1} general feat for Sailing Lore or for a specific coastal city you have a connection to (such as Port Peril Lore). You ignore the effects of {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain} or {@rule Uneven Ground|PC1|uneven ground} caused by unstable ground (such as the deck of a ship). Additionally, you gain the Boarding Assault action.

{@b Boarding Assault} {@as 2} ({@trait Flourish|PC1|flourish}) Either {@action Stride|PC1} twice or attempt an {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} check (DC determined by the GM, but usually DC 20) to swing up to twice your Speed on a rope or similar object, then {@action Strike|PC1}. If you boarded or disembarked from a boat or similar vehicle during this movement, the Strike deals one additional weapon damage die.

feats.name: Play to the Crowd
entries: You show off for the crowd. Attempt a {@skill Performance|PC1} check; the DC is determined by the GM but is typically the standard DC for your level or the DC to {@action Make an Impression|PC1} on the spectators, whichever is higher. On a success, choose one of the following benefits to gain; on a critical success, choose two benefits:

items: A number of temporary Hit Points equal to your character level. These last for 1 minute.
A +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the end of your next turn.
A +1 circumstance bonus to your next attack roll before the end of your next turn.

feats.trigger: You reduce an enemy to 0 Hit Points during a combat encounter with spectators.

feats.name: Plentiful Snares
entries: You can prepare incredible numbers of {@trait Snare|PC2|snares} each day out of simple ingredients. Double the number of prepared snares granted by Snarecrafter Dedication.

feats.name: Plot the Future
entries: You spend 10 minutes in contemplation to uncannily predict how events will play out. Choose a particular goal or activity you plan to engage in within 1 week, or an event you expect might happen within 1 week. You analyze whether it's likely to come to pass, learning whether it's highly likely, somewhat likely, somewhat unlikely, or highly unlikely. You also gain a piece of advice suggesting a course of action you or your allies could take that might make the chosen event more or less likely, whichever you prefer. The GM determines the likeliness of the event and the piece of advice you learn.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Plummeting Roll
entries: Through nimble movements, a graceful landing, and a bit of luck, you can manage to fall from spectacular heights without a scratch. You gain the {@feat Cat Fall|PC1} skill feat and the following reaction.

{@b Plummeting Roll} {@as r} {@b Trigger} You fall at least 10 feet and take no damage from the fall; {@b Effect} You tuck and roll with the motion. You land on your feet and Stride up to half your Speed.

feats.name: Poison Coat
entries: In nature, certain animals are covered in venomous spines, and just brushing against them can prove deadly. You expend a {@trait Contact|GMC|contact} or {@trait Injury|GMC|injury} poison and spend 10 minutes brushing that poison onto your clothing or weaving sharp, poisoned needles into the garment's fabric. You can have only one poison suffused into your clothing at a time. You can use the Once Bitten reaction while you have a poison suffused in this way.

{@b Once Bitten} {@as r} A creature adjacent to you hits you with a melee unarmed {@action Strike|PC1}; {@b Requirements} You have prepared your clothing to poison attackers; {@b Effect} The triggering creature is exposed to the suffused poison, and the poison becomes inert.

feats.name: Poisoner Dedication
entries: You make a point of always having a few toxins near at hand—you never know when some {@equipment Arsenic|PC2|arsenic} or the like might prove useful. You gain the advanced alchemy benefits. You can use advanced alchemy to create four alchemical poison {@trait Consumable|PC1|consumables} each day. You remember alchemical poison formulas and don't need a formula book for them.

feats.name: Poisoner's Twist
entries: Poisons attack specific parts of the body—one venom might target the lungs, another the circulatory system, while another deteriorates the nerves. You know how to take advantage of such weaknesses. You deal 1d6 damage of the required {@action Strike|PC1}'s damage type and 1d6 {@trait Poison|PC1|poison} damage to the target. If you're at least 18th level, you deal 2d6 damage of each type.
feats.requirements: Your last action was a successful melee {@action Strike|PC1} that dealt damage against a target afflicted by a poison, and you know which poison.

feats.name: Portentous Spell
entries: Your spellcasting is rife with strange lights, mild fumes, and other captivating effects that befuddle your foes. If the next action you use is to {@action Cast a Spell|PC1}, any creature that attempts to use a reaction triggered by your Cast a Spell activity takes a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls and skill checks rolled as part of the reaction. In addition, if the spell includes a spell attack or requires a saving throw, creatures you hit or that fail their saves are {@condition Fascinated|PC1|fascinated} with you until the start of your next turn.

feats.name: Posse
entries: By spending 1 minute giving guidance to help hunt down your prey, you instruct up to five willing creatures to assist you. They gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Seek your prey, to Track your prey, and to Gather Information about your prey. You and the creatures assisting you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls when entering combat with your prey. These benefits lasts until you designate a new prey or your prey dies, whichever comes first. An individual creature assisting you loses this benefit if they’re out of your presence for too long to benefit from your instructions. This is usually 1 hour, but is determined by the GM.
feats.requirements: You have designated prey with {@action Hunt Prey|PC1}.

feats.name: Poultice Preparation
entries: When you create an {@trait Elixir|PC1|elixir} as an herbal item, you can prepare it as a poultice instead. A poultice gains the oil trait (but remains {@trait Alchemical|PC1|alchemical}, not {@trait Magical|PC1|magical}) and loses the elixir trait. You can apply a poultice by Interacting with one hand. When you apply a poultice, in addition to the item’s normal effects, the recipient can attempt an immediate flat check to recover from a single source of persistent acid, bleed, or fire damage, with the DC reduction from appropriate assistance.

feats.name: Precious Ammunition
entries: You have learned to mimic the power that lies between magic and material. You enchant a piece of ammunition on your person with the magical essence of a precious material, allowing you to leverage certain creatures' weaknesses. Choose cold iron or silver; if you shoot the arrow or bolt before the end of your turn, it counts as that material. At 14th level, add adamantine to the list of materials you can choose from.

feats.name: Precise Finisher
entries: Even when your foe avoids your {@action Confident Finisher|PC2}, you can still hit a vital spot. On a failure with Confident Finisher, you apply your full precise strike damage instead of half.

feats.name: Predator's Growl
entries: You give a throaty growl to attempt to {@action Demoralize|PC1} a creature you just found. You don't take the –4 penalty for not sharing a language with the creature.
feats.trigger: You successfully {@action Seek|PC1} a {@condition Hidden|PC1|hidden} or {@condition Undetected|PC1|undetected} creature.

feats.name: Predator's Pounce
entries: You close the distance to your prey in a blur, pouncing on the creature before it can react. You Stride up to your Speed and make a Strike at the end of your movement.
feats.requirements: You are unarmored or wearing light armor.

feats.name: Predictive Purchase
entries: You have just the thing for the situation. You gain the {@feat Prescient Planner|PC1} and {@feat Prescient Consumable|PC1} feats. When using Prescient Planner, you can pull out the item as a 2-action activity to remove your backpack (or a similar container) and draw the item, rather than taking 1 minute.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Prevailing Position
entries: Your flexibility with stances lets you sacrifice their benefits to better protect yourself. You leave the stance you were in, gaining a +4 circumstance bonus to the triggering saving throw or to your AC against the triggering attack.
feats.trigger: You are targeted by an attack or attempt a Reflex saving throw against a damaging effect, and you are in a {@trait Stance|PC1|stance}.

feats.name: Pride Hunter
entries: You avoid the attention of creatures focused on your allies. You can use lesser cover from your allies to {@action Hide|PC1}.

feats.name: Pride in Arms
entries: With a shout of triumph, you grant inspiration to an ally fight on. The triggering ally gains temporary Hit Points equal to their Constitution modifier until the end of their next turn.
feats.trigger: An ally within 30 feet brings an enemy to 0 Hit Points.

feats.name: Primal Dragonblood
entries: A dragon with a deep connection to the natural world, such as an adamantine dragon or a horned dragon, resides somewhere on your family tree. You tend to trust your instincts and might take on the role of a protector of the wilderness. You gain the trained proficiency rank in {@skill Nature|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in Nature (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You can use Nature to {@action Sense Direction|PC1} and {@action Subsist|PC1} in the wilds. If you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose a primal dragon.

feats.name: Primal Evolution
entries: You can call upon the creatures of the wild for aid. You gain an additional spell slot of your highest rank, which you can use only to cast {@spell Summon Animal|PC1|summon animal} or {@spell Summon Plant or Fungus|PC1|summon plant or fungus}. You can cast either of these spells using that spell slot, even if they aren't in your spell repertoire.

feats.name: Primal Rampage
entries: You gain {@spell Unfettered Movement|PC1|unfettered movement} and {@spell Mountain Resilience|PC1|mountain resilience} as 4th-rank primal innate spells that you can cast once per day. As a 3-action activity, you can Cast a Spell twice to cast both of these innate spells, as long as they are both still available for the day.

feats.name: Prodigious Climber
entries: Your natural climbing ability and technique has made you a potent climber. You gain a climb Speed of 10 feet.
special: If you have the stickytoe tripkee heritage, you instead gain a climb Speed of 20 feet.

feats.name: Projectile Snatching
entries: You pluck missiles from the air and hurl them back at their source. When you successfully deflect an attack with Deflect Projectile, as part of that same reaction, you can then immediately make a ranged Strike against the attacker using the projectile you deflected. This is a {@trait Thrown|PC1|thrown} weapon with the same range increment and effect on a hit as the triggering attack.

feats.name: Propelling Sorcery
entries: The force of your magic can be used to propel yourself or another. You know the following blood magic effect.

{@b Blood Magic—Propelling Sorcery} You channel your magic outward into a rush of movement. Either you {@action Step|PC1} as a free action or {@trait Move|PC1|move} the target 5 feet in a direction of your choice.

feats.name: Qi Center
entries: You center yourself with the universe and draw upon its vast power. You cast a single action qi spell with the {@trait Stance|PC1|stance} trait, without spending a Focus Point.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Master of Many Styles|PC2}; Qi Spells

feats.name: Qi Spells
entries: You have cultivated your qi to produce magical effects. You gain {@spell Inner Upheaval|PC2|inner upheaval}, {@spell Qi Rush|PC2|qi rush}, or another 1st-rank monk qi spell you have access to.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

special: You can select this feat more than once, choosing a different spell each time.

feats.name: Quaking Stomp
entries: You stomp the ground with such force that it creates a minor earthquake, with the effects of the {@spell Earthquake|PC1|earthquake} spell.

feats.name: Quick Bomber
entries: You keep your bombs and bomb-related reagents in easy-to-reach pouches from which you draw without thinking. You {@action Interact|PC1} to draw a bomb, draw a versatile vial, or use {@action Quick Alchemy|PC2} to create a bomb, then {@action Strike|PC1} with the bomb. If you have the ability to create more than one bomb at a time with Quick Alchemy (such as from the double brew class feature), you can Strike with only one of the bombs you create with this action.

feats.name: Quick Change
entries: You can shift between your identities with ease. Instead of spending 1 minute to change your identity, you can now do so as a 3-action activity. If you are legendary in {@skill Deception|PC1}, you can perform this change as a single action.

feats.name: Quick Fix
entries: You can attach a talisman using only a bit of glue and some string. You gain the {@feat Rapid Affixture|PC2} skill feat, even if you don't meet the prerequisites. When you use it, you can affix or remove up to four talismans in 1 minute instead of just one.
You gain the ability to Affix a Talisman as a 3-action activity from that feat at 12th level, regardless of your {@skill Crafting|PC1} proficiency.

feats.name: Quick Mount
entries: You and your mount can spring into action at a moment’s notice. You {@action Mount|PC1} the creature and {@action Command an Animal|PC1} to issue it an order of your choice.
feats.requirements: You are adjacent to a creature that is at least one size larger than you and is willing to be your mount.

feats.name: Quick Shield Block
entries: You can bring your shield into place with hardly a thought. At the start of each of your turns, you gain an additional reaction that you can use only to Shield Block.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.prerequisites: {@feat Shield Block|PC1} * This archetype offers Quick Shield Block at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Quick Shot
entries: You draw your bow and attack with the same action. You Interact to draw a weapon from the bow or crossbow weapon group that is loaded or has {@rule Reload|PC1|reload 0}, then Strike with that weapon.

feats.name: Quick Stow
entries: You Interact to store one item you're holding in your cheek pouches (provided it fits).

feats.name: Quickened Casting
entries: If your next action is to cast a {@trait Cantrip|PC1|cantrip} or a spell that is at least 2 ranks lower than the highest-rank spell slot you have, reduce the number of actions to cast it by 1 (minimum 1 action).

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.frequency: once per day * This archetype offers Quickened Casting at a different level than displayed here.
special: This feat can only be used on a cantrip or spell that is at least 2 ranks lower than the highest-rank spell slot from the class or archetype matching the one you gained this feat from.

feats.name: Quietus Strikes
entries: Your connection to the Boneyard empowers you to bring death to all forms of life and unlife, exploiting their weaknesses. All your weapon and unarmed Strikes are {@trait Magical|PC1|magical} and deal 1 additional void damage to living creatures and 1 additional vitality damage to {@trait Undead|PC1|undead}. The extra damage increases to 2 if the Strike has a {@i +3 potency rune}.

feats.name: Rabid Sprint
entries: You run on all fours as fast as you can. Stride three times.
feats.requirements: You have both your hands free.

feats.name: Radiant Armament
entries: Your blessed armament radiates power, further enhancing your chosen weapon. When you choose the weapon for your blessed armament during your daily preparations, add the astral and brilliant property runes to the list of effects you can choose from. If you're {@trait Holy|PC1|holy}, also add the holy rune, and if you're {@trait Unholy|PC1|unholy}, also add the unholy rune.

In addition, you can change the rune you've selected for the day to a different rune from your list as a 10-minute activity that has the {@trait Concentrate|PC1|concentrate}, {@trait Divine|PC1|divine}, and {@trait Exploration|PC1|exploration} traits. Changing the rune doesn't restore abilities that can be used only a limited number of times, such as Holy Healing for the {@i holy} rune.

feats.name: Raging Athlete
entries: Physical obstacles can't hold back your fury. While you are raging, you gain a climb Speed and swim Speed equal to your land Speed, and the DC of {@action High Jump|PC1|High Jumps} and {@action Long Jump|PC1|Long Jumps} decreases by 10, and you increase your distance on a successful Long Jump by 10 feet. Your distance for a vertical {@action Leap|PC1} increases to 5 feet vertically, and your distance for a horizontal Leap increases to 15 feet if your Speed is at least 15 feet, and to 20 feet if your Speed is at least 30 feet.

feats.name: Raging Intimidation
entries: Your fury fills your foes with fear. While you are raging, your {@action Demoralize|PC1} and {@feat Scare to Death|PC1} actions (from the Intimidation skill and an Intimidation skill feat, respectively) gain the {@trait Rage|PC2|rage} trait, allowing you to use them while raging. As soon as you meet the prerequisites for the skill feats {@feat Intimidating Glare|PC1} and Scare to Death, you gain these feats.

feats.name: Raging Thrower
entries: {@trait Thrown|PC1} weapons become especially deadly in your fury. You apply the additional damage from {@action Rage|PC2} to your thrown weapon attacks. If you have the {@feat Brutal Critical|PC2} feat or the devastator class feature, apply their benefits to thrown weapon attacks.

feats.name: Rallying Charge
entries: Your fearless charge into battle reinvigorates your allies to carry on the fight. You {@action Stride|PC1} up to your Speed and make a melee {@action Strike|PC1}. If your Strike hits and damages an enemy, each ally within 60 feet who saw you hit gains {@rule Temporary Hit Points|PC1|temporary Hit Points} equal to your Charisma modifier. These temporary Hit Points last until the start of your next turn.

feats.name: Rallying Cry
entries: You call out to your allies and push them to give their all in combat. All allies in a 30-foot emanation that can hear you gain a number of temporary Hit Points equal to your level. In addition, these allies become {@condition Quickened|PC1|quickened} for 1 minute but can use the extra action only to Step, Stride, or Strike.

feats.name: Rapid Affixture
entries: You take only 1 minute to Affix a Talisman. If you're legendary in Crafting, you can Affix a Talisman as a 3-action activity.

feats.name: Rat Familiar
entries: You have a pet rat that has become magically bonded to you. You gain a familiar, and this familiar must be a rat. It still gets the benefits of familiar abilities, but its base form remains a rat.

feats.name: Rat Form
entries: You can transform into an innocuous-looking rat. You gain the effects of a 1st-rank {@spell Pest Form|PC1|pest form} spell, but you must assume the battle form of a Tiny rat.

feats.name: Rat Magic
entries: There always seems to be a little rat around to carry messages for you. You can cast {@spell Animal Messenger|PC1|animal messenger} once per day as a primal innate spell. When you do, the animal that responds is always a rat. If there are no rats within range, the spell is lost.

feats.name: Ratfolk Lore
entries: Years of experience among ratfolk communities have made you nimble, and you've learned to run and hide when enemies threaten. You gain the trained proficiency rank in {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} and {@skill Stealth|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
You also gain the {@feat Additional Lore|PC1} general feat for Ratfolk Lore.

feats.name: Ratfolk Roll
entries: You roll up into a ball and move up to four times your Speed in a straight line down an incline. If you reach the bottom of the incline or hit an obstacle during this first turn of movement, you stop rolling safely. Otherwise, you automatically keep rolling at this Speed during subsequent turns until you hit the bottom of the incline or an obstacle ends this movement (which can happen in the middle of your turn). You're {@condition Slowed|PC1|slowed 2} each turn after the first that you keep rolling, and if you hit an obstacle on a turn after the first, you and the obstacle both take 4d6 bludgeoning damage and you stop rolling.

feats.name: Ratspeak
entries: You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the {@skill Diplomacy|PC1} skill with rodents, including beavers, mice, porcupines, rats, and squirrels, but not with other mammals, such as dogs or bats. The GM determines which {@trait Animal|PC1|animals} count as rodents.

feats.name: Reach Spell
entries: You can extend your spells’ range. If the next action you use is to {@action Cast a Spell|PC1} that has a range, increase that spell’s range by 30 feet. As is standard for increasing spell ranges, if the spell normally has a range of touch, you extend its range to 30 feet.

feats.name: Reactive Strike
entries: You lash out at a foe that leaves an opening. Make a melee Strike against the triggering creature. If your attack is a critical hit and the trigger was a manipulate action, you disrupt that action. This Strike doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Strike.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.trigger: A creature within your reach uses a {@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate} action or a {@trait Move|PC1|move} action, makes a ranged attack, or leaves a square during a move action it’s using. * This archetype offers Reactive Strike at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Read Disaster
entries: You spend 10 minutes and open yourself to the {@trait Divine|PC1|divine} mysteries of the world, peering into the most sinister portents of the future. You gain the effects of {@spell Augury|PC1|augury}, except you learn only about the dangers ahead; any results of “good” are instead “nothing,” and results of “mixed” are instead “bad.” If you are legendary in {@skill Religion|PC1}, you take only 1 minute to {@feat Read Disaster|PC2}.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Read Shibboleths
entries: All communication is filled with slight tells and signals. If you interact with someone for at least 10 minutes, their regional words, pronunciation changes, and nonverbal cues provide you with a minor fact about their social environment, such as their hometown or certain groups they might belong to. If a target of this ability is being deceptive about their social environment, such as a commoner pretending to be a noble, they secretly attempt a {@skill Deception|PC1}, {@skill Society|PC1}, or appropriate {@skill Lore|PC1} check against your Society DC, providing you a false minor fact consistent with their assumed identity on a success.

Once you’ve gleaned one or more true minor facts about a person, you can then incorporate these mannerisms into your speech to present yourself in a way that they find familiar. This grants you a +1 circumstance bonus to your {@skill Diplomacy|PC1} and Deception checks with them.

feats.name: Reason Rapidly
entries: Your mind works through clues at an unbelievable speed. You instantly use up to five {@action Recall Knowledge|PC1} actions. If you have any special abilities or free actions that would normally be triggered when you Recall Knowledge, you can't use them for these actions.

feats.name: Recognize Ambush
entries: Your combat training has honed you to be ready for an attack at all times. You Interact to draw a weapon.
feats.trigger: You roll initiative.

feats.name: Reconstruct The Scene
entries: You spend 1 minute surveying a small location (such as a single room) to get an impression of events that occurred there in the last day. This involves moving about the area and studying footprints, spilled drinks or blood, and so forth. You get an indistinct mental impression of significant events that happened there. This gives you clues and details of the past, including the overall events and their time frame, but it’s not a perfect record. This also isn’t enough to identify who was involved in these events if you weren’t already aware the person was there. As determined by the GM, you also pick out various seemingly small details that could serve as important clues, like a memorable weapon someone used for a murder or the type of cloak someone wore when passing through.

feats.name: Reflect Harm
entries: You can wrap your magic around you like a cloak that causes those who dare to target you with spells to suffer a similar fate. You know the following blood magic effect.

{@b Blood Magic—Reflect Harm} Your blood ensures that those who harm you with magic are harmed in return. The first time you take damage from a spell before the beginning of your next turn, attempt spell {@trait Attack|PC1|attack} roll against the creature who cast the triggering spell. On a hit, the creature takes the same amount and type of damage that you just took. If you critically hit, the creature takes twice the damage.

feats.name: Reflexive Riposte
entries: You can riposte almost without a thought. At the start of each of your turns when you regain your actions, you gain an additional reaction that can be used only to perform an {@action Opportune Riposte|PC2}.

feats.name: Reflexive Stance
entries: You enter a stance without a thought. Use an action that has the {@trait Stance|PC1|stance} trait.
feats.trigger: You roll initiative.

feats.name: Regurgitate Mutagen
entries: You redirect a mutagen within your body to spit a stream of stomach acid at a foe. A creature within 30 feet takes 1d6 acid damage for every 2 levels you have, with a basic Reflex save against your class DC. On a failure, the creature is also {@condition Sickened|PC1|sickened 1} (or sickened 2 on a critical failure). The mutagen's duration immediately ends.
feats.requirements: You are under the effects of a mutagen.

feats.name: Rejuvenating Touch
entries: Your healing energies linger after you cast, providing continual benefits. An ally that recovers Hit Points from your {@i lay on hands} gains 10 temporary Hit Points immediately and at the start of their turn during each of the next 10 rounds. These temporary HP last until the start of the creature's next turn. This effect ends if the ally is knocked {@condition Unconscious|PC1|unconscious}.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.prerequisites: {@spell Lay on Hands|PC2|lay on hands} * This archetype offers Rejuvenating Touch at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Reliable Luck
entries: You survive danger with surprising regularity. You can use Cat's Luck once per hour, rather than once per day.

feats.name: Remorseless Lash
entries: You're skilled at beating an enemy when their morale is already breaking. When you succeed at a melee weapon Strike against a {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened} enemy, that enemy can't reduce their frightened condition below 1 until the beginning of your next turn.

feats.name: Remote Trigger
entries: You've learned how to trigger {@trait Snare|PC2|snares} from afar, creating ranged hazards to assail your opponents and allowing you to disarm enemies' snares harmlessly. You can {@action Strike|PC1} a snare to trigger it prematurely. If you crafted the snare, you automatically hit. If someone else crafted it, attempt a ranged Strike against the {@skill Crafting|PC1} DC, triggering the snare only if you hit.

feats.name: Renewed Vigor
entries: Through the haze of battle, you quickly recover your raging vigor. You gain temporary Hit Points equal to half your level plus your Constitution modifier. If you made an {@trait Attack|PC1|attack} action this turn, increase the number of temporary Hit Points to your level plus your Constitution modifier. These temporary Hit Points last until the end of your rage.

feats.name: Reptile Speaker
entries: You hear the sounds of reptiles as language. You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the {@skill Diplomacy|PC1} skill with {@trait Animal|PC1|animals} that are reptiles (the GM determines which animals count as reptiles).

feats.name: Resist Ruin
entries: Your duskwalker heritage allows you to extend protection against void energy. You gain resistance 5 to void, and once per day, you can cast {@spell False Vitality|PC1|false vitality} as a 5th-rank divine innate spell.

feats.name: Resounding Blow
entries: You strike your enemy in the head with such force that its ears ring. Make a melee Strike. If the Strike hits and deals damage, the target is {@condition Deafened|PC1|deafened} until the start of your next turn (or for 1 minute on a critical hit).
feats.requirements: You are wielding a melee weapon that deals bludgeoning damage.
