entries: You swap places with the target enemy and the enemy becomes the target of the triggering attack.

items.name: Success
entries: As critical success, except the target has lesser cover against the triggering attack, and you lose your panache.

items.name: Failure
entries: You lose your panache.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You become {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} against the triggering attack, and you lose your panache.

feats.requirements: You are adjacent to an enemy and have panache.
feats.trigger: You are targeted by a ranged attack.

feats.name: Symphony of Blood
entries: You call forth the blood of your foes to grant you vigor. You can cast {@spell Vampiric Exsanguination|PC1|vampiric exsanguination} as a 7th-rank divine innate spell once per day

feats.name: Tactical Cadence
entries: Your remarkable breath control and concise instructions allow you to coordinate your allies more effectively, even in desperate situations. When you grant allies the {@condition Quickened|PC1|quickened} condition using {@feat Cadence Call|PC2}, they can use the extra action to either {@action Stride|PC1} or {@action Strike|PC1}, and they aren’t {@condition Slowed|PC1|slowed} 1 on their following turn if they use the extra action.

feats.name: Takedown Expert
entries: You've mastered combat practices that let you get up close and bring down perpetrators alive. You can use your Intelligence modifier on attack rolls for an attack stratagem if you're using a weapon of the club group in one hand (like a {@equipment Club|PC1|club} or {@equipment Staff|PC1|staff}), in addition to the usual weapons, and those Strikes qualify for your strategic strike. Additionally, you can make any of your Strikes {@trait Nonlethal|PC1|nonlethal} without taking the normal –2 penalty.

feats.name: Talisman Dabbler Dedication
entries: You are trained in the use of talismans and similar magical paraphernalia. This training might have occurred in a formal classroom or been an accumulation of folk magic picked up over time. You can craft talismans and know the formulas for all common talismans of your level or lower. You remember talisman formulas and don't need a formula book for them.

Additionally, you carry a vast collection of magical baubles you can turn into temporary talismans. Each day during your daily preparations, you can make two talismans with an item level no higher than half your level. You must know each talisman's formula. A talisman created this way is a temporary item and loses its magic the next time you make your daily preparations if you haven't already used it. Any saving throw DC required by a temporary talisman you create uses the highest of your class DC, spell DC, or the talisman's DC.
Finally, when you Affix a Talisman, you can (in any combination) affix or remove up to four talismans in the 10-minute span.

feats.name: Talismanic Sage
entries: Normally, affixing more than one talisman to an item causes the talismans to be suppressed, but when you Affix a Talisman, you can specially treat one item you're working on, allowing it to have two active talismans at once. This special treatment ends if you use Affix a Talisman to treat a new item for this ability.

feats.name: Tangle of Battle
entries: Your vicious strike pulls your foe closer, giving you the opportunity to grab them. Attempt to {@action Grapple|PC1} the triggering enemy.
feats.trigger: You critically hit an adjacent enemy.

feats.name: Tangled Forest Rake
entries: You reposition foes with raking attacks. Make a lashing branch Strike. If you hit and deal damage, you can {@action Reposition|PC1} the target up to 10 feet. You can move the target through your space during this movement.
feats.requirements: You are in Tangled Forest Stance.

feats.name: Tangled Forest Stance
entries: You extend your arms like gnarled branches to interfere with your foes' movements. You can make lashing branch unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 slashing damage; are in the brawling group; and have the {@trait Agile|PC1|agile}, {@trait Finesse|PC1|finesse}, {@trait Nonlethal|PC1|nonlethal}, and {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed} traits.

While you're in Tangled Forest Stance and can act, every enemy in your reach that tries to move away from you must succeed at a Reflex save, {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} check, or {@skill Athletics|PC1} check against your class DC or be {@condition Immobilized|PC1|immobilized} for that action. If you prefer, you can allow the enemy to move.
feats.requirements: You are unarmored.

feats.name: Tap Into Blood
entries: The power in your blood allows you to perform minor feats of magic. You can perform one of the following actions depending on the tradition of your bloodline.

items: {@b {@trait Arcane|PC1}} Your mind temporarily opens to the secrets of the world. Attempt to {@action Recall Knowledge|PC1}; you can use {@skill Arcana|PC1}instead of the skill normally needed for that subject. If you critically fail at this check, you get a failure instead.

{@trait Divine|PC1} Whatever divine provenance is in your lineage guides you to instinctively move yourself or others out of harm's way. You {@action Step|PC1}, or you {@action Reposition|PC1} a target within your reach using {@skill Religion|PC1} for the check.
{@trait Occult|PC1} Strange mists or swirling colors hide your movement. You {@action Step|PC1} up to 10 feet.
{@trait Primal|PC1} The immense power of nature echoes in your voice. You can attempt a {@skill Nature|PC1} check to {@action Demoralize|PC1} a target.

feats.requirements: You are benefiting from a blood magic effect

feats.name: Target of Opportunity
entries: You capitalize on your ally’s attack and use the opportunity to secure a blow of your own, adding to the oncoming barrage. Make a ranged {@action Strike|PC1} with a –2 penalty against the opponent targeted by the triggering attack. This Strike doesn’t count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn’t apply to this Strike. If this Strike is successful, combine the damage from the attack with the damage from your ally’s attack for the purpose of {@rule Resistance|PC1|resistances} and weaknesses.
feats.requirements: You have a ranged or thrown weapon in hand.
feats.trigger: An ally succeeds at a ranged {@action Strike|PC1} against an opponent in your weapon’s first range increment.

feats.name: Targeting Finisher
entries: Your attack harms and hinders your foe. Choose a particular part of your foe from the list below and Strike. If you hit and damage the target, apply the effect corresponding to the chosen part. This hindrance lasts until the end of your next turn. On a critical hit, you also apply a lesser effect lasting for 1 minute.

items: {@b Arm} (or another limb used for attacks, such as a tentacle) The target is {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled 2}. On a critical hit, it is also enfeebled 1 for 1 minute.
{@b Head} The target is {@condition Stupefied|PC1|stupefied 2}. On a critical hit, it is also stupefied 1 for 1 minute.
{@b Legs} The target takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speeds. On a critical hit, it also takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 minute.

feats.name: Ten Lives
entries: When your character would die, you can attempt a DC 17 flat check. On a success, you're instead reduced to 0 HP and a {@condition Dying|PC1|dying} value 1 less than what would normally kill you (typically dying 3). This doesn't change the result for any other creature affected.

feats.name: Tenacious Net
entries: Escaping your nets is no simple task. The {@skill Athletics|PC1} DC to {@action Force Open|PC1} or {@action Escape|PC1} your nets increases from 16 to 18. After a creature you {@condition Grabbed|PC1|grabbed} with a net Escapes or Forces Open the net, stray strands of the net cling to the creature, causing them to remain {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} until the beginning of their next turn.

feats.name: Tenacious Toxins
entries: Your victims tend to expire long before your poisons, since the latter have been specifically formulated to last longer. The maximum duration of any poison you create increases by an amount equal to the poison's stage 1 interval, to a maximum of twice the poison's maximum duration.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Tengu Feather Fan
entries: You've learned to bind some of your feathers together into a fan to focus your ancestral magic. You gain a {@i tengu feather fan}: a magic item of light Bulk with a level equal to your level and the {@trait Primal|PC1|primal} trait. You (and only you) can cast tengu magic with the Wave Fan activation. If your fan is lost or destroyed, you can create a replacement during your daily preparations; if you do so, your previous fan falls apart into mundane feathers. Your {@i tengu feather fan} contains a 1st-rank {@spell Gust of Wind|PC1|gust of wind} spell. Further feats might add more spells and grant you additional activations of your tengu feather fan, but you can never have more than three activations per day, no matter how many such feats you have.

{@b Activate—Wave Fan} {@as 1} ({@trait Manipulate|PC1|manipulate}) {@b Frequency} once per day; {@b Effect} You cast your choice of one spell contained in your tengu feather fan. You can instead cast a cantrip you've gained from a heritage or an ancestry feat; this doesn't use up one of the fan's daily activations.
This activation takes the spell's normal number of actions. The spell's DC is your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.

feats.name: Tengu Lore
entries: You learned skills for surviving in the place where your people were dispersed. You gain the trained proficiency rank in {@skill Society|PC1} and {@skill Survival|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
You also gain the {@feat Additional Lore|PC1} general feat for Tengu Lore.

feats.name: Tengu Weapon Familiarity
entries: You gain access to all uncommon weapons with the {@trait Tengu|PC2|tengu} trait plus the {@equipment Katana|PC1|katana}, khakkara, {@equipment Temple Sword|PC1|temple sword}, and {@equipment Wakizashi|PC1|wakizashi}. You have familiarity with these weapons—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.

During your daily preparations, you can practice with a weapon from the sword group that's in your possession. You gain familiarity with that weapon as well. This lasts until you practice with a different sword in the same way.
At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.

feats.name: Terraforming Trickery
entries: You know how to channel the transformative aspects of your blood magic to alter your surroundings. You know the following blood magic effect.

{@b Blood Magic—Terraforming Trickery} Either each space adjacent to you becomes difficult terrain, or each space adjacent to you is no longer difficult terrain. This doesn't have any effect on greater difficult terrain and doesn't remove the damaging effects of hazardous terrain.

feats.name: Terrain Advantage
entries: Non-{@trait Lizardfolk|PC2|lizardfolk} creatures in {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain} are {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} to you. If you have a swim Speed, non-lizardfolk creatures that are in water and lack a swim Speed are also off-guard to you.

feats.name: Terrain Scout
entries: You have mastered movement in many different environments. You gain the {@feat Terrain Stalker|PC1} skill feat twice, choosing a different terrain each time. If you {@action Avoid Notice|PC1} while exploring and any allies use {@action Follow the Expert|PC1} to follow you as you do so, you can choose one of those allies to gain the benefit of any one Terrain Stalker feat you have.

feats.name: Terrifying Croak
entries: You release a haunting croak that reminds those around you of their fears. Attempt an Intimidation check to {@action Demoralize|PC1} a creature within 30 feet; you do not take a penalty to this check for not speaking a language. If the check is successful, the target cannot reduce their {@condition Frightened|PC1|frightened} condition below 1 for 1 round.

feats.name: Terrifying Howl
entries: You unleash a terrifying howl. Attempt {@skill Intimidation|PC1} checks to {@action Demoralize|PC1} each enemy within 30 feet: you don't take a penalty if the creature doesn't understand your language. Regardless of the results of your checks, each target is then temporarily immune to Terrifying Howl for 1 minute.

feats.name: Terrifying Resistance
entries: The spells of those you have Demoralized are less effective on you. If you succeed in Demoralizing a creature, for the next 24 hours you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against that creature's spells.

feats.name: That's Odd
entries: When you enter a new location, such as a room or corridor, you immediately notice one thing out of the ordinary. The GM determines what it is, or whether there's nothing reasonable to pick up, skipping obvious clues that can be easily noticed without a check or specifically looking for them. You learn only that an area or object is suspicious, but not why it's suspicious. For example, if you entered a study with a large bloodstain on the ground, the bloodstain is so obviously suspicious it's evident to you already, so the GM might note that there's something suspicious about the desk drawer instead. You would then need to investigate the drawer further to find out what specifically is out of the ordinary. If you wish, you can Pursue a Lead concerning this detail even if you have Pursed a Lead less than 10 minutes ago.

That's Odd doesn't reveal whether creatures are suspicious. You don't typically get any benefit when you leave and come back to a place, though if a major change has happened there and time has passed, the GM might determine that you do.

feats.name: The Bigger They Are
entries: With reckless speed, you dash, jump and swing around a creature to find a more vulnerable spot. Attempt to {@action Tumble Through|PC1} a creature at least one size category larger than you, using the following effects.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: You move through the enemy's space, treating the squares in its space as {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain} (every 5 feet costs 10 feet of movement). If you don't have enough Speed to move all the way through its space, you get the same effect as a failure. If you successfully pass through the target's square, the target gains weakness to your precision damage equal to half your level, which lasts until the end of your turn.

items.name: Success
entries: As success, but the weakness applies only against the next attack you make against the target.

items.name: Failure
entries: Your movement ends, and you trigger reactions as if you had moved out of the square you started in.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: As failure, and you fall {@condition Prone|PC1|prone}.

feats.name: The Dead Walk
entries: You beseech warrior spirits to come forth and aid you. Two ghostly warriors manifest within a 30-foot emanation of you and each attempt a {@action Strike|PC1} against an adjacent enemy, using your spell attack modifier. The warriors' Strikes each deal 4d6 {@trait Spirit|PC1|spirit} damage and the warriors can flank with one another and with you and your allies. If you are {@trait Cursebound|PC2|cursebound} 2 when you use The Dead Walk, you instead summon three warriors, and if you are cursebound 3, you instead summon four warriors. The warriors disappear at the start of your next turn.

feats.name: Thorough Research
entries: You have comprehensive knowledge in your fields of interest. When you succeed at a {@action Recall Knowledge|PC1} check, you gain additional information or context. When you critically succeed at a check to Recall Knowledge, you get additional information or context or can ask an additional follow-up question (the GM chooses which).

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Thorough Search
entries: You take your time searching to ensure you find everything. When Searching, you can take twice as long to search. Normally this means you Search at up to one quarter of your Speed, to a maximum of 150 feet per minute to check everything, or 75 feet per minute to check everything before you walk into an area. If you do and the GM rolls your secret check to Seek to notice something, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to that Perception check and if you succeed, you get a critical success instead.

feats.name: Thousand Visions
entries: You open your senses to numerous visions of the immediate future. The visions grant you subtle details of your immediate surroundings within 30 feet. Within this range, you don't need to succeed at a flat check to target a concealed creature, you're not {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} to creatures that are {@condition Hidden|PC1|hidden} from you (unless you're off-guard to them for reasons other than the hidden condition), and you need only a successful DC 5 flat check to target a hidden creature. Beyond 30 feet, the visions become overwhelmed with too many possible futures, making all of your senses imprecise beyond this range. The visions persist for 1 minute.

feats.name: Thrash
entries: You thrash your foe around. An enemy you have {@condition Grabbed|PC1|grabbed} or {@condition Restrained|PC1|restrained} takes bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier plus your weapon specialization damage plus your {@action Rage|PC2} damage, with a basic Fortitude save against your class DC.
feats.requirements: You have an enemy {@condition Grabbed|PC1|grabbed} or {@condition Restrained|PC1|restrained}.

feats.name: Thunder God's Fan
entries: Your fan unleashes the fury of the storm. You can use the Wave Fan activation one additional time per day. Add a 5th-rank {@spell Lightning Bolt|PC1|lightning bolt} spell to the spells contained within your fan.

feats.name: Tiger Slash
entries: You make a fierce swipe with both hands. Make a tiger claw Strike. It deals two extra weapon damage dice (three extra dice if you're 14th level or higher), and you can {@creatureability Push|RoE|push} the target 5 feet away as if you had successfully Shoved them. If the attack is a critical success and deals damage, add your Strength modifier to the {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent bleed damage} from your tiger claw.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.requirements: You are in Tiger Stance. * This archetype offers Tiger Slash at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Tiger Stance
entries: You enter the stance of a tiger and can make tiger claw attacks. These deal 1d8 slashing damage; are in the brawling group; and have the {@trait Agile|PC1|agile}, {@trait Finesse|PC1|finesse}, {@trait Nonlethal|PC1|nonlethal}, and {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed} traits. On a critical success with your tiger claws, if you deal damage, the target takes 1d4 {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent bleed damage}.
As long as your Speed is at least 20 feet while in Tiger Stance, you can Step 10 feet.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.requirements: You are unarmored.  * This archetype offers Tiger Stance at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Tinkering Fingers
entries: You're trained in {@skill Crafting|PC1}. If you are trained in Crafting from another source (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You can {@action Repair|PC1} an item without using a {@equipment Repair Toolkit|PC1|repair toolkit} without taking the –2 circumstance penalty, improvising tools from whatever you have at hand. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Crafting checks to Repair an item when you have a repair toolkit.

feats.name: Titan's Stature
entries: You grow to even greater size. When using Giant's Stature, you can instead become Huge (increasing your {@trait Reach|PC1|reach} by 10 feet if you were Medium or smaller).

feats.name: To Battle!
entries: With a resounding cry, you rally your ally to take the offensive. Choose one ally in your marshal’s aura who has a reaction available. If you spend 1 action, that ally can use their reaction to immediately {@action Stride|PC1}. If you spend 2 actions, that ally can use their reaction to immediately {@action Strike|PC1}.

feats.name: Tongue Tether
entries: Your tongue can momentarily latch on as readily as your hands. So long as you can freely open your mouth, you do not need free hands in order to {@action Disarm|PC1}, {@action Grab an Edge|PC1}, {@action Reposition|PC1}, or {@action Trip|PC1}. If you have the {@feat Long Tongue|PC2} feat, you can Disarm, Grab an Edge, Reposition, and Trip with your tongue at a distance that is 5 feet beyond your normal reach.

feats.name: Tools of the Trade
entries: You’re well-versed in weapons that allow you to bring bounties back in one piece, or at least alive. You have familiarity with the bola, sap, and whip; for the purposes of proficiency, you treat these weapons as simple weapons. You deal an additional 1d4 precision damage with these weapons when using them to make nonlethal Strikes against your prey while they’re off-guard to you. In addition, you take no penalty when making a nonlethal attack with a weapon without the nonlethal trait.

feats.name: Topple Foe
entries: You take advantage of the opening created by your ally to tip your foe off their feet. Attempt an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check to {@action Trip|PC1} the target of the triggering attack.
feats.trigger: An ally succeeds at a melee {@action Strike|PC1} against an enemy you are both adjacent to.

feats.name: Traditional Resistances
entries: Due to your blood, you have some resistance to certain types of magic. You gain a +1 status bonus to AC and saves against spells and other magical effects from the same tradition as your lineage. This bonus increases to +2 against {@trait Sleep|PC1|sleep} and paralysis effects.
feats.prerequisites: {@feat Arcane Dragonblood|PC2}, {@feat Divine Dragonblood|PC2}, {@feat Occult Dragonblood|PC2} or {@feat Primal Dragonblood|PC2}

feats.name: Trampling Charge
entries: You urge your mount to charge into the fray, trampling all enemies who stand in your path. You command your mount to {@action Stride|PC1} up to double its Speed (or to {@action Burrow|PC1}, {@action Climb|PC1}, {@action Fly|PC1}, or {@action Swim|PC1}, if it has the corresponding movement type), moving through the spaces of any foes in your path up to one size smaller than your mount. Your mount deals the damage of one of its melee {@action Strike|PC1|Strikes} to each creature whose space you move through, with a basic Reflex save against your mount’s {@skill Athletics|PC1} DC. On a critical failure, the creature also becomes off-guard until the end of your next turn. Roll the damage only once. You can damage a given creature only once during this movement.
feats.requirements: You are riding a mount that has a melee {@action Strike|PC1} using its legs (claw, talons, hoof, etc.). * This archetype offers Trampling Charge at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Trap Finder
entries: You have an intuitive sense that alerts you to the presence of traps. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to find traps, to AC against attacks made by traps, and to saves against traps. Even if you aren’t Searching, you get a check to find traps that normally require you to be Searching. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap.

You can disable traps that require a proficiency rank of master in Thievery. If you have master proficiency in Thievery, you can disable traps that require a proficiency rank of legendary instead, and your circumstance bonuses against traps increase to +2.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Treat Condition
entries: You treat an adjacent creature in an attempt to reduce the {@condition Clumsy|PC1|clumsy}, {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled}, or {@condition Sickened|PC1|sickened} condition. If a creature has multiple conditions from this list, choose one. Attempt a counteract check against the condition using your {@skill Medicine|PC1} modifier as your counteract modifier and the condition’s source to determine the DC. You can’t treat a condition that came from an artifact or effect above 20th level unless you have {@feat Legendary Medic|PC1}; even if you do, the counteract DC increases by 10. Treating a Condition that is continually applied under certain circumstances (for instance, the enfeebled condition a {@trait Holy|PC1|holy} character gains from carrying a weapon with the unholy rune) has no effect as long as the circumstances continue.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: Reduce the condition value by 2.

items.name: Success
entries: Reduce the condition value by 1.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: Increase the condition value by 1.

feats.requirements: You are holding healer's tools, or you are wearing them and have a hand free.

feats.name: Trial by Skyfire
entries: Your lips murmur as you portend a great disaster, one you hope you survive. A rain of blazing bolts begins to fall from the heavens in a 10-foot emanation, centered on you, that deals 2d6 fire damage to all creatures in the emanation at the end of each of your turns (basic Reflex save); you can't exclude yourself from the emanation. The skyfire persists for 1 minute; while you can't {@action Dismiss|PC1} it, you can suppress the effect for 1 round with a {@action Sustain|PC1} action. The rain of fire is suppressed if you fall {@condition Unconscious|PC1|unconscious}. If you become {@trait Cursebound|PC2|cursebound} 3 or 4 at any point during Trial by Skyfire's duration, the emanation increases to 15 feet and the damage increases to 4d6.

feats.name: Triangle Shot
entries: You string three arrows to your bow and fire them all at once. Make three ranged Strikes against a single target with the required weapon, each using your current multiple attack penalty, and you take an additional –2 penalty. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty, and you combine the attacks' damage for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses. Your {@feat Stunning Blows|PC2} benefit applies to Triangle Shot, even though it isn't a {@action Flurry of Blows|PC2}. If all three Strikes hit, the target takes 3d6 {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent bleed damage}.
feats.requirements: You are in Monastic Archer Stance and wielding a bow usable with that stance.

feats.name: Trickster Tengu
entries: You can transform yourself or the bodies of others to express your displeasure. Once per day, you can cast either {@spell Aerial Form|PC1|aerial form} or {@spell Cursed Metamorphosis|PC1|cursed metamorphosis} as a 7th-rank primal innate spell. You must take the form of a bird when casting this {@i aerial form}.

feats.name: Trickster's Ace
entries: Whether from jury-rigged magic items, deduction from the study of magical interactions, or other means, you have a contingency in your back pocket for desperate situations. When the trigger occurs, you cause the spell to come into effect. The spell targets only you, no matter how many creatures it would affect normally. If you define particularly complicated conditions, as determined by the GM, the trigger might fail. Once the contingency is triggered, the spell is expended until your next daily preparations.
feats.requirements: When you make your daily preparations, you must specify a trigger for this reaction using the same restrictions as the triggers for the {@action Ready|PC1} action. You also choose a single spell from the arcane, divine, occult, or primal list of 4th level or lower. The spell can’t have a cost, nor can its casting time be more than 10 minutes. The spell must be able to target a single creature, and you must be a valid target for it.
feats.trigger: You specify the trigger when you make your daily preparations.

feats.name: Tripkee Glide
entries: You can use your webbed feet to guide your fall. You glide slowly toward the ground, 5 feet down (10 feet if you don't have both hands free) and up to 25 feet forward through the air. As long as you spend at least 1 action gliding each round and have not yet reached the ground, you remain in the air at the end of your turn.
feats.requirements: You must have at least one hand free.

feats.name: Tripkee Lore
entries: You are well versed in tripkee culture and tactics. You gain the trained proficiency in {@skill Nature|PC1} and {@skill Stealth|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
You also gain the {@feat Additional Lore|PC1} general feat for Tripkee Lore.

feats.name: Tripkee Weapon Familiarity
entries: You gain access to all {@trait Uncommon|PC1|uncommon} weapons with the {@trait Tripkee|PC2|tripkee} trait. You have familiarity with weapons with the tripkee trait plus the {@equipment Blowgun|PC1|blowgun}, {@equipment Dart|PC1|dart}, {@equipment Hatchet|PC1|hatchet}, {@equipment Scythe|PC1|scythe}, and {@equipment Shortbow|PC1|shortbow}—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.
At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.

feats.name: True Debilitating Bomb
entries: You have discovered increasingly devastating ways for your bombs to impede your foes. When you use Debilitating Bomb, add the following to the list of effects you can choose from: {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled 2}, {@condition Stupefied|PC1|stupefied 2}, or a –15-foot status penalty to Speeds.

feats.name: True Dragon's Flight
entries: Your wings have grown more powerful, capable of keeping you aloft longer. You have a fly Speed of 20 feet at all times.

feats.name: True Perception
entries: Your perceptive abilities and ability to process sensory information are so far beyond the pale that you notice minute discrepancies in all sorts of illusions and physical transformations. You are constantly under the effects of a 6th rank truesight spell, using your Perception modifier for the counteract check.

feats.name: Tumble Behind (Swashbuckler)
entries: Your tumbling puts your foes on the back foot. When you {@action Tumble Through|PC1} successfully, the foe you Tumbled Through is {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} against the next attack you make before the end of your turn.

feats.name: Tumbling Diversion
entries: Attempt to {@action Tumble Through|PC1} an opponent's space. If you succeed or critically succeed and don't end your movement adjacent to that opponent, you can attempt to {@action Create a Diversion|PC1} to distract that opponent. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the Deception check (or a +2 circumstance bonus if you critically succeeded at the Acrobatics check to Tumble Through) to Create a Diversion. If you succeed or critically succeed to Create a Diversion, you become {@condition Hidden|PC1|hidden} to only the creature whose space you Tumbled Through.

feats.name: Tumbling Opportunist
entries: You use a burst of stamina to perform a breathtaking feat of Acrobatics as you speed through a foe's space, leaving your foe lying flat on their back. You attempt to {@action Trip|PC1} the enemy whose space you moved through. You can use {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} instead of {@skill Athletics|PC1} for this check.
feats.requirements: Your most recent action was to {@action Tumble Through|PC1} or {@feat Tumbling Strike|PC2}, and you successfully moved through an enemy’s space.

feats.name: Tumbling Strike
entries: You deftly dive through a gap left by a foe to deliver an advantageous blow. Attempt an {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} check against the Reflex DC of an enemy adjacent to you.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: You move through the enemy’s space to an unoccupied space on the other side of the enemy from your starting position. This movement doesn’t trigger reactions. You can’t move farther than your Speed, and you must end your movement adjacent to the enemy whose space you moved through. After moving, you make a melee {@action Strike|PC1} against the enemy whose space you moved through, and the enemy is {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} against that Strike.

items.name: Success
entries: As critical success, but the enemy isn’t off-guard against the Strike.

items.name: Failure
entries: You remain in your original space but can still Strike.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You neither move nor Strike.

feats.requirements: You are adjacent to an enemy.

feats.name: Tumbling Teamwork
entries: Your tumbling distracts a foe enough to create an advantage for one of your allies. When you successfully {@action Tumble Through|PC1} an enemy's space, an ally who is adjacent to that enemy can {@action Step|PC1} as a reaction, but they must remain adjacent to that enemy.

feats.name: Tumbling Theft
entries: You reach for an opponent's item as you move past a foe. If you critically succeed at your check to {@action Tumble Through|PC1} an enemy's space, you can attempt to {@action Steal|PC1} something from the enemy as a reaction. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your Thievery check to Steal as your tumbling make it difficult for your enemy to keep track of your movement. You can Steal any immediately accessible item of light or negligible Bulk on the enemy's person, such as a potion or coin purse hanging from a belt, but not anything inside a container or anything the enemy is holding. The GM has final say on what you can Steal.

feats.name: Twirling Throw
entries: Your thrown weapons seem to defy physics as they soar through the air and spin back to you after a strike. Make a {@trait Thrown|PC1|thrown} weapon Strike, ignoring the penalty for making ranged attacks within the second and third range increment. The weapon returns to your hand after the attack unless you critically failed on the attack roll.

feats.name: Ultimate Mercy
entries: Your mercy transcends the bounds of life and death. Add ultimate mercy to the types of mercy you can provide. When you use Mercy, you can target a creature that died since your last turn to return it to life. The target returns to life with 1 Hit Point and becomes {@condition Wounded|PC1|wounded 1}. You can't return the target to life if it died from {@spell Disintegrate|PC1|disintegrate} or a {@trait Death|PC1|death} effect. The creature gains the other benefits of {@i lay on hands} after it returns to life.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.prerequisites: {@feat Mercy|PC2} * This archetype offers Ultimate Mercy at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Unbalancing Finisher
entries: You attack with a flashy assault that leaves your target off balance. Make a melee Strike. If you hit and deal damage, the target is {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} until the end of your next turn.

feats.name: Unbalancing Sweep
entries: You make a great sweep with your weapon or fists about yourself, knocking creatures off their feet and away from you. Choose up to three enemies within your reach and choose whether to {@action Shove|PC1} or {@action Trip|PC1} all three of them. Whichever of the two options you choose, roll a separate {@skill Athletics|PC1} check against each enemy, performing the same action against each enemy. Each attempt counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but don't increase your penalty until you have made all the attempts.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Unbound Leaper
entries: Your jumping prowess is unmatched. You can {@action Leap|PC1} up to 30 feet in any direction without touching the ground and without requiring an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check; when doing so, you must land on a space of solid ground within 30 feet of you, or else you fall after using your next action. You can exceed your normal Speed while Leaping.
special: If you have the {@feat Fantastic Leaps|PC2} feat, the total distance you can Leap horizontally is 40 feet, and the total distance you can Leap vertically is 35 feet.

feats.name: Uncanny Agility
entries: You have near-supernatural poise that lets you move swiftly across the most unsteady surfaces. You gain the {@feat Steady Balance|PC1} skill feat. You can Step into {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain} caused by uneven ground, such as a rocky field, hilly incline, or rocking ship.

feats.name: Uncanny Bombs
entries: You lob bombs unerringly, despite obstructions or distance. When you throw an {@trait Alchemical|PC1|alchemical} item with the {@trait Bomb|PC1|bomb} trait, its range increment increases to 60 feet, you reduce any circumstance bonus to the target's AC from {@rule Cover|PC1|cover} by 1, and you automatically succeed at the flat check when targeting a {@condition Concealed|PC1|concealed} creature.

feats.name: Uncanny Cheeks
entries: You gain the {@feat Prescient Consumable|PC1} and {@feat Prescient Planner|PC1} feats, except that you always withdraw the objects from your cheek pouches. This means the object you retrieve must fit in your cheek pouches; this is generally an item of negligible Bulk unless you also have the {@feat Cheek Pouches|PC2} feat.

feats.name: Undead Slayer
entries: Your knowledge of your own not-quite-living anatomy, combined with your experience in combat, helps you take down undead foes with ease. Against {@trait Undead|PC1|undead} creatures, you gain a circumstance bonus to damage with weapon and unarmed Strikes equal to the number of weapon damage dice for the Strike. This bonus increases to double the number of weapon damage dice if your target has the {@trait Vampire|MC1|vampire} trait.

feats.name: Underground Network
entries: You're connected to groups that know what's going on in the streets, and you can get information out of them quickly. When you use Society to {@action Gather Information|PC1} in an area where you have a network (typically a settlement where you've spent at least a week or spent a day of downtime to build a network faster), you can contact a member of these groups to get information directly from them. This usually takes about an hour, and it doesn't draw as much attention as Gathering Information in public might. The check and information gained otherwise follow the normal rules for Gather Information.

In addition, if you have successfully consulted the underground network, you get a +1 circumstance bonus to the next check to {@action Recall Knowledge|PC1} you attempt about the subject you were Gathering Information on, or a +2 circumstance bonus if you're using Underworld Lore for the check. The GM might change the Lore skill related to the network depending on your location or the specifics of the network you're tapping into.

feats.name: Underworld Investigator
entries: Your work as an investigator makes you familiar with the criminal element. You might be a criminal yourself, or you might have gained an understanding of how they operate from the outside. You become trained in Underworld Lore, and you gain your Pursue a Lead investigation bonus to {@skill Thievery|PC1} checks to investigate a case (such as checks to {@action Steal|PC1} a clue from a suspect or {@action Pick a Lock|PC1} to open a safe with damning documents).

feats.name: Unimpeded Step
entries: With a burst of divine liberation, your ally's movement from your {@action Liberating Step|PC2} is unaffected by {@rule Difficult Terrain|PC1|difficult terrain}, greater difficult terrain, {@rule Narrow Surfaces|PC1|narrow surfaces}, and {@rule Uneven Ground|PC1|uneven ground}. If you have the exalted reaction benefit, this applies to everyone who Steps.

feats.name: Unobstructed Shot
entries: With a quick use of brute force, you remove an obstacle and take a calculated shot as part of the same motion. Attempt to {@action Shove|PC1} or {@action Trip|PC1} one adjacent creature, then make a ranged Strike with a bow or crossbow you're wielding. The Strike is made at the same multiple attack penalty as the Shove or Trip attempt, and this activity counts as one attack when calculating your multiple attack penalty.

feats.name: Unseat
entries: With a mighty blow from atop your companion, you attempt to knock an opponent off their mount. Make a melee {@action Strike|PC1} against a mounted creature. If your attack hits, attempt an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check against the target’s Fortitude DC. If you succeed, the target is knocked off its mount into a space of its choice adjacent to its mount. If you critically succeed, the target also lands prone.
feats.requirements: You are riding your mount and wielding a {@trait Jousting|PC1} weapon.

feats.name: Unstable Concoction
entries: You can mix a wondrous yet volatile liquid into an {@trait Alchemical|PC1|alchemical} {@trait Consumable|PC1|consumable} if it has an initial effect that uses dice. You increase the size of any dice for the item's initial effect by one step. For instance, you could increase damage from a {@equipment Alchemist's Fire|PC2|moderate alchemist's fire} to 2d10 or healing from a {@equipment Elixir of Life|PC2|moderate elixir of life} to 5d8+12. Because this affects only initial dice, it wouldn't increase unarmed attack damage from a {@equipment Bestial Mutagen|PC2|bestial mutagen}, {@condition Persistent Damage|PC1|persistent damage} from an {@equipment Acid Flask|PC2|acid flask}, and the like. When this item is activated, the creature activating it must succeed at a DC 10 flat check or take acid damage equal to the item's level.

feats.name: Unstoppable Juggernaut
entries: You have become a brutal, unstoppable force of nature, able to shrug off mortal wounds with ease. You gain resistance equal to 3 + your Constitution modifier to all damage, and your resistance from raging increases to 8 + your Constitution modifier.

In addition, if you are reduced to 0 Hit Points while raging, you can end your rage as a reaction to stay at 1 Hit Point. If you do, you become {@condition Wounded|PC1|wounded 2} (or increase your wounded condition by 2 if you are already wounded).

feats.name: Vampire Lore
entries: You were raised by your vampiric parent, or you've invested substantial time and energy researching the secrets of your undead progenitors. You're trained in {@skill Religion|PC1} and {@skill Society|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in one of those skills (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
You also gain the {@feat Additional Lore|PC1} general feat for Vampire Lore.

feats.name: Vengeful Strike
entries: When struck by an enemy, you respond in turn. Make a melee Strike against the triggering creature. If the triggering attack was a critical success, you can use Vengeful Strike as a free action instead of a reaction.
feats.requirements: You’re under the effect of Come and Get Me.
feats.trigger: A creature within your reach succeeds at an attack against you.

feats.name: Vexing Tumble
entries: You tumble around your foes, expertly avoiding their reactions. Stride up to half your Speed and roll an {@skill Acrobatics|PC1} check. Compare the result to the Reflex DC of each enemy whose reach you began in or enter during the movement, in sequence.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: This movement doesn't trigger reactions from the enemy, and the enemy is {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} to you until the end of your turn

items.name: Success
entries: This movement doesn't trigger reactions from the enemy.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: Your movement immediately stops when you enter the creature's reach; if you began in the creature's reach, you don't move.

feats.name: Vicious Evisceration
entries: You make a vicious attack that maims your enemy. Make a melee Strike. If the Strike hits and deals damage, the target is {@condition Drained|PC1|drained 1}, or drained 2 on a critical success.

feats.name: Vicious Incisors
entries: Your jaws unarmed attack deals 1d6 piercing damage instead of 1d4, and gains the {@trait Backstabber|PC1|backstabber} trait. You can file down your teeth and regrow them later on, enabling you to select this feat at any level, and to retrain into and out of this feat.

feats.name: Vicious Snares
entries: You deal an additional 1d6 precision damage with damage snares you craft. This increases to 2d6 additional precision damage if you're legendary in Crafting.

feats.name: Vicious Vengeance
entries: While your vengeance is painful for both you and your foe, none can doubt that your enemies suffer more. You gain a circumstance bonus to the damage you deal from {@action Destructive Vengeance|PC2} equal to the number of damage dice from the reaction. This applies to only the damage the enemy takes, not the damage to yourself or the extra damage you gain after using the reaction.

feats.name: Vigilante Dedication
entries: You have two identities, each with its own name and abilities. Your social identity is an upstanding member of society, while your vigilante identity is a skilled and cunning warrior. Neither of these identities is a false front; you really are both of these people. If someone attempts to discern your other identity, they must use a {@action Seek|PC1} action to attempt a Perception check against your Deception DC, as if you were using the {@action Impersonate|PC1} action. Your Deception DC against such attempts is 20 + your proficiency modifier instead of the normal DC. Unlike with Impersonate, you don't have to attempt a Deception check to interact with someone to conceal your other identity—a check happens only if someone else specifically tries to uncover your other identity.

Changing from one identity to the other takes 1 minute and must be done out of sight from other creatures. As this process involves both physical changes such as clothing and makeup, along with an altered state of mind, other effects that change your appearance don't reduce the time required to change identities.

Your two identities are completely distinct. Checks to {@action Recall Knowledge|PC1} about one of your identities don't reveal information about the other unless the person attempting the check knows both identities are the same person. Effects that detect you based on your identity work only if you are currently in the identity the effect is trying to detect; otherwise, the effect fails as if the target didn't exist.

To maintain the separation between your identities, some of your abilities have the {@trait Vigilante|PC2|vigilante} trait. Your class feats and vigilante feats are associated with your vigilante identity, and using them while in your social identity may risk exposing you as a vigilante. If your identity is exposed to the public, you lose the benefits of Vigilante Dedication to disguising yourself, but you can spend 1 week of downtime to create a new social identity.

feats.name: Vigorous Health
entries: You can withstand blood loss startlingly well. Whenever you would gain the {@condition Drained|PC1|drained} condition, you can attempt a DC 17 flat check. On a success, you don't gain the drained condition.

feats.name: Viking Dedication
entries: Vikings spend long periods of time at sea, only to leap from their boats at a moment's notice, charge through the surf, and take their enemies by storm. You gain the {@feat Additional Lore|PC1} general feat for Sailing Lore and Warfare Lore.

When using your land Speed, you ignore difficult terrain from shallow water, such as in bogs or on beaches. In addition, if you roll a success on an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check to {@action Swim|PC1}, you get a critical success instead.

feats.name: Viking Weapon Familiarity
entries: From childhood, you have been exposed to traditional viking combat techniques, and you soon learned to handle axe, sword, and shield in battle. Now, you can raid proudly alongside your fellows. You gain the {@feat Shield Block|PC1} reaction. Additionally, you have familiarity with the {@equipment Battle Axe|PC1|battle axe}, {@equipment Hatchet|PC1|hatchet}, {@equipment Longsword|PC1|longsword}, {@equipment Shield Boss|PC1|shield boss}, {@equipment Shield Spikes|PC1|shield spikes}, and {@equipment Shortsword|PC1|shortsword}—for the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these weapons as simple weapons.
At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its critical specialization effect.

feats.name: Vivacious Bravado
entries: Your ego swells, granting you a temporary reprieve from your pain. You gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level plus your Charisma modifier that last until the start of your next turn.
feats.requirements: You gained panache this turn.

feats.name: Voice of the Night
entries: You hear and understand the words of creatures you share the darkness with. You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the {@skill Diplomacy|PC1} skill with bats, rats, and wolves. You also gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Make an Impression on such animals.

feats.name: Voluminous Vials
entries: Your number of versatile vials per day increases to 5.
special: At 12th level or higher, you can select this feat a second time to increase your number of versatile vials per day to 6. At 18th level or higher, you can select this feat a third time to increase your number of versatile vials per day to 7.

feats.name: Vomit Stomach
entries: In dire circumstances you can vomit out your stomach to expel toxins. Reduce your sickened condition by 2 and immediately attempt a saving throw with a +2 circumstance bonus against any ingested poisons you have been exposed to within the last minute. You become {@condition Off-guard|PC1|off-guard} for 1 round as your exposed stomach makes you especially vulnerable to attacks.
feats.trigger: You gain the {@condition Sickened|PC1|sickened} condition or fail a saving throw against an {@trait Ingested|GMC|ingested} {@trait Poison|PC1|poison}.

feats.name: Walk the Plank
entries: You frighten a foe into moving where you want them, traditionally demanding they walk the plank. Attempt to {@action Demoralize|PC1} an opponent. On a success, in addition to the normal effects, you can also force the target to {@action Stride|PC1} up to its Speed immediately. You choose the path the target takes, but you can't force it to move into an obviously harmful space (such as into hazardous terrain or a space where it would fall) unless your check was a critical success. As normal for forced movement, this movement doesn't trigger reactions. The target then becomes temporarily immune to Walk the Plank for 10 minutes.

feats.name: Wall Run
entries: You defy gravity, traversing vertical planes as easily as the ground. Stride up to your Speed. You must start your movement on a horizontal surface. During this movement, you can run up vertical surfaces, like walls, at your full Speed. If you end the Stride off the ground, you fall after taking your next action or when your turn ends, whichever comes first (though you can {@action Grab an Edge|PC1}, if applicable). If you have {@feat Water Step|PC2} or a similar ability, Wall Run lets you run along flimsy vertical surfaces, as well as vertical liquids, such as a waterfall.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: War Conditioning
entries: You have extensive training in remote environments, allowing you to move through these areas easily. When you gain this feat, you can choose to gain either a climb Speed of 20 feet or a swim Speed of 20 feet.

feats.name: Ward Against Corruption
entries: Your soul is warded against the power of undeath and plague, as well as that of the evil former psychopomps known as sahkils. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against {@trait Death|PC1|death} effects, {@trait Disease|PC1|disease}, and all effects from {@trait Undead|PC1|undead} or {@trait Sahkil|MC2|sahkils}. This bonus increases to +2 against an undead or sahkil's death effect or disease.

feats.name: Warren Digger
entries: You've learned to put your sturdy claws to work digging through the earth. You gain a burrow Speed of 15 feet.

feats.name: Warren Navigator
entries: You gain the trained proficiency rank in {@skill Survival|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in Survival (from your background or class, for example), you become trained in another skill of your choice. When you {@action Sense Direction|PC1} or attempt a roll against a {@spell Quandary|PC1|quandary} spell, you get a result one degree of success better than you rolled. You don't take a penalty to Sense Direction when you lack a {@equipment Compass|PC1|compass}.

feats.name: Wary Skulker
entries: You can perform the {@action Scout|PC1} exploration activity at the same time as the {@action Avoid Notice|PC1} exploration activity.

feats.name: Water Sprint
entries: Experience and training have taught you that water has just enough surface tension for a master sprinter to traverse the surface. When you {@action Stride|PC1} in a straight line, if you move at least half your Speed over ground, you can move any amount of the remaining distance across a level body of water. If you don't end your Stride on solid ground, you fall into the water.

If you're legendary in Athletics, as long as you start on solid ground, any part of your Stride can cross the water's surface, even if you aren't moving a straight line, though you still fall into the water if you don't end your movement on solid ground.

feats.name: Water Step
entries: You can Stride across liquid and surfaces that don't support your weight. This benefit lasts only during your movement. If you end your movement on a surface that can't support you, you fall in or it collapses as normal.

feats.name: Water Walker
entries: When in the throes of your curse, your steps take on a supernatural buoyancy. When you are {@trait Cursebound|PC2|cursebound} 1, you can {@action Stride|PC1} across liquids that don't support your weight, but you must end your movement on a surface that can support you or you fall into the liquid as normal. When you are cursebound 2 or worse, you gain the effects of {@spell Water Walk|PC1|water walk}.

feats.name: Waters of Creation
entries: Water is the source of life, and you draw upon this primordial force to heal your allies' wounds. A gentle ring ripples out from you in a 15-foot emanation, restoring 5d6 Hit Points to creatures in the area. At 12th level and every two levels thereafter, the amount restored increases by 1d6. If you are {@trait Cursebound|PC2|cursebound} 3 when you use Waters of Creation, the amount healed increases to d8s.

feats.name: Weapon Improviser Dedication
entries: You don't take the normal –2 penalty to attack rolls with {@rule Improvised Weapons|PC1|improvised weapons}. Improvised weapons you use have a minimum weapon damage die of 1d6, or 1d4 if the improvised weapon is {@trait Agile|PC1|agile}.

feats.name: Weight of Guilt
entries: Guilt clouds the minds of those who ignore your {@action Glimpse of Redemption|PC2}. Instead of making an enemy who refuses redemption {@condition Enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled 2}, you can make it stupefied 2 for the same duration.

feats.name: Well-Groomed
entries: You are fastidious about keeping clean. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against {@trait Disease|PC1|diseases}. If you roll a success on a saving throw against a disease, you get a critical success instead. If you have a different ability that would improve the save in this way (such as the battle hardened fighter class feature), if you roll a critical failure on the save you get a failure instead.

feats.name: Well-Met Traveler
entries: You naturally adopt a pleasant and affable demeanor when meeting others. You are trained in {@skill Diplomacy|PC1}. If you would automatically become trained in Diplomacy (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
In addition, you gain the {@feat Hobnobber|PC1} skill feat.

feats.name: Whirling Blade Stance
entries: You enter a mindful stance that creates a deep connection between you and your monk weapons, allowing you to manipulate them with your qi, even at a distance. All melee {@trait Monk|PC1|monk} weapons you wield with the {@trait Finesse|PC1|finesse} trait gain the {@trait Thrown|PC1|thrown 10 feet} trait (unless they already have the thrown trait with a greater range).

Once you've made a thrown Strike with such a weapon, you can use the precision of your throw to make additional strikes with it, even from a distance. Start from the space of the previous Strike's target to determine the range increment and whether the new target has cover. At the end of your turn, the thrown weapon flies directly back to you in a straight line. If a solid barrier blocks its path, it falls to the ground after hitting the barrier.

feats.name: Whirling Throw
entries: You propel your enemy away. Attempt an {@skill Athletics|PC1} check against the foe's Fortitude DC. You take a –2 circumstance penalty to your check if the target is one size larger than you and a –4 circumstance penalty if it's larger than that. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your check if the target is one size smaller than you and a +4 circumstance bonus if it's smaller than that.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: You throw the creature any distance up to 10 feet, plus 5 feet × your Strength modifier. It takes bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier plus 1d6 per 10 feet you threw it. If you threw the target at least 10 feet and into a solid obstacle, use the maximum distance you could have thrown it to calculate the damage. The creature falls {@condition Prone|PC1|prone}.

items.name: Success
entries: As critical success, but the creature doesn't fall prone.

items.name: Failure
entries: You don't throw the creature.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You don't throw the creature, and it's no longer grabbed or restrained by you.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.requirements: You have a creature {@condition Grabbed|PC1|grabbed} or {@condition Restrained|PC1|restrained}. * This archetype offers Whirling Throw at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Whirlwind Strike
entries: You lash out in a blur of motion, attacking all nearby adversaries. Make a melee Strike against each enemy within your melee reach. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but you do not increase your penalty until you have made all your attacks.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.name: Whirlwind Toss
entries: You whirl a foe to smash into all nearby creatures before throwing them far away. You {@feat Thrash|PC2}. During this Thrash, your Collateral Thrash feat applies to all other enemies adjacent to you. You can then throw the {@condition Grabbed|PC1|grabbed} creature 10 feet, where they fall {@condition Prone|PC1|prone}.
If the enemy you choose for Collateral Thrash is also adjacent to you, it attempts only one save and takes the damage only once.

feats.name: Whispers of Weakness
entries: Voices whisper to you how to best lay a creature low. You target one creature within 60 feet; if it has any weaknesses, you learn them, as well as which of its saving throw modifiers is lowest. You also come to understand its movements, gaining a +2 status bonus to your next attack roll (or skill check made as part of an attack action) against that foe before the end of your turn. The target is then temporarily immune for 1 day.

feats.name: Whodunnit?
entries: You carefully consider your case and narrow down some of the details. When you Pursue a Lead and learn there's a larger mystery, you can ask two questions related to your investigation when you open it. The GM must answer truthfully with “yes” or “no,” though if the answer would be misleading or have no practical application to your investigation, the GM can answer “immaterial.” You can't use Whodunnit? more than once for the same lead, even across different days.
Your questions must come from the following list, applying to the detail that spurred your investigation.

items: Was this clue left by a [creature trait]? (Choose a creature trait such as {@trait Humanoid|PC1|humanoid}, {@trait Undead|PC1|undead}, or {@trait Dwarf|PC1|dwarf}; this trait must be accurate as of the time the clue was left.)
Was this clue left within the last hour?
Was this clue left within the last day?
Was the creature that left this clue in a heightened emotional state when it left the clue?
Did anyone attempt to conceal this clue?

feats.name: Widen Spell
entries: You manipulate the energy of your spell, causing it to spread out and affect a wider area. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that has an area of a burst, cone, or line and does not have a duration, increase the area of that spell. Add 5 feet to the radius of a burst that normally has a radius of at least 10 feet (a burst with a smaller radius is not affected). Add 5 feet to the length of a cone or line that is normally 15 feet long or smaller, and add 10 feet to the length of a larger cone or line.

feats.name: Wild Winds Gust
entries: You build air pressure with repeated motions, before releasing an enormous crescent of rushing wind strikes. Make a wind crash Strike against each creature in your choice of a 30-foot cone or a 60 foot line. These attacks all count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after you make all the attacks.
feats.requirements: You are in Wild Winds Stance.

feats.name: Wild Winds Initiate
entries: You learn a stance that lets you attack from a distance. You gain the {@spell Wild Winds Stance|PC2|wild winds stance} qi spell. Though entering the stance is a qi spell, the wind crash Strikes the stance grants are not, so you can use them as often as you like while in the stance.

feats.name: Wind God's Fan
entries: Your fan can stir up even more powerful winds. You can use the Wave Fan activation one additional time per day. Add a 3rd-rank {@spell Wall of Wind|PC1|wall of wind} spell to the spells contained within your fan.

feats.name: Wind Jump
entries: You gather the wind beneath you, allowing you to soar as you jump. You gain the {@spell Wind Jump|PC2|wind jump} qi spell.

feats.name: Winding Flow
entries: Any journey consists of more than simply reaching your destination. You use two of the following actions in any order: Stand, Step, and Stride. You can't use the same action twice.

feats.name: Wing Buffet
entries: You have a pair of draconic wings strong enough to batter your foes away and shove them away. Choose up to two creatures adjacent to you. Attempt an Athletics check and compare it to the Fortitude DC of each target. This counts as two attacks for your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after both attacks.

items.name: Critical Success
entries: The target takes bludgeoning damage equal to double your level and is pushed up to 10 feet away from you.

items.name: Success
entries: The target takes bludgeoning damage equal to your level and is pushed up to 5 feet away from you.

items.name: Failure
entries: The target takes bludgeoning damage equal to half your level.

items.name: Critical Failure
entries: You fall {@condition Prone|PC1|prone} at the end of this activity.

feats.name: Winglet Flight
entries: Intense use and exercise have made your winglets more powerful. You {@action Fly|PC1}. If you don't normally have a fly Speed, you gain a fly Speed of 20 feet for this movement. If you aren't on solid ground at the end of this movement, you fall.

feats.name: Winglets
entries: Through the lingering influence of your warren's patron, you've sprouted a small set of wings. While not suitable for full flight, these weak wings can help you jump further with a small flap. When Leaping horizontally, you move an additional 5 feet. This additional distance isn't cumulative with the increased Leap distance from the {@feat Powerful Leap|PC1} feat. In addition, when you attempt a {@action Long Jump|PC1}, you can jump a distance up to 10 feet farther than you normally would based on the result of your {@skill Athletics|PC1} check, though you still can't jump farther than your Speed. You don't automatically fail your checks to {@action High Jump|PC1} or Long Jump if you don't Stride at least 10 feet first.

feats.name: Wolf Drag
entries: You rip your enemy off their feet. Make a wolf jaw Strike. Your wolf jaw gains the {@trait Fatal|PC1|fatal d12} trait for this Strike, and if the attack succeeds, you knock the target {@condition Prone|PC1|prone}.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.requirements: You are in Wolf Stance.  * This archetype offers Wolf Drag at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Wolf Stance
entries: You enter the stance of a wolf, low to the ground with your hands held like fangs. You can make wolf jaw unarmed attacks. These deal 1d8 piercing damage; are in the brawling group; and have the {@trait Agile|PC1|agile}, {@trait Backstabber|PC1|backstabber}, {@trait Finesse|PC1|finesse}, {@trait Nonlethal|PC1|nonlethal}, and {@trait Unarmed|PC1|unarmed} traits.
If you're flanking a target while in Wolf Stance, your wolf jaw unarmed attacks also gain the {@trait Trip|PC1|trip} trait.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.requirements: You are unarmored. * This archetype offers Wolf Stance at a different level than displayed here.

feats.name: Wounded Rage
entries: You roar in pain, awakening the rage within you. You {@action Rage|PC2}.
feats.trigger: You take damage and are capable of entering a rage.

feats.name: Wrestler Dedication
entries: Your training in the wrestling arts has made you particularly adept at moving, striking, and grappling while unencumbered. You become an expert in {@skill Athletics|PC1} and gain the {@feat Titan Wrestler|PC1} skill feat. You don’t take the –2 circumstance penalty for making a lethal attack with your nonlethal unarmed attacks. In addition, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude DC when resisting an opponent’s attempts to {@action Grapple|PC1} you or Swallow you Whole.

feats.name: You're Next
entries: After downing a foe, you menace another. Attempt to Demoralize a creature within 60 feet, with a +2 circumstance bonus. If you have legendary proficiency in Intimidation, you can use this as a free action with the same trigger.

entries.name: Archetype Use
entries: This feat can be used for one or more archetypes in addition to the listed classes. When selected this way, the feat does not have its class traits.

feats.trigger: You reduce an enemy to 0 Hit Points * This archetype offers You're Next at a different level than displayed here.
